It represents, for each foreground pixel, the distance to the nearest background pixel -- (if there is no background, it is uniformly 1.0 = everywhere is farthest) the larger the value, the "deeper" the pixel is inside the region. Note that the output type is ``image``, not ``region``. Equivalent to HALCON's ``distance_transform`` (Compute the distance transformation of a region.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_cell_counting`, `poc_crack_width`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_particle_sizing`, `poc_vessel_network`
- `em_skeleton` `region → region` GPU: none — Eckhardt–Maderlechner-style invariant thinning (the same family as HALCON `skeleton`). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `erosion_circle` (halcon: `erosion_circle`) `region → region` GPU: yes (erosion_circle) — Binary erosion with a disk-shaped structuring element (``ndimage.binary_erosion``). The most basic binary morphological operation, eroding the foreground region from its outer boundary to shrink it. Corresponds to HALCON's ``erosion_circle`` (Erode a region with a circular structuring element). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_livestock_body_volume`
- `erosion_golay` (halcon: `erosion_golay`) `region → region` GPU: yes (erosion_golay) — Binary erosion using a circular structuring element (disk, radius ``_rad(a)``=1-4). b is unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `erosion_rectangle1` (halcon: `erosion_rectangle1`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Binary erosion with a square structuring element. The only difference from ``erosion_circle`` is the shape of the structuring element (square instead of circular). Corresponds to HALCON's ``erosion_rectangle1`` (Erode a region with a rectangular structuring element). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `erosion_seq` (halcon: `erosion_seq`) `region → region` GPU: yes (erosion_seq) — Sequential erosion using a fixed cross-shaped structuring element (4-connectivity), repeated 1-4 times depending on a. b is unused. More iterations produce greater erosion (each iteration corresponds to roughly a 1-pixel radius). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `fill_holes` (halcon: `fill_up`) `region → region` GPU: yes (fill_holes) — Fills holes within a region. Equivalent to HALCON's ``fill_up`` (Fill up holes in regions.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_cell_counting`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_mesh_quality_repair`, `poc_mixed_case_depalletizing`, `poc_real_coin_metrology`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_symmetry_restoration`
- `fill_up` (halcon: `fill_up`) `region → region` GPU: yes (fill_up) — Fills holes inside a region (areas completely surrounded by background) using ``ndimage.binary_fill_holes``. Only background holes that are not connected to the outer boundary are filled; indentations connected to the outer boundary are not filled. Equivalent to HALCON's ``fill_up`` (Fill up holes in regions.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_bev_sensor_fusion`
- `fill_up_shape` (halcon: `fill_up_shape`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_fill_up_shape) — Fills small holes inside the region. Only fills holes with an area of ``area_threshold = 16+200a`` pixels or fewer (skimage's ``remove_small_holes``). b is unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `get_region_contour` (halcon: `get_region_contour`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Extracts the contour (boundary, 1 pixel wide) of the region. Subtracts a single binary erosion of the region to leave the contour. **For a region with holes it returns the hole boundaries as well, not only the outer one** (measured 2026-09-16: on an 8x8 frame with a 4x4 hole, 16 of the 20 foreground pixels adjacent to the hole come out as contour). "region minus its erosion" leaves one pixel on the outside and on the hole side alike, so fill the holes first if you want the outer boundary only. a and b are unused. Same implementation as the ``boundary`` seed op. · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_document_scan`
- `get_region_convex` (halcon: `get_region_convex`) `region → region` GPU: none — Returns the convex hull of the region as a filled region (``skimage.morphology.convex_hull_image``). a and b are unused. Same implementation as ``shape_trans`` (the seed op that converts shape to its convex hull). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `invert_region` (halcon: `complement`) `region → region` GPU: yes (invert_region) — Complement of a region (foreground/background inversion). Equivalent to HALCON's ``complement`` (Return the complement of a region.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `junctions_skeleton` (halcon: `junctions_skeleton`) `region → region` GPU: none — From a skeletonized region, keeps only pixels that have 3 or more skeleton pixels in their 3x3 neighborhood (branch points / junctions). Detects branching nodes, not skeleton endpoints (the targets that ``pruning`` removes). Corresponds to HALCON's ``junctions_skeleton`` (Find junctions and end points in a skeleton.) -- an approximation that detects only junctions, whereas HALCON also returns endpoints at the same time. · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`
- `morph_skeleton` (halcon: `morph_skeleton`) `region → region` GPU: none — Extracts the skeleton of a region. The implementation uses skimage's ``skeletonize`` (a Zhang-Suen-type iterative thinning algorithm); a and b are unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `opening_circle` (halcon: `opening_circle`) `region → region` GPU: yes (opening_circle) — Binary opening with a disk-shaped structuring element (erosion followed by dilation). Removes small protrusions and thin connections while preserving the overall shape. Corresponds to HALCON's ``opening_circle`` (Open a region with a circular structuring element). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_change_detection_misreg`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`
- `opening_golay` (halcon: `opening_golay`) `region → region` GPU: yes (opening_golay) — Binary opening using a circular structuring element (disk, radius ``_rad(a)``=1-4) (opening: erosion followed by dilation). Removes small protrusions and isolated points. b is unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `opening_rectangle1` (halcon: `opening_rectangle1`) `region → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Binary opening with a square structuring element. The rectangular version of ``opening_circle``. Equivalent to HALCON's ``opening_rectangle1`` (Open a region with a rectangular structuring element.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `pruning` (halcon: `pruning`) `region → region` GPU: none — After skeletonization (``skeletonize``, or the input as-is if unavailable), repeatedly (``1+4*a`` times) trims off endpoint pixels with a neighbor count of 1 or fewer (spurs = stray branches), removing short branches from the skeleton. Corresponds to HALCON's ``pruning`` (Prune the branches of a region.) (HALCON can specify branch length, but this is an approximation using an iteration count). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`
- `r2_endpoints_skeleton` `region → region` GPU: none — Extract the end points of a skeleton (the points with exactly one skeleton pixel in their 8-neighbourhood). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`
- `r2_inner_circle` (halcon: `inner_circle`) `region → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Largest inscribed circle drawn as a mask (a scales drawn radius; a=0.5=exact). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_inner_rectangle1` (halcon: `inner_rectangle1`) `region → region` GPU: none — Largest axis-aligned inscribed rectangle (a shrinks the drawn rect; a=0=exact). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_partition_rectangle` (halcon: `partition_rectangle`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Split the region bbox into an NxN grid; keep cells overlapping the region. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_runlength_features` (halcon: `runlength_features`) `region → feature` GPU: none — Region -> feature: mean length of horizontal foreground runs. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_smallest_circle` (halcon: `smallest_circle`) `region → region` GPU: none — Minimum enclosing circle as a mask (Welzl); a inflates radius (>=0). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_smallest_rectangle1` `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Axis-aligned bounding box (smallest_rectangle1). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_smallest_rectangle2` (halcon: `smallest_rectangle2`) `region → region` GPU: none — Minimum-area ORIENTED bounding rectangle as a mask (rotating calipers). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_sort_region` (halcon: `sort_region`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_sort_region) — Keep the k-th largest connected component; k = round(a*(n-1)). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r2_split_skeleton_lines` (halcon: `split_skeleton_lines`) `region → region` GPU: none — Thin the region to a skeleton, then break it at junctions (>=3 neighbours). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_vessel_network`
- `r2_union1` (halcon: `union1`) `region → region` GPU: yes (r2_union1) — Union of all connected components into a single mask (OR of labels). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_background_seg` (halcon: `background_seg`) `region → region` GPU: yes (lbl_background_seg) — Splits the region's background (the complement of the foreground) into connected components, discards components that are too small, and returns the rest (equivalent to HALCON ``background_seg``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_clip_region` (halcon: `clip_region`) `region → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Clips the region with a rectangular window centred on the image (equivalent to HALCON ``clip_region``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_eliminate_runs` (halcon: `eliminate_runs`) `region → region` GPU: none — Removes horizontal connected runs (sequences of consecutive foreground pixels) shorter than a specified length (equivalent to HALCON ``eliminate_runs``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_label_to_region` (halcon: `label_to_region`) `region → region` GPU: none — Extracts only the pixels with one specific gray value (label) from a label image (equivalent to HALCON ``label_to_region``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_partition_dynamic` (halcon: `partition_dynamic`) `region → region` GPU: none — Splits the region horizontally at columns where the vertical extent narrows (a 'neck') (equivalent to HALCON ``partition_dynamic``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_polar_trans_region` (halcon: `polar_trans_region`) `region → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Remaps the region to polar coordinates centred on its centroid (equivalent to HALCON ``polar_trans_region``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_rank_region` (halcon: `rank_region`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Morphological rank operator on a region (HALCON's genuine ``rank_region``: a generalisation that is neither pure erosion nor pure dilation). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_region_features` (halcon: `region_features`) `region → feature` GPU: none — Returns one shape feature of the region (implements part of HALCON ``region_features``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_runlength_distribution` (halcon: `runlength_distribution`) `region → feature` GPU: none — Returns one summary statistic of the horizontal run-length distribution (equivalent to HALCON ``runlength_distribution``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `r3_select_region_point` (halcon: `select_region_point`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_select_region_point) — Keeps only the connected component that contains a specified point (equivalent to HALCON ``select_region_point``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `reg_close` (halcon: `closing_circle`) `region → region` GPU: none — Binary closing of a region (dilation followed by erosion). Equivalent to HALCON's ``closing_circle`` (Close a region with a circular structuring element.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`
- `reg_dilate` (halcon: `dilation_circle`) `region → region` GPU: yes (reg_dilate) — Binary dilation of a region. Equivalent to HALCON's ``dilation_circle`` (Dilate a region with a circular structuring element.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `reg_erode` (halcon: `erosion_circle`) `region → region` GPU: yes (reg_erode) — Binary erosion of a region. Equivalent to HALCON's ``erosion_circle`` (Erode a region with a circular structuring element.). · examples: `degenerate_inputs`, `gallery2d_region`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`
- `reg_open` (halcon: `opening_circle`) `region → region` GPU: none — Binary opening of a region (erosion followed by dilation). Equivalent to HALCON's ``opening_circle`` (Open a region with a circular structuring element.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `region_boundary` (halcon: `boundary`) `region → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Extracts the contour (boundary ring) of a region. Equivalent to HALCON's ``boundary`` (Reduce a region to its boundary.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `remove_noise_region` (halcon: `remove_noise_region`) `region → region` GPU: yes (remove_noise_region) — Removes isolated small speck noise using binary opening (erosion followed by dilation) with a circular structuring element (radius ``_rad(a)``=1 to 4). b is unused. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_region`
- `remove_small` (halcon: `select_shape`) `region → region` GPU: yes (lbl_remove_small) — Removes small connected regions based on area. Equivalent to HALCON's ``select_shape`` (Choose regions with the aid of shape features.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `quickstart`
- `select_largest` (halcon: `select_shape_std`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_select_largest) — Keeps only the connected region with the largest area. Equivalent to HALCON's ``select_shape_std`` (Select regions of a given shape.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `mcp_task_score`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`
- `select_shape` (halcon: `select_shape`) `region → region` GPU: yes (lbl_select_shape) — Removes connected components (foreground is 8-connected) whose area is below a threshold (``16+a*200`` pixels) -- i.e., removes small noise-like regions. HALCON's ``select_shape`` (Choose regions with the aid of shape features.) is a general-purpose operator that can filter by any shape feature such as area, circularity, or convexity, but here it is fixed to a single area-based cutoff (an approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_ai_built_inspection_scored`
- `select_shape_std` (halcon: `select_shape_std`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_select_shape_std) — Keeps only the connected component with the largest area (selected via ``_largest_label``; foreground is 8-connected). HALCON's ``select_shape_std`` (Select regions of a given shape.) is an operator that lets you choose among several standard criteria including ``max_area``, but here it is fixed to the single criterion "largest area" (an approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `shape_trans` (halcon: `shape_trans`) `region → region` GPU: none — Returns the convex hull of a region (``skimage.morphology.convex_hull_image``). HALCON's ``shape_trans`` (Transform the shape of a region.) is originally an operator that lets you choose among several transform modes -- convex, rectangle1, ellipse, etc. -- via the ``Type`` argument, but this stand-in is fixed to the single convex-hull mode (a limitation of the approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `sk_clear_border` `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_clear_border) — Removal of components touching the image border. Drops all connected components of the foreground region that touch the image's outer edge back to background -- a standard preprocessing step for excluding objects cut off at the edge of the field of view (not fully captured) from analysis. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `sk_convex` (halcon: `shape_trans`) `region → region` GPU: none — Region transformation by convex hull. Finds the smallest convex polygon enclosing the foreground region and returns the filled interior as a region -- filling in all constrictions and concavities. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `sk_find_boundaries` (halcon: `boundary`) `region → region` GPU: none — Region boundary extraction. In a label image (here, a boolean region), returns a boundary mask that is True only at pixels where two different labels (foreground/background) meet. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `sk_medial` (halcon: `skeleton`) `region → region` GPU: none — Medial axis transform. A different algorithm from sk_skeleton that finds the skeleton by extracting the ridge lines of the distance transform, tending to produce a skeleton that retains distance-from-contour information. · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_crack_width`, `poc_vessel_network`
- `sk_remove_holes` (halcon: `fill_up`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_sk_remove_holes) — Small hole filling. Fills only the background holes inside the foreground region whose area is below a threshold -- larger holes (intentional openings) are left as is. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `sk_skeleton` (halcon: `skeleton`) `region → region` GPU: none — Region skeletonization. Thins the foreground region down to lines one pixel wide while preserving its topology (connectivity and number of holes). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`
- `sk_thin` (halcon: `thinning`) `region → region` GPU: none — Morphological thinning. Similar to sk_skeleton in reducing to one-pixel width, but uses a different algorithm based on the hit-or-miss transform, and tends to produce fewer skeleton branches (spurs). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `skeleton` (halcon: `skeleton`) `region → region` GPU: none — Thins a region to a 1-pixel-wide skeleton while preserving topology (``skimage.morphology.skeletonize``). Branch points and endpoints are preserved in position, so it is often used to analyze branching shapes (such as counting the number of fingers). Equivalent to HALCON's ``skeleton`` (Compute the skeleton of a region.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_crack_width`, `poc_em_branch_territory`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_swc_tree_truth`, `poc_vessel_network`
- `smallest_rectangle1` (halcon: `smallest_rectangle1`) `region → region` GPU: inside a chain only (lbl_smallest_rectangle1) — Returns a region filled with the axis-aligned bounding box enclosing the region. a and b are unused. Returns all zeros if the region is empty. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `thinning` (halcon: `thinning`) `region → region` GPU: none — Reduces a region to 1-pixel width using ``skimage.morphology.thin`` (a Zhang-Suen-family thinning algorithm). Its purpose is similar to ``skeleton``, but the internal algorithm differs, so results can differ slightly near branch points and similar areas. A stand-in for HALCON's ``thinning`` (Remove the result of a hit-or-miss operation from a region.). · examples: `gallery2d_region`, `poc_crack_width`, `poc_fabric_defect`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_real_grain_skiz`, `poc_vessel_network`
- `thinning_golay` (halcon: `thinning_golay`) `region → region` GPU: none — Thins a region. The implementation uses skimage's ``thin`` (Guo-Hall-type iterative thinning), repeated until the region is completely 1 pixel wide; a and b are unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `thinning_seq` (halcon: `thinning_seq`) `region → region` GPU: none — Thins a region. The implementation is identical to thinning_golay (skimage's ``thin``, Guo-Hall-type thinning iterated to convergence); a and b are unused. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `xcv2_hitmiss` `region → region` GPU: none — Detects the cross pattern 'center is background, up/down/left/right are foreground' using the hit-or-miss transform (``cv2.MORPH_HITMISS``). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `xsk2_isotropic_close` `region → region` GPU: none — Isotropic closing. Applies ``skimage.morphology.isotropic_closing`` to a binary region (dedicated to `region` -> `region`; unlike ordinary morphological closing, it works isotropically based on a distance transform). · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `xsk3_rank_majority` `region → region` GPU: none — Local majority-vote filter (skimage ``filters.rank.majority``). The skimage version of the same majority-vote smoothing as xmh_majority: sets a pixel to 1 if more than half of the pixels in the disk neighborhood are 1. · examples: `gallery2d_region`
- `xsp_chamfer_dist` `region → image` GPU: none — City-block (chamfer) distance to the nearest background pixel, normalised to [0,1]. · examples: `gallery2d_region`

#### 2d / region-morphology (1)
- `xmh_majority` `region → region` GPU: none — Majority filter (``mahotas.majority_filter``). For a binary region, a smoothing operation that keeps a pixel as 1 only where 1s form a majority within a square neighborhood. Used to remove isolated noise and smooth jagged region boundaries. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_region`

#### 2d / region-transform (1)
- `xmh_bwperim` `region → region` GPU: none — Region contour extraction (``mahotas.bwperim``). From a binary region, produces a 1-pixel-wide contour keeping only the boundary pixels that touch the background. · examples: `gallery2d_region`

#### 2d / restoration (12)
- `iv_backproject_superres` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Single-image iterative back-projection super-resolution (Irani-Peleg). Upscale to a higher grid, simulate the low-res observation by blurring and downscaling, back-project the residual into the high grid, then downscale the consistent estimate back to HxW. Net effect: high-frequency detail is boosted (sharpening-by-consistency). ``a`` sets iterations n = 1 + round(a*4) (1..5); ``b`` sets the back-projection step gain g = 0.5 + b (0.5..1.5). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `iv_gradient_inpaint` `image → image` GPU: none — Harmonic (Laplace) inpainting of a central masked window. The interior of a centred window (side fraction from ``a``) is discarded and refilled by solving nabla^2 u = 0 with Dirichlet boundary equal to the surrounding known pixels (Jacobi relaxation = repeatedly replacing each masked pixel by its 4-neighbour mean). The recovered interior is the smoothest (minimum-gradient) fill of the hole. ``a`` sets the window size; ``b`` is ignored. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `iv_motion_deblur` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Wiener deconvolution of an assumed LINEAR MOTION blur. ``a`` sets the blur length L = 3 + round(a*10) (3..13 px); ``b`` sets the blur angle theta = b*180 deg (b=0 -> horizontal). The op builds that motion PSF and inverts it, narrowing a bar that was smeared along the motion direction. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_real_deblur_honesty`
- `iv_richardson_lucy` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Richardson-Lucy deconvolution assuming a small Gaussian PSF (sigma = ``RL_SIGMA``). ``a`` sets the iteration count n = 1 + round(a*14) (1..15); ``b`` is ignored. RL multiplicatively drives the estimate ``u`` so that ``u (*) psf`` matches the blurred measurement, sharpening real edges. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_real_deblur_honesty`
- `iv_unsharp_deblur` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Iterative unsharp masking as an approximate deblur. Each pass adds a scaled high-pass (image minus its Gaussian blur) back to the image. ``a`` sets the iteration count n = 1 + round(a*5) (1..6); ``b`` sets the per-pass amount amt = 0.4 + b (0.4..1.4). More iterations / larger amount -> sharper. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_real_deblur_honesty`
- `iv_wiener_deconv_spatial` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Self-contained spatial Wiener deconvolution of an assumed small Gaussian PSF. ``a`` sets the assumed blur sigma in [0.4, ``WIENER_SIGMA_MAX``] to invert (larger a -> stronger sharpening); ``b`` sets the noise-to-signal ratio nsr = 1e-3 + b*0.15 (larger b -> gentler, more regularized restoration). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xcv3_inpaint_ns` `image → image` GPU: none — Inpainting by the Navier-Stokes method (OpenCV ``cv2.inpaint``, ``INPAINT_NS``). A restoration algorithm that fills in missing regions by propagating information from surrounding pixels using fluid-dynamics principles. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xcv_inpaint` `image → image` GPU: none — Inpainting that estimates and fills in missing regions. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsk2_wiener` `image → image` GPU: none — Wiener deconvolution (deblurring using a known point spread function). Calls ``skimage.restoration.wiener``. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsk_inpaint` `image → image` GPU: none — Restoration (inpainting) that estimates and fills missing regions. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsk_richardson_lucy` `image → image` GPU: none — Richardson-Lucy deconvolution. Iteratively sharpens the image assuming the blur is a 3x3 mean kernel (box PSF) (calls ``skimage.restoration.richardson_lucy`` directly). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsk_unwrap_phase` `image → image` GPU: none — Phase unwrapping. Treats the input [0,1] as phase [-pi, pi], removes 2*pi wraps using ``skimage.restoration.unwrap_phase``, then converts back to [0,1] via ``signed01`` while preserving sign (0 -> 0.5). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`

#### 2d / segment (7)
- `sg_felzenszwalb` `image → region` GPU: none — Returns the boundaries of Felzenszwalb's graph-based region segmentation (``skimage.segmentation.felzenszwalb``; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sg_gmm_segment` `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Fits a 2-class Gaussian mixture model (EM algorithm) to the intensity values and returns the brighter cluster as the region (a self-contained EM implementation independent of ``skimage``; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`
- `sg_kmeans_intensity` `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Applies k-means clustering to the intensity values and returns the brightest cluster as the region (a self-contained Lloyd's-algorithm implementation; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sg_normalized_cut_2` `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Splits the image into two regions (bright / dark) using normalized cut on the intensity graph (spectral 2-way partitioning, Shi & Malik; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sg_region_growing_seeded` `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Seeded region growing that starts from the image centre and connects pixels with similar intensity (HALCON ``regiongrowing`` is already covered by another op, so ``halcon=""`` is used here to avoid double-reporting it). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sg_slic_superpixels` `image → region` GPU: none — Returns the boundary grid of a SLIC superpixel over-segmentation (``skimage.segmentation.slic``; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sg_watershed_gradient` `image → region` GPU: none — Returns the boundaries of a watershed segmentation seeded from h-minima markers on the gradient image (``skimage``; no corresponding HALCON operator). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`

#### 2d / segmentation (56)
- `adaptive_gauss_thresh` (halcon: `local_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (adaptive_gauss_thresh) — Adaptive thresholding based on a locally Gaussian-smoothed mean. Equivalent to HALCON's ``local_threshold`` (Segment an image using local thresholding.). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_matrix_code_reading`
- `auto_threshold` (halcon: `auto_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — The implementation is identical to ``binary_threshold`` (automatic thresholding via Otsu's discriminant analysis method). HALCON's ``auto_threshold`` (Segment an image using thresholds determined from its histogram) is originally an operator that determines **multiple thresholds** (multi-class segmentation) from multiple valleys in the histogram, but this substitute is simplified to binarization with a single Otsu threshold (a limitation of the approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_battery_electrode_breathing`, `poc_bump_coplanarity`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `bin_threshold` (halcon: `bin_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Automatic threshold binarization using Otsu's method. Shares the ``otsu`` branch of ``_sh_threshold`` with ``binary_threshold``/``auto_threshold``; a and b are unused. Pixels brighter than the threshold become the foreground (1). Without scikit-image the same 256-bin Otsu is computed by the numpy twin (``numpy_twins.threshold_otsu``), bit-identical (until 2026-10-25 it silently fell back to a different answer: the image mean as the threshold). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_metal_grain_size`
- `binary_threshold` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Automatic threshold binarization using Otsu's method (``skimage.filters.threshold_otsu``, falling back to the mean value if unavailable). Automatically determines the threshold that maximizes between-class variance from the image histogram. Corresponds to HALCON's ``binary_threshold`` (Segment an image using binary thresholding) -- HALCON allows selecting among several algorithms besides Otsu, but here Otsu is fixed. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `canny` (halcon: `edges_image`) `image → region` GPU: yes (canny) — Simplified Canny-style edge detection (returns a region). Mapped to HALCON's ``edges_image`` (Extract edges using Deriche, Lanser, Shen, or Canny filters.), but this is a simplified version (an approximation) that does not perform non-maximum suppression or hysteresis thresholding. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_real_coin_metrology`, `poc_water_inspection_images`
- `cv_adaptive_gauss` (halcon: `local_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Thresholding based on a locally Gaussian-weighted average (adaptive threshold, Gaussian variant, OpenCV implementation). Same framework as cv_adaptive_mean, but since the local average is taken as a Gaussian-weighted average rather than a simple average, abrupt changes near the window boundary are less likely to appear. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `cv_adaptive_mean` (halcon: `dyn_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Thresholding based on the local mean (adaptive threshold, mean variant, OpenCV implementation). Uses, as the threshold, the simple average of each pixel's neighborhood minus a constant - more stable than a global threshold on images with uneven illumination. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `cv_canny` (halcon: `edges_image`) `image → region` GPU: none — Canny edge detection (region variant, OpenCV implementation). Same algorithm as sk_canny, but the OpenCV version's API takes two thresholds directly rather than the sigma of Gaussian smoothing. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `cv_otsu` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Global thresholding using Otsu's discriminant analysis method (OpenCV implementation). Same algorithm as sk_otsu, but it differs in that it quantizes internally to 8 bits before computing (results may shift slightly). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_vegetation_cover`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `dual_threshold` (halcon: `dual_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — A thresholding operation for signed images. Treats the median value 0.5 as "zero" and takes pixels satisfying ``|x - 0.5| > 0.1+0.35*a`` (pixels sufficiently far from 0.5) as foreground — responding symmetrically to both the positive and negative side. Corresponds to HALCON's ``dual_threshold`` (Threshold operator for signed images.) (HALCON can have separate thresholds for positive and negative, but this is simplified to a symmetric band centered on 0.5). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `dyn_threshold` (halcon: `dyn_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (dyn_threshold) — Local thresholding. Uses the local mean (``uniform_filter`` with window side ``_k(a)``) plus an offset ``(b-0.5)*0.4`` as the threshold -- this allows extracting foreground based on local contrast even in images with uneven illumination. Corresponds to HALCON's ``dyn_threshold`` (Segment an image using a local threshold). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_metal_grain_size`
- `edges_image` (halcon: `edges_image`) `image → region` GPU: none — Region extraction via Canny edge detection (``skimage.feature.canny``, sigma ``0.5+2*a``). A widely used edge detection method that combines multiple stages: Gaussian smoothing -> gradient -> non-maximum suppression -> hysteresis thresholding. Corresponds to HALCON's ``edges_image`` (Detect edges using Deriche, Lanser, Shen, or Canny filters) -- HALCON allows choosing among Deriche/Lanser/Shen/Canny, but here Canny is fixed. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `fast_threshold` (halcon: `fast_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Binarization with a fixed threshold. Pixels where ``x`` falls within the band ``(a, a+0.5+0.5b)`` become the foreground (1) (sharing the ``fixed`` branch of ``_sh_threshold`` with the ``threshold`` seed op). a sets the lower bound, and b sets the band width (upper bound). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `h_threshold` (halcon: `threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Band thresholding (pixels satisfying ``a < x < a+0.5+0.5*b`` are treated as foreground). HALCON's ``threshold`` (Segment an image using global threshold) is an operator that directly specifies Min/Max values, but this substitute is a simplification roughly equivalent to a single parameter, deriving the lower bound from ``a`` and the band width from ``b``. The registered name becomes ``h_threshold`` because ``threshold`` is treated as a reserved-word-like name on the Python side (the spec's ``halcon`` field remains ``threshold``). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `hysteresis_threshold` (halcon: `hysteresis_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Hysteresis thresholding (``skimage.filters.apply_hysteresis_threshold``). Among pixels exceeding a low threshold (``0.2+0.3*a``), only those connected to pixels exceeding a high threshold (``0.5+0.3*b``) are kept as foreground -- an edge-extraction technique resistant to gaps, also used as post-processing for Canny edge detection. Corresponds to HALCON's ``hysteresis_threshold`` (Perform a hysteresis threshold operation on an image). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`
- `it_region_to_bin` (halcon: `region_to_bin`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — region_to_bin: threshold the image at ``a`` to obtain a region, then render that region as a two-gray-level binary image -- foreground pixels get the high gray value, background pixels the low one. ``b`` sets the two levels: lo = 0.5 - 0.5*b, hi = 0.5 + 0.5*b. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `local_max` (halcon: `local_max`) `image → region` GPU: yes (local_max) — Local maxima detection. Only pixels where ``x`` matches the maximum value within the window (``_k(a)``) and also satisfy ``x > 0.3+0.4*b`` are treated as foreground -- note that in flat, plateau-like regions, multiple adjacent pixels can simultaneously remain as "maxima" (there is no guarantee that only true isolated peak points remain). Corresponds to HALCON's ``local_max`` (Detect all local maxima in an image). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `local_min` (halcon: `local_min`) `image → region` GPU: none — Detects local minima (regional minima). Takes as foreground pixels where ``x`` matches the minimum value within the window (``_k(a)``) and also satisfies ``x < 0.7-0.4*b`` — the dark-side counterpart of ``local_max``. Corresponds to HALCON's ``local_min`` (Detect all local minima in an image.). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `local_threshold` (halcon: `local_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (local_threshold) — Thresholding via local Gaussian smoothing plus an offset (the threshold is ``gaussian_filter(x, 1+3*a)`` plus offset ``(b-0.5)*0.3``). A similar idea to ``dyn_threshold``, but differs in that the local mean is computed with a Gaussian instead of a rectangular window. Corresponds to HALCON's ``local_threshold`` (Segment an image using local thresholding). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `nonmax_suppression_amp` (halcon: `nonmax_suppression_amp`) `image → region` GPU: yes (nonmax_suppression_amp) — Non-maximum suppression that extracts local maxima. Only pixels that match the maximum value in their window and exceed the threshold ``0.3+0.4b`` are kept as foreground. a sets the window size to 3/5/7/9. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `otsu` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (otsu) — Automatic thresholding using Otsu's method. Equivalent to HALCON's ``binary_threshold`` (Segment an image using binary thresholding.). · examples: `ct_inspection`, `degenerate_inputs`, `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_segmentation`, `genspark_external_review`, `line_handshake`, `mcp_task_score`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_matrix_code_reading`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_real_coin_metrology`, `poc_real_file_formats`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`, `poc_vegetation_cover`, `poc_water_inspection_images`, `quickstart`, `segment_and_classify`, `threshold_family_agreement`, `typed_results_json`
- `pouring` (halcon: `pouring`) `image → region` GPU: none — Boundary extraction via watershed segmentation. Treats a gradient image (Sobel amplitude) as terrain, computes the watershed using dark regions (``x < 0.2+0.3a``) as seeds (markers), and returns the boundaries as foreground using ``skimage.segmentation.find_boundaries``. b is unused. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `ptile_threshold` `image → feature` GPU: none — Returns a P-tile threshold chosen by area fraction as a feature. · examples: `poc_threshold_transfer_after_normalization`
- `regiongrowing` (halcon: `regiongrowing`) `image → region` GPU: none — A simplified approximation of region growing. First creates seed regions using a high threshold (``x > 0.5+0.3*a``), then expands them by binary dilation ``1+4*b`` times -- this is a lightweight substitute using threshold + dilation rather than true region growing (which expands by sequentially judging similarity with neighboring pixels) (a limitation of the approximation). A stand-in for HALCON's ``regiongrowing`` (Segment an image using region growing). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `regiongrowing_mean` (halcon: `regiongrowing_mean`) `image → region` GPU: none — The implementation is identical to ``regiongrowing`` (threshold-based seed generation + dilation). HALCON's ``regiongrowing_mean`` (Perform a region growing using mean gray values.) is originally an operator that grows regions based on closeness to each region's mean intensity, but this stand-in performs no judgment based on mean intensity and returns the same processing as ``regiongrowing`` (a limitation of the approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `segment_image_mser` (halcon: `segment_image_mser`) `image → region` GPU: none — MSER (Maximally Stable Extremal Regions) detection (``cv2.MSER_create``). Detects regions whose shape remains stable even as the threshold is continuously varied, and returns their boundaries (used for detecting regions such as text and logos robustly against illumination changes). Corresponds to HALCON's ``segment_image_mser`` (Segment image using Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER).). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sigma_threshold` `image → region` GPU: none — Robustly standardises an image and binarises it at ``k = 2 + 3*a`` sigma. · examples: `poc_threshold_transfer_after_normalization`
- `sk_canny` (halcon: `edges_image`) `image → region` GPU: none — Canny edge detection (region version). Finds edge pixels through the classic multi-stage pipeline -- Gaussian smoothing -> gradient computation -> non-maximum suppression -> hysteresis thresholding -- and returns them as a boolean region. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_segmentation`, `genspark_external_review`
- `sk_chan_vese` `image → region` GPU: none — Chan-Vese segmentation. An active contour model that iteratively moves a level set so that the brightness variance within each region is minimized, allowing detection of regions even for objects without sharp edges. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_active_contours`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `sk_felzenszwalb` `image → region` GPU: none — Felzenszwalb's graph-based segmentation. A fast method that clusters using a minimum spanning tree with pixels as nodes, over-segmenting the image even without clear boundaries. Here it returns the boundaries of the segmentation result as a region. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `sk_hysteresis` (halcon: `hysteresis_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Hysteresis thresholding. Uses two threshold levels: pixels above the higher one are confirmed first, then pixels above the lower one that are connected to a confirmed pixel are also adopted -- the same idea as Canny's edge-linking step, applied to general response images. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sk_li` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Global thresholding by Li's minimum cross entropy method. Determines the threshold by iteratively minimizing the cross entropy between the foreground/background distributions -- an automatic thresholding method in a different lineage from Otsu's method. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `sk_local_maxima` (halcon: `local_max`) `image → region` GPU: none — Local maxima detection. Returns, as a region, the set of pixels that are strictly greater than every neighboring pixel (plateaus -- connected regions of equal value -- are also allowed) -- a preprocessing step for peak detection and feature-point extraction. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `sk_niblack` (halcon: `var_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Niblack's local adaptive thresholding. Like Sauvola, it determines the threshold from the local mean and standard deviation, but with a simpler (classic) way of setting the coefficients, and tends to judge the foreground more broadly than Sauvola (i.e. more prone to picking up noise). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `sk_otsu` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Global thresholding by Otsu's method (discriminant analysis). Automatically selects the threshold that maximizes between-class variance, splitting the whole image into foreground/background. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_cell_counting`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_vegetation_cover`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `sk_sauvola` (halcon: `var_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Sauvola's local adaptive thresholding. Determines the threshold locally from the local mean and standard deviation around each pixel -- designed for binarizing (text extraction from) document images with uneven illumination. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_matrix_code_reading`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `sk_slic` `image → region` GPU: none — Superpixel segmentation by SLIC (Simple Linear Iterative Clustering). Performs k-means clustering in a combined color (here, gray value) and coordinate space, dividing the image into regions of roughly equal size. Here it returns the boundaries of the segmentation result as a region. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `sk_yen` (halcon: `binary_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Global thresholding by Yen's maximum correlation criterion. Chooses the threshold by maximizing an entropy-based measure of the histogram -- yet another automatic thresholding method distinct from Otsu's and Li's methods. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `threshold` (halcon: `threshold`) `image → region` GPU: yes (threshold) — Global thresholding. Equivalent to HALCON's ``threshold`` (Segment an image using global threshold.). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_ai_built_inspection_scored`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_change_detection_misreg`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_real_bg_kalman_tracking`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_real_walnut_cbct`, `poc_screw_thread_metrology`, `poc_tof_camera`, `poc_traffic_counting`, `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`, `poc_water_level`, `tof_realdata`, `video_streaming`
- `var_threshold` (halcon: `var_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — Sauvola's local adaptive binarization (``skimage.filters.threshold_sauvola``, window size ``2*int(a*6)+3``). Since the threshold is determined using both the local mean and local standard deviation, it is more robust to uneven illumination and low-contrast documents than ``dyn_threshold``. An approximation corresponding to HALCON's ``var_threshold`` (Threshold an image by local mean and standard deviation analysis) -- the formulation follows a similar idea, but Sauvola's formula and HALCON's formula have different coefficients, so the numerical results are not identical. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_document_scan`
- `watersheds` (halcon: `watersheds`) `image → region` GPU: none — Watershed segmentation. Treats the gradient image as terrain, uses dark regions (``x < 0.2+0.3*a``) as markers to find the watershed lines, and returns those boundary lines. Corresponds to HALCON's ``watersheds`` (Extract watersheds and basins from an image). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `watersheds_threshold` (halcon: `watersheds_threshold`) `image → region` GPU: none — The implementation is identical to ``watersheds`` (``kind: "watershed"``). HALCON's ``watersheds_threshold`` (Extract watershed basins from an image using a threshold) is originally an operator with a depth threshold that merges adjacent catchment basins, but this substitute does not implement the merge threshold and returns the same result as ``watersheds`` (a limitation of the approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xcv2_meanshift` `image → image` GPU: none — Smooths color/brightness region by region using mean-shift filtering (``cv2.pyrMeanShiftFiltering``). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xcv_grabcut` `image → region` GPU: none — Automatic foreground/background separation via GrabCut (iterative graph cut). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xcv_watershed_markers` (halcon: `watersheds`) `image → region` GPU: none — Boundary extraction via marker-controlled watershed. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xkor_canny` `image → region` GPU: none — Edge (binary region) detection by the Canny method. Calls ``kornia.filters.canny`` and adopts the binary edge map (``edges``) among its return values (the gradient-magnitude side is discarded). · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xmh_bernsen` `image → region` GPU: none — Bernsen local thresholding (``mahotas.thresholding.bernsen``). Uses the midpoint between the local maximum and minimum brightness as the local threshold, falling back to a global threshold only in low-contrast regions. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `xsk2_h_maxima` `image → region` GPU: none — h-maxima transform (removes local maxima with a height less than h). Calls ``skimage.morphology.h_maxima``. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_cell_counting`
- `xsk2_multiotsu` `image → image` GPU: none — Quantizes tonal levels using multi-level Otsu's method, an extension of Otsu's discriminant analysis method to multiple thresholds. Uses ``skimage.filters.threshold_multiotsu``. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `poc_mri_bias_field`
- `xsk3_h_minima` `image → region` GPU: none — h-minima transform (skimage ``morphology.h_minima``). Flattens shallow valleys (local minima) with depth less than ``h``, then binary-marks the remaining minima - a valley-picking process similar to xmh_regmin, but one that can explicitly exclude shallow, noise-derived valleys by depth. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `genspark_external_review`
- `xsk3_peak_local_max` `image → region` GPU: none — Local maxima map (skimage ``feature.peak_local_max``). Detects the coordinates of local brightness maxima that are at least ``min_distance`` pixels apart from each other, and returns a sparse binary image where only those coordinates are set to 1 (single-pixel points, not regions as areas). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xsk3_rank_otsu` `image → region` GPU: none — Local Otsu binarization (skimage ``filters.rank.otsu``). Computes an Otsu's-method (discriminant analysis) threshold within a local disk neighborhood only, and binarizes by whether the pixel value exceeds that local threshold - unlike global Otsu, this can select a locally appropriate threshold even on images with uneven illumination. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `threshold_family_agreement`
- `xsk3_threshold_local_median` `image → region` GPU: none — Local median adaptive binarization (skimage ``filters.threshold_local`` with ``method='median'``). Uses the median of each block as the local threshold and binarizes by whether the pixel value exceeds it. More robust to outliers (noise pixels) than the version using local mean. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xsk_flood` `image → region` GPU: none — Region extraction by flood fill. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`
- `xsk_random_walker` `image → region` GPU: none — Graph-based region segmentation using the random walker method. · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`, `genspark_external_review`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `zero_crossing` (halcon: `zero_crossing`) `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Detects pixels where the sign of the Laplacian (with built-in Gaussian smoothing, sigma ``0.5+2*a``) flips (zero crossings). LoG zero crossings are a classic detection method known for locating edges with high precision. Corresponds to HALCON's ``zero_crossing`` (Extract zero crossings from an image.). · examples: `gallery2d_segmentation`

#### 2d / self-similarity (1)
- `xmh_selfmatch` `image → image` GPU: none — Self-similarity map (self-template matching using ``mahotas.template_match``). Template-matches a small patch cut from the center of the image against the whole image, and normalizes the result so that locations more similar to the patch approach 1. · examples: `gallery2d_features`

#### 2d / smoothing (50)
- `anisotropic_diffusion` (halcon: `anisotropic_diffusion`) `image → image` GPU: yes (anisotropic_diffusion) — Perona-Malik type anisotropic diffusion. Pixel differences in the four directions (up/down/left/right) are multiplied by a Gaussian-type conductance function ``exp(-(delta/K)^2)`` and added iteratively -- this is edge-preserving smoothing that does not diffuse in directions where the difference exceeds threshold K (= an edge), and smooths only in directions where the difference is small (= flat). Corresponds to HALCON's ``anisotropic_diffusion`` (Perform an anisotropic diffusion of an image). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `bilateral` (halcon: `bilateral_filter`) `image → image` GPU: yes (bilateral) — Edge-preserving smoothing (bilateral filter). Equivalent to HALCON's ``bilateral_filter`` (bilateral filtering of an image.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `quickstart`
- `bilateral_filter` (halcon: `bilateral_filter`) `image → image` GPU: none — OpenCV's bilateral filter (``cv2.bilateralFilter``). A standard method that averages neighboring pixels weighted by both spatial distance and intensity difference, smoothing while preserving edges. Corresponds to HALCON's ``bilateral_filter`` (bilateral filtering of an image). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `binomial_filter` (halcon: `binomial_filter`) `image → image` GPU: yes (binomial_filter) — A separable smoothing filter weighted by binomial coefficients (Pascal's triangle). It approximates a Gaussian with a discrete binomial kernel by applying ``ndimage.correlate1d`` successively along rows and columns -- an implementation based on the same idea as the kernel used by HALCON's ``binomial_filter`` (Smooth an image using the binomial filter.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `coherence_enhancing_diff` (halcon: `coherence_enhancing_diff`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — The implementation is identical to ``anisotropic_diffusion`` (``kind: "anisotropic"``). True coherence-enhancing diffusion is a method that controls the diffusion direction along the eigenvectors of the structure tensor (connecting linear structures), but this substitute does not compute the structure tensor and instead uses plain Perona-Malik anisotropic diffusion (a limitation of the approximation -- the effect of connecting linear structures is not reproduced). A stand-in for HALCON's ``coherence_enhancing_diff`` (Perform a coherence enhancing diffusion of an image). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `cv_bilateral` (halcon: `bilateral_filter`) `image → image` GPU: none — Bilateral filter (OpenCV implementation). A Gaussian-style smoothing that weights by both spatial proximity and brightness-value proximity, smoothing only flat areas without blurring edges (boundaries with large brightness differences). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `cv_box` (halcon: `mean_image`) `image → image` GPU: none — Simple averaging filter (box filter, OpenCV implementation). The most basic smoothing method, simply taking the average within a square neighborhood -- computationally lighter than Gaussian smoothing, but more prone to ring-shaped artifacts. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `cv_gaussian` (halcon: `gauss_filter`) `image → image` GPU: none — Gaussian smoothing (OpenCV implementation). Standard blurring using a Gaussian kernel; less prone to ringing than a box filter. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `cv_nlmeans` `image → image` GPU: none — Non-local means denoising (OpenCV implementation, grayscale variant). Applies the same idea as sk_nlm (searching the whole image for similar patches and averaging them) using OpenCV's fast implementation. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `cv_sharpen` (halcon: `emphasize`) `image → image` GPU: yes (cv_sharpen) — An unsharp-mask-like sharpening filter (3x3 kernel convolution, OpenCV implementation). Convolves with a kernel whose center is ``1+4a`` and whose top/bottom/left/right neighbors are ``-a`` (at a=0 this is the identity kernel = no change; the larger a is, the stronger the discrete-Laplacian-like high-frequency boost), lifting the contrast near edges. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `dl_aniso_diffusion` (halcon: `anisotropic_diffusion`) `image → image` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — A Perona-Malik-type anisotropic diffusion filter (torch implementation; runs on the GPU if one is available). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `dl_guided_filter` (halcon: `guided_filter`) `image → image` GPU: none — A self-guided filter (guided filter, with the guide image being the input itself; torch implementation). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `f2_gauss_pyramid` (halcon: `gen_gauss_pyramid`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Return one level of the image's Gauss pyramid, down-sampled by 2 ``level`` times (blur + decimate) and then up-sampled back to the original HxW so the result is a band-limited (low-pass) version at reduced resolution. ``a`` selects the level (1..4); ``b`` is ignored. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `gauss_filter` (halcon: `gauss_filter`) `image → image` GPU: yes (gauss_filter@twin) — Smoothing via Gaussian blur (``scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter``, sigma ``0.3+2.7*a``). A stand-in for HALCON's ``gauss_filter`` (Smooth using discrete Gauss functions.) -- HALCON uses a discrete Gaussian kernel (integer arithmetic), while this uses a continuous-Gaussian scipy implementation; it is an approximation, but the results are very close. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_cell_counting`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_focus_stacking`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_sea_ice_concentration`, `poc_search_sweep_width`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`, `poc_vanishing_detail_and_morphing_area`, `poc_vessel_network`, `poc_white_balance`
- `gauss_image` (halcon: `gauss_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (gauss_image) — The implementation is identical to ``gauss_filter`` (the same ``kind: "gauss"`` branch, Gaussian blur with sigma ``0.3+2.7*a``). In HALCON, ``gauss_filter`` (discrete approximation) and ``gauss_image`` (frequency-domain/continuous Gaussian) are separate operators, but this stand-in makes no distinction and points to the same function. A stand-in for HALCON's ``gauss_image`` (Smooth an image using discrete Gaussian functions.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`, `poc_moire_screen`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `gaussian` (halcon: `gauss_filter`) `image → image` GPU: yes (gauss_filter) — Isotropic Gaussian smoothing. Equivalent to HALCON's ``gauss_filter`` (Smooth using discrete Gauss functions.). · examples: `coherence_scanning`, `color_transport`, `ct_inspection`, `degenerate_inputs`, `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `genspark_external_review`, `inspection_workflow`, `mcp_task_score`, `mcp_usability`, `perf_pointcloud_descriptors`, `photon_timeresolved`, `poc_ai_built_inspection_scored`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_chromatic_confocal`, `poc_dtof_ranging`, `poc_flybrain_pointcloud`, `poc_interferometry_step`, `poc_itof_multifreq`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_nir_silicon_transmission`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`, `poc_star_astrometry`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`, `quickstart`, `typed_results_json`, `video_streaming`
- `guided_filter` (halcon: `guided_filter`) `image → image` GPU: none — The implementation is identical to ``bilateral_filter`` (``kind: "bilateral"``). The true guided filter (edge-preserving smoothing based on a local linear model) is a mathematically different algorithm, but this substitute uses the bilateral filter instead (an approximation to satisfy the similar purpose of edge-preserving smoothing; the resulting values do not match). A stand-in for HALCON's ``guided_filter`` (Guided filtering of an image). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `isotropic_diffusion` (halcon: `isotropic_diffusion`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — The implementation is a simple Gaussian blur (``gaussian_filter``, sigma ``0.5+2.5*a``). Since the solution of the isotropic diffusion equation is mathematically equivalent to convolution with a Gaussian kernel, this approximation is theoretically valid (it has no edge-preserving effect like anisotropic diffusion, and smooths uniformly regardless of direction). Corresponds to HALCON's ``isotropic_diffusion`` (Perform an isotropic diffusion of an image). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `kuwahara` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Kuwahara filter (1976): edge-preserving smoothing that outputs the mean of whichever of four overlapping windows has the smallest variance. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `mean_box` (halcon: `mean_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (mean_image) — Simple averaging (box) filter over a rectangular window. Equivalent to HALCON's ``mean_image`` (Smooth by averaging.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `mean_box_wh` (halcon: `mean_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Averaging (box) filter with independently chosen width and height. Equivalent to HALCON's ``mean_image`` (Smooth by averaging.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `mcp_task_score`
- `mean_curvature_flow` (halcon: `mean_curvature_flow`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Smoothing that **approximates** mean curvature flow by repeatedly applying a small-sigma (0.6) Gaussian blur. Rather than the true mean-curvature PDE (the diffusion equation that a separate implementation on the ``ops`` side actually performs), it substitutes computationally cheap iterative blurring -- a limitation specific to this backend's approximation. A stand-in for HALCON's ``mean_curvature_flow`` (Apply the mean curvature flow to an image.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `mean_image` (halcon: `mean_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (mean_image@twin) — Rectangular mean filter (box filter). An approximation equivalent to HALCON's ``mean_image`` (Smooth by averaging.) that replaces the pixel of interest with the average over a window of side length k. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_document_scan`, `poc_focus_stacking`, `poc_white_balance`
- `sigma_image` (halcon: `sigma_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Non-linear smoothing via a sigma filter. It averages only the neighboring pixels close to the center pixel value (``|x-mean|<σ``) -- near edges, tones from the opposite side are not mixed into the average, so this results in noise removal that preserves edges better than a mean filter. Equivalent to HALCON's ``sigma_image`` (Non-linear smoothing with the sigma filter.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `simulate_defocus` (halcon: `simulate_defocus`) `image → image` GPU: yes (simulate_defocus) — Smoothing that simulates uniform out-of-focus blur (defocus). Implemented as a rectangular-window mean filter (box filter, ``ndimage.uniform_filter``), approximating with a square window rather than the true blur shape from a circular aperture (circle-of-confusion). a sets the window width to one of four levels, 3/5/7/9 (``_k(a)``), and b is unused. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `simulate_motion` (halcon: `simulate_motion`) `image → image` GPU: none — Simulates linear motion blur. Creates a line-segment kernel of length ``5+10*b`` pixels in the direction of angle ``pi*a`` (0-180 degrees) and convolves it. Equivalent to HALCON's ``simulate_motion`` (Simulation of (linearly) motion blur.). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `sk_nlm` `image → image` GPU: none — Non-local means denoising. Searches the entire image, not just nearby pixels, for similar patches and averages them -- the difference from simple smoothing is that it can remove noise only in flat areas while preserving repeating patterns and textures. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`
- `sk_rolling_ball` `image → image` GPU: yes (sk_rolling_ball) — Background subtraction by the rolling-ball method. Treats image brightness as terrain, rolls a ball of a given radius underneath it, estimates the resulting envelope surface as the background, and subtracts it from the original image -- used to remove uneven illumination (gradual brightness gradients). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `sk_tv` `image → image` GPU: yes (sk_tv) — Total variation denoising (TV denoising, Chambolle's method). Smooths noise in flat regions while preserving edges - unlike median/Gaussian blur, it is characterized by not easily degrading the sharpness of contours. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`
- `sk_tv_bregman` `image → image` GPU: none — Total variation denoising (TV denoising, Split-Bregman method). Uses the same TV-regularization idea as sk_tv but with a different optimization algorithm (Bregman splitting), said to converge faster. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `sk_wavelet` `image → image` GPU: none — Denoising via wavelet transform. Decomposes the image into the wavelet domain, discards small coefficients (regarded as noise) using BayesShrink-criterion thresholding, and then applies the inverse transform. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`
- `smooth_image` (halcon: `smooth_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — General-purpose smoothing approximated by a single Gaussian blur (sigma ``0.5+2.0*a``). HALCON's ``smooth_image`` (Smooth an image using various filters.) is a versatile operator that lets you choose among several filter types such as Deriche/Gauss/Mean, but here it is simplified to a single Gaussian type (a limitation of this approximation). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `unsharp` (halcon: `emphasize`) `image → image` GPU: yes (unsharp_masking) — Unsharp mask. ★It clips to [0,1] on the way out (2026-09-02). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_camera_shake_deblur`, `poc_real_deblur_honesty`, `poc_superresolution_limits`
- `xcv3_denoise_tvl1` `image → image` GPU: none — Total variation L1 denoising (OpenCV ``cv2.denoise_TVL1``, Primal-Dual algorithm). A method based on total variation minimization that removes noise while preserving edges, leaving edges sharper than ordinary Gaussian smoothing. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xcv3_pyr_laplacian` `image → image` GPU: none — Sharpening via a Laplacian pyramid. A kind of unsharp masking that enhances the image by adding back the difference (one level of a Laplacian pyramid, corresponding to a band-pass component) obtained by subtracting, from the original image, the image restored via ``pyrUp`` after being shrunk with ``pyrDown`` (the low-frequency component). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xcv_edge_preserving` `image → image` GPU: none — OpenCV's edgePreservingFilter (edge-preserving smoothing; ``flags=1`` = RECURS_FILTER = recursive filter method). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xkor_bilateral` `image → image` GPU: none — Bilateral filter (edge-preserving smoothing). Calls ``kornia.filters.bilateral_blur`` with a 5x5 kernel. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xkor_gaussian` `image → image` GPU: none — Gaussian blur (kornia's GPU-native implementation). Applies ``kornia.filters.gaussian_blur2d`` on a torch tensor with a window sized to sigma. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xkor_motion_blur` `image → image` GPU: none — Motion blur. Calls ``kornia.filters.motion_blur``. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xkor_unsharp` `image → image` GPU: none — Unsharp mask (sharpening). Calls ``kornia.filters.unsharp_mask`` with a window sized to sigma (``v + (v - G_σ * v)``, strength fixed at 1). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xpil_smooth_more` `image → image` GPU: none — Pillow's smoothing filter (strong version). Blurs more strongly than ``SMOOTH`` using the fixed kernel of ``PIL.ImageFilter.SMOOTH_MORE``. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xpil_unsharp_mask` `image → image` GPU: none — Pillow's unsharp mask. Calls ``PIL.ImageFilter.UnsharpMask`` (a CPU implementation corresponding to the kornia version ``xkor_unsharp``). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsk3_rank_mean_bilateral` `image → image` GPU: none — Local bilateral mean (skimage ``filters.rank.mean_bilateral``). An edge-preserving smoothing that, within the disk neighborhood, averages only the pixels falling within the range from ``s0`` below to ``s1`` above the center pixel's value. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsp_cspline_smooth` `image → image` GPU: none — Cubic spline smoothing filter (``scipy.signal.cspline2d``). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsp_dct_denoise` `image → image` GPU: none — Noise removal via hard-thresholding of DCT coefficients (a DCT-based version of wavelet shrinkage). · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`
- `xsp_savgol` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Smooths the image with a Savitzky-Golay filter (applied one-dimensionally, column direction first then row direction). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xsp_wiener` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Suppresses noise using the Wiener adaptive filter (``scipy.signal.wiener``). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`, `poc_prnu_camera_fingerprint`
- `xwt_firm_denoise` `image → image` GPU: none — Wavelet denoising using firm thresholding (firm/semisoft thresholding, ``pywt.threshold_firm``). Has characteristics between soft and hard thresholding; applied to each detail coefficient from a 2-level ``sym4`` decomposition before reconstruction. · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xwt_lf_reconstruct` `image → image` GPU: none — Low-frequency reconstructed image. Decomposes with ``db2``, zeroes out all detail coefficients, and reconstructs via inverse transform from the approximation component alone -- the result is a multi-level wavelet-smoothed image close to a Gaussian blur. · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`
- `xwt_visushrink` `image → image` GPU: none — VisuShrink-style wavelet denoising. Decomposes with ``db4`` over 2 levels, applies soft thresholding to each level's detail coefficients, then reconstructs via inverse transform (VisuShrink normally derives this threshold automatically from the noise level, but here it is a simplified version given directly via ``a``). · examples: `gallery2d_smoothing_rank`

#### 2d / subpix (6)
- `sp_critical_points_sub_pix` (halcon: `critical_points_sub_pix`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Detects the sub-pixel positions of maxima, minima, and saddle points together (equivalent to HALCON ``critical_points_sub_pix``). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`
- `sp_local_max_sub_pix` (halcon: `local_max_sub_pix`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Detects local maxima of the gray-value surface with sub-pixel accuracy (an alternative implementation of HALCON ``local_max_sub_pix``. ``halcon=""``: not double-claimed under that name because an existing core op already covers the same coordinates). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`, `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `sp_local_min_sub_pix` (halcon: `local_min_sub_pix`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Detects local minima of the gray-value surface with sub-pixel accuracy (equivalent to HALCON ``local_min_sub_pix``). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`
- `sp_lowlands_center` (halcon: `lowlands_center`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Returns the centroid of minimum 'basins' (flat regions lower than their surroundings) (equivalent to HALCON ``lowlands_center``). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`
- `sp_plateaus` (halcon: `plateaus`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Returns the centroid of connected flat regions (plateaus) of equal (quantised) gray value as a sub-pixel position (equivalent to HALCON ``plateaus``). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`
- `sp_saddle_points_sub_pix` (halcon: `saddle_points_sub_pix`) `image → contour` GPU: none — Detects saddle points of the gray-value surface with sub-pixel accuracy (equivalent to HALCON ``saddle_points_sub_pix``). · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`

#### 2d / tactile (5)
- `tac_contact_mask` `image → region` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Contact region of a tactile frame by pseudo-reference background subtraction: ``dev = |v - G_sigma(v)|`` with ``sigma = max(2, min(H,W)/6)`` (the low-frequency envelope stands in for the undeformed reference frame), thresholded at ``thr = 0.005 + 0.145*a`` gray levels, then cleaned with ``round(3*b)`` iterations of binary opening followed by binary closing (3x3, 8-connected). ``a`` = deviation threshold (sensitivity), ``b`` = morphological cleanup strength. Returns a BINARY 0/1 float64 region of the input HxW; a perfectly flat (constant) frame has zero deviation everywhere and therefore yields an EMPTY mask. · examples: `poc_tacsim_elastic_membrane`, `sim2real_and_alife`
- `tac_height_from_shading` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Height/relief map by Poisson integration of the shading gradients -- the integration stage of GelSight depth reconstruction (and of photometric stereo): the image gradients are read as surface slopes ``p = gain*gx``, ``q = gain*gy`` and the Poisson equation ``lap(h) = div(p,q)`` is solved spectrally, ``h_hat = div_hat / lap_hat`` with the discrete Laplacian symbol ``2cos(2*pi*u/W)+2cos(2*pi*v/H)-4`` and the (undetermined) DC mode pinned to zero. ``a`` = gradient gain (0.25..4.25x), ``b`` = pre-smoothing sigma of the gradient field (0..3). Output is min-max normalised to [0,1] and refit to HxW; a constant frame integrates to a flat (all-zero) relief. · examples: `sim2real_and_alife`
- `tac_pressure_proxy` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Contact-pressure proxy map: the rectified deviation from the pseudo-reference background ``dev = |v - G_sigma(v)|`` is gated to the high-deviation (contact) area -- a relative gate at ``0.15 * max(dev)`` plus an absolute floor of 0.005 -- amplified by the sensitivity gain and Gaussian-smoothed, which is the standard "indentation depth is monotone in normal force" surrogate used when a tactile pad carries no force sensor. ``a`` = sensitivity (gain 1..10x), ``b`` = smoothing radius (sigma 0.5..4.5). Output clipped to [0,1], HxW; a flat frame yields an all-zero pressure map (no contact, no force). · examples: `sim2real_and_alife`
- `tac_shear_field` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — In-plane shear proxy from the 2-D structure tensor (Foerstner / Bigun-Granlund orientation coherence). The tensor ``J = G_sigma(grad v * grad v^T)`` has eigenvalues l1 >= l2, and the coherence ``(l1-l2)/(l1+l2) = sqrt((J11-J22)^2 + 4*J12^2) / (J11+J22)`` is 1 where the gel texture is stretched into a single dominant orientation (as it is under tangential/shear load) and 0 where it is isotropic. The result is additionally weighted by the tensor trace (gradient energy) so that texture-free, un-contacted gel stays dark instead of amplifying noise orientation. ``a`` = tensor integration sigma (0.6..4.6), ``b`` = output gain (0.5..2.5). Output clipped to [0,1], HxW; a constant frame has zero gradient energy and yields an all-zero shear field. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`, `sim2real_and_alife`
- `tac_surface_normal` `image → image` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Surface-normal z-component (slope map) from the shading gradients, using Horn's shape-from-shading normal parameterisation ``n = (-p, -q, 1)/sqrt(1+p^2+q^2)`` so that ``nz = 1/sqrt(1+p^2+q^2)`` with ``p = gain*gx``, ``q = gain*gy``. Flat (uncontacted) gel gives nz = 1, steep indentation walls tend to 0, so the map is already a valid [0,1] encoding. ``a`` = gradient gain (1..21x -- how steep the shading is taken to be), ``b`` = pre-smoothing sigma of the image (0..3) to tame sensor noise. Constant input -> all-ones (perfectly flat gel). · examples: `sim2real_and_alife`

#### 2d / texture (28)
- `bootstrap_std_error` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Measures the **standard error** of the local standard deviation without assuming a distribution (bootstrap). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `cooc_feature_matrix` (halcon: `cooc_feature_matrix`) `image → feature` GPU: none — Computes the Haralick texture feature ``energy`` (angular second moment, i.e., how concentrated the matrix values are = texture uniformity) from a gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM, ``skimage.feature.graycomatrix``, quantized to 16 levels, distance ``1+3*a``, angle 0 degrees). Equivalent to HALCON's ``cooc_feature_matrix`` (Calculate gray value features from a co-occurrence matrix.) (HALCON can return multiple features and multiple angles simultaneously, but this is simplified to energy at a fixed 0-degree angle). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_real_texture_invariance`
- `deviation_image` (halcon: `deviation_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (deviation_image) — An image obtained by normalizing the standard deviation of pixel values within a rectangular window (local standard deviation, the square root of ``E[x^2]-E[x]^2``). Visualizes local variation (roughness) in texture. Corresponds to HALCON's ``deviation_image`` (Calculate the standard deviation of gray values within rectangular windows). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `entropy_image` (halcon: `entropy_image`) `image → image` GPU: none — An image obtained by normalizing the grayscale Shannon entropy within a circular window (``skimage.filters.rank.entropy``, 8-bit quantized). A texture measure of the "spread" of gray levels within the window: low in uniform regions and high in regions where diverse gray levels mix. Corresponds to HALCON's ``entropy_image`` (Calculate the entropy of gray values within a rectangular window) -- an approximation using a circular window here versus HALCON's rectangular window. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `f2_symmetry` (halcon: `symmetry`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Local reflective symmetry of gray values along a row. For each pixel the weighted asymmetry sum_d (1/d)|I(i,j-d) - I(i,j+d)| over d=1..r is measured; a low response means the neighbourhood is left-right symmetric about that column. ``a`` sets the radius r (1..6); ``b`` is ignored. Output is the asymmetry response normalised to [0,1]. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `gabor` (halcon: `gen_gabor`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Gabor energy |v * g| — an oriented band-pass texture response. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_patch_anomaly`
- `gen_gabor` (halcon: `gen_gabor`) `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns the absolute value of the convolution response from a single Gabor kernel (orientation ``theta=pi*a``, frequency ``0.1+0.3*b``), normalized by the kernel's L1 norm. A real-part-only kernel with the DC component removed (mean subtracted), acting as a band-pass texture filter that responds selectively to stripe patterns of the specified direction and frequency. Corresponds to HALCON's ``gen_gabor`` (Generate a Gabor filter) -- a simplified version using only a real kernel with no imaginary part / phase. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `local_bimodality` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — **Local bimodality** (bimodality coefficient). Without choosing even 1 threshold, returns only "does this place split into 2 values?" as a 0-to-1 map. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `local_std` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns the standard deviation within a local window **in the same units as the input** (not normalized). Corresponds to HALCON's ``deviation_image`` (Calculate the standard deviation of gray values within rectangular windows.). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `scale_select_std` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Local standard deviation that **chooses the window size** per pixel (Lepski / ICI rule). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `sk_entropy` (halcon: `entropy_image`) `image → image` GPU: none — Local entropy. Computes the Shannon entropy (base-2 logarithm) of the gray-value distribution in the neighborhood (disk-shaped) around each pixel, and images it as the minimum number of bits needed to encode that location -- a measure of texture complexity/information content. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `sk_frangi` (halcon: `lines_gauss`) `image → image` GPU: none — Frangi's tubular structure detection filter (vesselness filter).
