Detects elongated tubular structures such as blood vessels, wrinkles, or rivers from the eigenvalue ratios of the Hessian matrix. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`
- `sk_gabor` (halcon: `gen_gabor`) `image → image` GPU: none — Gabor filter response magnitude. A classic feature extractor that convolves a sinusoidally modulated Gaussian kernel and responds strongly to texture with a specific spatial frequency and orientation. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `sk_hessian` (halcon: `lines_gauss`) `image → image` GPU: none — Hybrid Hessian filter. Detects tubular structures much like Frangi, but with a different smoothing method (it can be used approximately as a substitute for Frangi). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `sk_lbp` `image → image` GPU: none — LBP (Local Binary Pattern). A texture descriptor robust to illumination changes, built by comparing each pixel to its neighbors on a surrounding circle to form a binary code. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_real_texture_invariance`
- `sk_meijering` (halcon: `lines_gauss`) `image → image` GPU: none — Meijering's neurite detection filter (neuriteness filter). Like Frangi, it computes a similarity to tubular structures from the eigenvalues of the Hessian, but uses a different normalization method (a formula tuned for neurite images). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `sk_shape_index` `image → image` GPU: none — Shape index. Represents local surface shape as a single scalar from -1 (spherical cup/pit) through 0 (saddle point) to +1 (spherical cap/dome), derived from the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix -- a descriptor that summarizes the "orientation" of curvature. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `std_filter` (halcon: `deviation_image`) `image → image` GPU: yes (std_image) — Standard deviation within a local window (an indicator of texture coarseness). Equivalent to HALCON's ``deviation_image`` (Calculate the standard deviation of gray values within rectangular windows.). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `structure_tensor_coherence` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns the local **degree of orientation alignment** (anisotropy of the structure tensor) in ``[0,1]``. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `structure_tensor_orientation` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns the local **direction in which stripes run** (principal axis of the structure tensor) mapped to ``[0,1]``. · examples: `degenerate_inputs`, `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `texture_laws` (halcon: `texture_laws`) `image → image` GPU: yes (texture_laws) — The implementation is the local variance (the variance version of ``deviation_image``, i.e. ``E[x^2]-E[x]^2`` within the window). The true Laws' texture filter is a bank of 25 convolutions built from 1D kernel pairs such as L5/E5/S5/W5/R5 (capturing energy/edges/waves/spots/ripples), but this substitute uses a single local variance instead of the full kernel bank (a limitation of the approximation -- direction- and frequency-specific information is lost). A stand-in for HALCON's ``texture_laws`` (Filter an image using a Laws texture filter). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `tf_census_transform` `image → image` GPU: none — census_transform: the 3x3 non-parametric census bit-signature image. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `tf_rank_transform` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — rank_transform: the local rank of each pixel among its neighbours. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `xsk2_hog` `image → image` GPU: none — A visualization image of HOG (Histogram of Oriented Gradients) features. Calls ``skimage.feature.hog`` with ``visualize=True`` and returns the visualization image (discarding the feature vector itself). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `xsk_meijering` `image → image` GPU: none — Meijering neuriteness filter. Applies ``skimage.filters.meijering`` at three scales (sigma=1,2,3) to enhance thin curvilinear structures (such as blood vessels or neurites) (like the Frangi family, it computes ridge-likeness from the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix, but Meijering also responds strongly at branch points). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`
- `xsk_sato` `image → image` GPU: none — Sato tubeness filter. Applies ``skimage.filters.sato`` at three scales (sigma=1,2,3) to enhance tubular structures (such as blood vessels). Computing line/tube-likeness from the eigenvalue ratio of the Hessian matrix is the same family as ``xsk_meijering``, but the response weighting differs, and it doesn't respond as strongly at branch points as Meijering does. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`
- `xsk_struct_coherence` `image → image` GPU: none — Structure tensor coherence (consistency of orientation). · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `xsp_hilbert_env` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Extracts the amplitude envelope of the analytic signal (Hilbert transform) along the row direction. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`

#### 2d / texture-feature (1)
- `xmh_pftas` `image → feature` GPU: none — Variance of the 54-dimensional PFTAS (parameter-free threshold adjacency statistics, ``mahotas.features.pftas``) feature vector. A texture feature that aggregates histograms counting adjacent-pixel intensity relationships using a parameter-free threshold. · examples: `gallery2d_features`

#### 2d / texture/shape-feature (1)
- `xmh_zernike` `image → feature` GPU: none — Sum of Zernike moments (``mahotas.features.zernike_moments``). Collapses the rotation-invariant shape/intensity-distribution features of the image mapped onto the unit circle into a single real number. · examples: `gallery2d_features`

#### 2d / tomography (5)
- `tm_backproject_unfiltered` `image → image` GPU: none — Plain (UN-filtered) back-projection of the input sinogram -- the classic blurry reconstruction. No ramp filter is applied, so high frequencies are suppressed and every point spreads a 1/r blur: this deliberately shows why FBP's filter is needed. ``a``/``b`` are unused (this is the fixed naive baseline). Uses ``skimage.transform.iradon`` with ``filter_name=None`` when available, else the NumPy plain back-projection. Output refit to HxW. · examples: `gallery2d_physics_alife_3d`
- `tm_fbp_reconstruct` `image → image` GPU: none — Filtered back-projection: treat ``v`` as a sinogram (rows = angles, cols = detector, angles assumed uniform over [0,180)) and reconstruct the slice. ``b`` picks the reconstruction filter -- b < 0.5 -> Ram-Lak (ramp), b >= 0.5 -> Shepp-Logan. ``a`` is unused (the filter is the meaningful knob). Uses ``skimage.transform.iradon`` when available, else the NumPy FFT-ramp-filtered back-projection. Output refit to HxW. · examples: `gallery2d_physics_alife_3d`
- `tm_radon_forward` `image → image` GPU: none — Forward Radon projection: treat ``v`` as a slice image and integrate it along parallel rays to build a sinogram (rows = angles, cols = detector), refit to the original HxW. ``a`` sets how many angles are acquired (``n = round(H*a)`` clamped to 8..360 -- the sparse-view knob), ``b`` sets the angular span (``span = 180*min(1, 0.5+b)`` deg: b < 0.5 is limited-angle CT, b >= 0.5 -- including the default b = 0.5 -- is the full [0,180) span that ``tm_fbp_reconstruct`` / ``tm_sart_reconstruct`` / ``tm_backproject_unfiltered`` assume, so the natural chain forward -> inverse round-trips at default knobs). Uses ``skimage.transform.radon`` when available, else the NumPy rotate-and-sum Radon transform. · examples: `gallery2d_physics_alife_3d`
- `tm_sart_reconstruct` `image → image` GPU: none — Algebraic reconstruction: run a few SART/SIRT sweeps on the input sinogram (rows = angles). ``a`` sets the iteration count (``round(1+a*4)`` -> 1..5), ``b`` sets the relaxation factor (``0.05 + b*0.35``). Uses ``skimage.transform.iradon_sart`` when available, else a self-contained NumPy SIRT (project -> residual -> weighted back-projection) loop. Output refit to HxW. · examples: `gallery2d_physics_alife_3d`
- `tm_sinogram_denoise` `image → image` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Smooth the input sinogram along the ANGLE direction (rows). Neighbouring projection angles view almost the same object, so angle-direction smoothing is a genuine consistency prior that suppresses per-angle detector noise while preserving the sinusoidal traces. ``a`` sets the angle-axis Gaussian sigma (``a*4``), ``b`` adds a gentle detector-axis sigma (``b*1.5``). Output stays a same-shape sinogram in [0,1]. · examples: `gallery2d_physics_alife_3d`

- `xmh_daubechies` `image → image` GPU: none — Daubechies wavelet transform (``mahotas.daubechies``). Same layout as xmh_haar (single level, coefficients packed into an array of the original image size and min-max normalized), but with the basis changed to the Daubechies family. · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`
- `xmh_haar` `image → image` GPU: none — Haar wavelet transform (``mahotas.haar``). Truncates the image to an even size before transforming, then displays the resulting coefficient array -- a Matlab-style in-place layout where the approximation/horizontal/vertical/diagonal subbands are packed into an array the same size as the original image -- directly as an image after min-max normalization. · examples: `gallery2d_geometry`

#### 3d / metrics (8)
- `chamfer_distance` `points × points → measurement` GPU: none — The symmetric Chamfer distance = 0.5*(mean_a min_b + mean_b min_a). → scalar. Smaller is a closer match. · examples: `itokawa_pose_canonical`, `itokawa_shape_match`, `mesh_lod_download`, `metrics_eval`, `poisson_surface_recon`

- `hausdorff_distance` `points × points → measurement` GPU: none — The symmetric Hausdorff distance = max(max_a min_b, max_b min_a). → scalar. The worst-case discrepancy. · examples: `mesh_lod_download`, `pointcloud_downsampling`, `poisson_surface_recon`
- `m3c2_distance` `points × points → signal` GPU: none — Measures the difference between point clouds from 2 epochs **along the normal direction** (M3C2). → the 2 values ``(distance, lod)``. · examples: `metrics_eval`
- `normal_consistency` `points × normals → measurement` GPU: none — Normal agreement over nearest-neighbour correspondences = mean|cos(na, nb)| (orientation ignored). → [0,1]. 1 = perfect agreement. · examples: `metrics_eval`
- `pose_error` `pose × pose → table` GPU: none — Pose error = (rotation angle [deg], translation norm). For comparing a registration result against ground truth. → (rot_deg, trans_err). · examples: `itokawa_self_register`
- `rmse_correspondence` `points × points → measurement` GPU: none — RMSE over known correspondences (same index) = sqrt(mean |a_i − b_i|²). → scalar. For judging the registration residual. · examples: `metrics_eval`
- `voxel_iou` `voxel × voxel → measurement` GPU: none — The IoU (intersection over union) of voxel occupancy. → [0,1]. Volumetric agreement. · examples: `metrics_eval`

#### 3d / morphology (7)
- `morph_blackhat3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D black-hat = closing − vol. Extracts the **dark structures and holes** smaller than the structuring element. · examples: `diff_features`
- `morph_close3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D closing = dilation → erosion. Fills the **dark structures (gaps and cavities)** smaller than the structuring element. · examples: `morphology_3d`
- `morph_dilate3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D greyscale dilation (the local max over a structuring element of radius r). Expands the bright regions. · examples: `morphology_3d`
- `morph_erode3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D greyscale erosion (the local min over the structuring element). Shrinks the bright regions. se is the same as for dilate. · examples: `morphology_3d`
- `morph_gradient3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D morphological gradient = dilation − erosion. Extracts **boundaries and surfaces** (an edge source in place of Sobel). · examples: `morphology_3d`
- `morph_open3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D opening = erosion → dilation. Removes the **bright structures (spikes and grains)** smaller than the structuring element. · examples: `morphology_3d`
- `morph_tophat3d` `voxel → voxel` GPU: native (device argument) — 3-D white top-hat = vol − opening. Extracts the **bright structures** smaller than the structuring element (keypoint pre-processing). · examples: `diff_features`, `morphology_3d`

- `mesh_edge_lengths` `mesh → signal` GPU: none — Local edge length of a triangle mesh, per vertex, per face or per unique edge. · examples: `itokawa_regolith_hero`
- `mesh_scatter_boulders` `mesh → mesh` GPU: none — Scatter partly-buried boulders on a mesh (power-law sizes, seeded) → ``(V, F)`` · examples: `itokawa_regolith_hero`
- `mesh_subdivide` `mesh → mesh` GPU: none — Refine a triangle mesh → ``(V, F)`` by midpoint subdivision or adaptive tessellation. · examples: `itokawa_regolith_hero`
- `terrain_region_mask` `mesh → signal` GPU: none — Per-face terrain weights (M,) in [0,1]: 0 = smooth regolith "sea", 1 = rough highland. · examples: `itokawa_regolith_hero`

#### 3d / transform (12)
- `depth_to_points` `depth → points` GPU: none — Depth map (2.5-D) → point cloud (pinhole back-projection). It connects the depth row to every method. · examples: `structured_light_scan`, `transforms_repr`
- `estimate_point_normals` `points → normals` GPU: none — Point set (N,3) → unit normals (the smallest eigenvector of the local k-neighbourhood covariance = PCA). · examples: `fpfh_correspondence`
- `gaussians_to_voxel` `points → voxel` GPU: none — 3DGS (anisotropic Gaussians) → a density voxel volume. Each Gaussian is placed at its mean with its opacity, then smoothed by the mean scale. · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `mesh_to_points` `mesh → points` GPU: none — Mesh (vertices + faces) → a surface point set (area-weighted uniform sampling). The mesh → point-cloud conversion. · examples: `mesh_decimate`
- `mesh_to_voxel` `mesh → voxel` GPU: native (device argument, inside a chain only) — Mesh (vertices + faces) → a density voxel volume. Uniform sampling on the faces → splat (it connects the mesh row to every method). · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `points_to_voxel` `points → voxel` GPU: none — Point set (N,3) → a density voxel volume (size³). Splatted with scatter_add, optionally Gaussian-smoothed. · examples: `sh_descriptor_retrieval`, `shape_desc_pose`
- `sdf_to_occupancy` `sdf → voxel` GPU: none — SDF → an occupancy voxel volume (at or below iso = inside = 1). The way back from an SDF to voxels. · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `signed_distance_field` `voxel → sdf` GPU: native (device argument) — Occupancy/density voxels → a signed distance field SDF (inside < 0, outside > 0). edt_jfa applied to both sides. · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `to_points` `voxel × points × mesh × depth × gaussians → points` GPU: none — Any 3-D structure → a point set (the common representation). It funnels all five structures into one entry point. · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `tsdf_from_depth` `depth → sdf` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Depth map (2.5-D) → a TSDF volume (the standard representation of RGB-D reconstruction). The depth → TSDF conversion. · examples: `transforms_repr`
- `voxel_to_mesh` `voxel → mesh` GPU: none — Voxel → mesh (marching cubes, skimage). Returns (verts, faces, normals). The voxel → mesh conversion. · examples: `mesh_smooth`
- `voxel_to_mips` `voxel → images` GPU: none — 3-D → maximum-intensity projections along the three orthogonal directions. The entry point for applying 2-D methods (e.g. accel's 2-D NCC). · examples: `transforms_repr`

#### 3d / tsdf_fusion (3)
- `extract_surface_points` `sdf → points` GPU: none — Extract surface points (M,3) from the TSDF zero crossing (no marching cubes needed; linear interpolation). · examples: `transforms_repr`, `tsdf_fusion_demo`
- `fuse` `depth → sdf` GPU: none — Fuse a depth series into one TSDF volume with new_volume + integrate. Returns (tsdf, weight). · examples: `tsdf_fusion_demo`
- `integrate` `sdf × depth → sdf` GPU: none — Integrate one depth frame into the volume by projective TSDF (in place, a weighted running average). · examples: `transforms_repr`

#### 3d / two_view (5)
- `essential_8point` `image2d × image2d → matrix` GPU: none — The essential matrix E directly from correspondences and K. → E (3,3). · examples: `sfm_recon`
- `fundamental_8point` `image2d × image2d → matrix` GPU: none — Estimate the fundamental matrix F by the normalised eight-point algorithm (rank 2 enforced). → F (3,3). At least eight points are needed. · examples: `two_view_pose`
- `recover_pose` `image2d × image2d → pose` GPU: none — Recover the relative pose (R,t) and the 3-D structure from correspondences and K (disambiguated by cheirality). → (R, t_unit, points3d). · examples: `two_view_pose`
- `sampson_distance` `image2d × image2d → signal` GPU: none — The Sampson distance of the epipolar constraint (the first-order geometric error, per correspondence). → (N,). · examples: `two_view_pose`
- `triangulate` `image2d × image2d → points` GPU: none — DLT triangulation: correspondences from two views plus the projection matrices → 3-D points. → (N,3). · examples: `sfm_recon`

### fit (3 ops / 2 categories)

#### fit / fit (2)
- `fit_circle_geometric` `keypoints → table` GPU: none — Fit a circle and radius to (row, col) points, including short arcs, by geometric least squares. · examples: `fit_ops_from_knowhow`
- `fit_curve_principal_axis` `keypoints → table` GPU: none — Rotate a slanted curved edge to its principal axis, then fit polynomial y'=f(x'). · examples: `fit_ops_from_knowhow`

- `phase_correlation_shift` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Estimate the subpixel translation needed to align two images by phase-only correlation. · examples: `fit_ops_from_knowhow`

### math (115 ops / 12 categories)

Math ops that support visual measurement (linear algebra / statistics / interpolation, polynomials) + computable entry points into complex analysis (contour integrals, Cauchy's integral formula, the argument principle, Laurent coefficients / residues, conformal maps, Cauchy-Riemann residuals). For FFT / complex images see complexops and volfreq; for 1-D functions see funct1d.

#### math / complex (18)
- `cplx_argument_principle` `cpoints × cpoints → measurement` GPU: none — Argument principle: count zeros minus poles enclosed by a contour, from sampled values of ``f`` alone. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_cauchy_value` `cpoints × cpoints → cscalar` GPU: none — Cauchy's integral formula: recover ``f(w)`` **inside** a contour from its values **on** the contour. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_contour_circle` `no input → cpoints` GPU: none — Sample a circle as a closed contour — the standard integration path. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_contour_integral` `cpoints × cpoints → cscalar` GPU: none — Closed contour integral ``∮ f(z) dz`` by the chordal trapezoidal rule. · examples: `math_complex`, `representation_conversion`
- `cplx_cr_residual` `cimage → measurement` GPU: none — Cauchy-Riemann residual of a sampled complex field — "is this field holomorphic?" as a number. · examples: `math_complex`, `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_domain_colour` `cimage → rgbimage` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Domain colouring: turn a complex field into an RGB image you can read. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_escape_time` `no input → image2d` GPU: none — How many steps of ``z -> z**2 + c`` it takes to leave the escape disc. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_joukowski` `cpoints → cpoints` GPU: none — Joukowski (Zhukovsky) conformal map ``w = z + c^2 / z``. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_laurent_coeffs` `cpoints × cpoints → table` GPU: none — Laurent (and Taylor) coefficients on a **uniformly sampled circle** — residues included. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_mobius` `cpoints → cpoints` GPU: none — Möbius (linear fractional) map ``w = (a z + b) / (c z + d)``. · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_newton_basins` `signal → labels2d` GPU: none — Which root of a polynomial does Newton's method fall into, from each point? · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_plane_grid` `no input → cimage` GPU: none — Turns a rectangular window of the complex plane into a grid (laid out like an image: row 0 is the top, i.e. the larger imaginary part). · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_poly_eval` `signal × cpoints → cpoints` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Evaluate a polynomial on the complex plane (Horner, complex-capable). · examples: `math_complex`
- `cplx_rational_field` `roots × roots → cimage` GPU: none — Sample a rational function ``R(z) = gain * prod(z - zeros) / prod(z - poles)``. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `cplx_winding_number` `cpoints → measurement` GPU: none — Winding number of a closed contour around a point (turning number). · examples: `math_complex`, `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `joukowski_circulation` `no input → measurement` GPU: none — The Kutta circulation ``Gamma = 4*pi*a*U*sin(alpha + beta)`` for that section. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `mandelbrot_interior` `cimage → mask` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Closed-form interior test for the main cardioid and the period-2 bulb. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`
- `potential_flow_joukowski` `no input → cimage` GPU: none — Inviscid flow past a Joukowski aerofoil, as a complex velocity field. · examples: `poc_complex_plane_fields`

#### math / construct (8)
- `circle_packing_apollonian` `no input → table` GPU: none — Apollonian gasket from a Descartes quadruple — every circle a theorem. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `curve_locality` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Points ``k`` apart along the curve — how far apart are they on the plane? · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `ford_circles` `no input → table` GPU: none — Ford circles for the Farey fractions — tangency *is* an integer identity. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `ifs_fractal` `no input → pairs` GPU: none — Chaos game on an iterated function system — the dimension is a closed form. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `ifs_similarity_dimension` `no input → measurement` GPU: none — Moran's equation ``sum(r_i**d) = 1`` solved for ``d`` — from the maps alone. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `neighbour_index_gaps` `pairs → signal` GPU: none — How far apart *in index* are a point's nearest neighbours — parastichy as a number. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `phyllotaxis_pattern` `no input → pairs` GPU: none — Vogel's spiral — the angle that packs best, and the spirals it makes. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `space_filling_curve` `no input → pairs` GPU: none — Hilbert / Moore / scan orders on a ``2**order`` square — a permutation, checked. · examples: `poc_theorems_as_pictures`

#### math / dynsys (6)
- `dynsys_bifurcation_map` `no input → pairs` GPU: none — The orbit diagram of a 1-D map — period doubling, as points you can count. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `dynsys_correlation_dimension` `points → measurement` GPU: none — Grassberger-Procaccia correlation dimension — the slope of ``log C(r)``. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `dynsys_lyapunov_spectrum` `no input → signal` GPU: none — The Lyapunov spectrum by tangent flow + QR — and the sum you can check. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `dynsys_poincare_section` `table → pairs` GPU: none — Where a trajectory crosses a plane — with the crossing point interpolated. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `ode_flow_states` `no input → table` GPU: none — Integrate a named vector field — the trajectory, with the order you paid for. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `ode_vector_field_grid` `no input → flow2d` GPU: none — Sample a named field on a grid — a ``flow2d`` the existing viewers take. · examples: `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`

#### math / estimation (12)
- `assign_hungarian` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Solves the assignment problem for a cost matrix (n, m) (Hungarian method of Kuhn 1955 / Munkres 1957, scipy implementation). · examples: `estimation_tour`
- `crlb_gaussian` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Cramér–Rao lower bound under white Gaussian noise (standard deviation sigma). · examples: `estimation_tour`
- `hist_distance` `signal × signal → measurement` GPU: none — Distance and divergence between 2 histograms (non-negative, normalized by their sum). · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `kalman_smooth` `matrix × matrix × matrix × matrix × matrix × signal × matrix → table` GPU: none — Kalman filter (forward) and Rauch–Tung–Striebel smoother (backward) for the linear Gaussian state-space model x_{k+1} = F x_k + w (w ~ N(0,Q)), z_k = H x_k + v (v ~ N(0,R)). · examples: `estimation_tour`, `poc_real_bg_kalman_tracking`
- `mat_expm` `matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Matrix exponential e^A (Padé approximation + scaling-and-squaring, scipy). · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `mat_logm` `matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Principal matrix logarithm log A (the X with e^X = A whose eigenvalues have imaginary parts in (−π, π], scipy). · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `se3_exp` `signal → matrix` GPU: none — Exponential map of SE(3): 6-dimensional twist ξ = (v, ω) (translational velocity v, rotation vector ω) → 4×4 rigid-body transform. · examples: `estimation_tour`
- `se3_log` `matrix → signal` GPU: none — Logarithm map of SE(3): 4×4 rigid-body transform → 6-dimensional twist ξ = (v, ω) (rotation angle < π). Gate: se3_log(se3_exp(ξ)) = ξ. · examples: `estimation_tour`
- `stat_chi2_gof` `signal → table` GPU: none — χ² goodness-of-fit test: whether the counts ``observed`` match the expected counts (uniform by default). Degrees of freedom = number of bins − 1. · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `stat_ks_test` `signal → table` GPU: none — Kolmogorov–Smirnov test. Given ``y``, a 2-sample test (whether both come from the same distribution); without it, goodness of fit to the standard normal distribution. · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `stat_ttest_paired` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Paired t-test: whether the mean of the differences d = x − y from measuring the same subjects 2 times is 0. · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `stat_ttest_welch` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Welch's t-test: the difference in means of 2 groups without assuming equal variances (degrees of freedom by Welch–Satterthwaite). · examples: `estimation_tour`

#### math / geometry (10)
- `angle_defect` `mesh → table` GPU: none — Per-vertex angle defect (discrete Gaussian curvature) K_v = 2π − Σ(angles of the triangles at that vertex). For boundary vertices, π − Σ (geodesic curvature). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `delaunay_triangulate` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Triangulation of planar points (N, 2) or tetrahedralization of spatial points (N, 3) (Delaunay, scipy.spatial = Qhull). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `geodesic_heat` `mesh → table` GPU: none — Geodesic distance on a surface by the heat method (Crane et al. 2013). ``source`` is a vertex index (or a sequence of indices; default vertex 0). The mesh may be given as ``(vertices, faces)`` or as 1 mesh tuple. · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `geodesic_heat_grid` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Computes obstacle-avoiding geodesic distance on the grid of a 2-D image or 3-D volume by the heat method (grid version of Crane et al. 2013). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `mesh_euler_characteristic` `mesh → table` GPU: none — V − E + F of a triangle mesh and, for a closed orientable surface, the genus g = (2 − χ)/2. · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `mesh_torus` `no input → mesh` GPU: none — Closed triangle mesh (vertices, faces) of a torus (doughnut). Major radius R, tube radius r (R > r > 0). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `nurbs_circle` `no input → table` GPU: none — A degree-2 NURBS that represents a circle exactly (Piegl & Tiller Example 7.1: the 4 corners and the midpoints of the 4 sides of a square, corner weights 1/√2). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `nurbs_curve` (halcon: `gen_contour_nurbs_xld`) `matrix → table` GPU: none — Evaluates a NURBS curve (weighted; in general it does not pass through the control points). · examples: `geometry_tour`, `machine_vision_tour`
- `nurbs_revolve` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Surface of revolution obtained by sweeping a planar NURBS curve (r, z) 1 full turn around the z axis (Piegl & Tiller §8.5). · examples: `geometry_tour`
- `nurbs_surface` `no input → table` GPU: none — Evaluates a NURBS surface (tensor product). · examples: `gallery_math_numerics_filters`

- `interp_cubic` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Cubic-spline interpolation (``scipy.interpolate.CubicSpline``). · examples: `math_metrology`
- `interp_linear` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Piecewise-linear interpolation of ``(x, y)`` samples at query *xq*. · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_thermal_radiometry`

- `poly_eval` `signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Evaluate a polynomial (coefficients highest-power-first) at *x*. · examples: `math_metrology`, `signal_filter`

- `poly_roots` `signal → roots` GPU: none — All roots of a polynomial (coefficients highest-power-first) — complex included. · examples: `math_metrology`

#### math / linalg (10)
- `mat_cholesky` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Cholesky factorisation ``A = L @ Lᵀ`` of a symmetric positive-definite matrix. · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `mat_cond` `matrix → measurement` GPU: none — Spectral (2-norm) condition number ``s_max / s_min`` — the numerical canary of the whole linalg family. · examples: `math_metrology`
- `mat_eig` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Eigen-decomposition of a **general** square matrix ``A V = V diag(w)`` (complex in general). · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `mat_eigh` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Eigen-decomposition of a **symmetric** matrix (LAPACK ``syevd``). · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_thermal_radiometry`
- `mat_lstsq` `matrix × signal → table` GPU: none — Least-squares solution of an over-determined system ``A x ≈ b`` (LAPACK ``gelsd``, SVD-based). · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`, `poc_sea_ice_concentration`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`
- `mat_lu` `matrix → table` GPU: none — LU factorisation ``P @ A = L @ U`` (``L`` unit lower, ``U`` upper). · examples: `gallery_math_stats_linalg`
- `mat_pinv` `matrix → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse via SVD, with the cutoff **explicit**. · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_machine_condition_fusion`
- `mat_qr` `matrix → table` GPU: none — QR factorisation ``A = Q @ R`` (``Q`` with orthonormal columns, ``R`` upper triangular). · examples: `numerics_tour`
- `mat_solve` `matrix × signal → signal` GPU: none — Solve the square linear system ``A x = b`` (LAPACK ``gesv``, LU with partial pivoting). · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`
- `mat_svd` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Singular value decomposition ``A = U @ diag(s) @ Vt`` (LAPACK ``gesdd``). · examples: `math_metrology`, `poc_water_level`

- `bessel` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Bessel functions. ``kind`` = ``"j"`` (J of the 1st kind) / ``"y"`` (Y of the 2nd kind) / ``"i"``, ``"k"`` (modified). · examples: `gallery_math_numerics_filters`
- `chebyshev_coeffs_nd` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Computes N-dimensional Chebyshev coefficients from values sampled on a tensor-product Chebyshev–Lobatto grid (DCT-I). · examples: `numerics_tour`
- `chebyshev_eval_nd` `table × matrix → signal` GPU: none — Evaluates the coefficients from ``chebyshev_coeffs_nd`` at points (M, d) (per axis T_k(t) = cos(k·arccos t)). · examples: `numerics_tour`

- `gauss_cubature` `no input → table` GPU: none — Nodes (n^dim, dim) and weights for quadrature over the box [a, b]^dim (a, b may also be per axis) by a tensor product of Gauss–Legendre rules. · examples: `gallery_math_numerics_filters`
- `gauss_quadrature` `no input → table` GPU: none — Nodes and weights of n-point Gauss quadrature. ∫ f ≈ Σ w_k f(x_k). · examples: `numerics_tour`
- `integrate_hamiltonian` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Integrates a named Hamiltonian system (mass 1) in time. Return value ``{"t","q","p","energy","energy_drift","method","system"}``. · examples: `numerics_tour`
- `interp_barycentric` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Evaluates at x the polynomial (degree len−1) through the points (xk, yk) with the barycentric formula (Berrut & Trefethen 2004). · examples: `numerics_tour`
- `low_discrepancy` `no input → matrix` GPU: none — Low-discrepancy point sequence (n, dim) in [0, 1)^dim. · examples: `numerics_tour`

- `esprit_doa` `matrix → table` GPU: none — ESPRIT (Roy & Kailath 1989): solves for the directions without a grid, from the array's invariance under a "shift by 1 element". · examples: `spectral_tour`

- `abel_inverse` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Recovers an axisymmetric distribution f(r) from the projection A(y) (inverse Abel transform = tomography of an axisymmetric object). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `abel_inverse_image` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Turns an **image** of an axisymmetric object taken from the side (vertical = direction of the symmetry axis, horizontal = distance from the axis) into a cross-section image by applying the inverse Abel transform row by row. · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `abel_revolve` `image2d → voxel` GPU: none — Revolves a cross-section f(z, r) ((H, R), r = 0, dr, …) around the symmetry axis into a 3-D volume (H, 2R−1, 2R−1). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `abel_transform` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Maps an axisymmetric distribution f(r) (samples at r = 0, dr, 2dr, …) to its projection A(y) (forward Abel transform). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `dct_transform` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Orthonormal DCT-II (with ``inverse=True``, DCT-III = the inverse transform) in N dimensions. · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `dwt_inverse` `table → image2d` GPU: none — Restores the original array from the result of ``dwt_transform`` (being orthonormal, it is the transpose of the analysis). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `dwt_transform` `image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Multi-level, N-dimensional discrete wavelet transform with Daubechies dbN (exactly orthonormal with periodic boundaries). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `hankel_image` `image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Computes an axisymmetric image's 2-D Fourier transform with a radial Hankel transform. ``memory_budget`` selects a low-memory path measured within 1e-10. · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `hankel_transform` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Hankel transform of order p, F(ν) = 2π ∫_0^∞ f(r) J_p(2πνr) r dr, by the quasi-discrete method. · examples: `perf_hankel_plan_and_piv_stream`, `transforms_tour`
- `laplace_inverse_talbot` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Numerical inverse Laplace transform of a rational function F(s) = num(s)/den(s) (fixed Talbot method). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `tf_bilinear` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Maps a continuous-time system to a discrete-time system with the Tustin (bilinear) transform s = K (z − 1)/(z + 1). · examples: `gallery_math_numerics_filters`
- `tf_freq_response` `signal × signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Frequency response H(jω) (the content of a Bode plot). ω is in rad/s. The phase is in degrees, unwrapped to be continuous. · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `tf_impulse_response` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Impulse response h(t) = L⁻¹[H(s)] (t) (the strictly proper part; the delta of the direct feedthrough term is not returned). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `tf_poles_zeros` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Poles, zeros, DC gain and stability of H(s) = num/den. · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `tf_step_response` `signal × signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Unit step response y(t) = L⁻¹[H(s)/s] (t). · examples: `transforms_tour`
- `wavelet_filters` `no input → table` GPU: none — Builds the filters of the Daubechies orthonormal wavelet dbN by the textbook construction (spectral factorization). · examples: `gallery_math_numerics_filters`

- `wave_dominant_frequency` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Return the frequency, period and orientation of the strongest periodicity of an image (the largest non-DC 2-D FFT peak) (``table``). · examples: `wave_dominant_frequency_grating`
- `wave_fringe_period` `image2d → measurement` GPU: none — The period of a striped image, measured back out of it (pixels). · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`, `wave_dominant_frequency_grating`
- `wave_grating_orders` `no input → table` GPU: none — Where a grating sends each order: ``d (sin_out - sin_in) = m lambda`` solved for the angle. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`, `poc_spectrometer_illumination`
- `wave_membrane_mode` `no input → matrix` GPU: none — One eigenmode of a vibrating **membrane** — the shape the sand draws. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `wave_mode_frequencies` `no input → signal` GPU: none — The eigenvalue ladder of a membrane — a closed form you can check against. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `wave_nodal_lines` `matrix → mask` GPU: none — Where a signed field changes sign — the nodal set, as a mask. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`

### optics (504 ops / 55 categories)

The layer above the lens and below the pixel. Geometric optics (thin-lens imaging, ABCD ray transfer, depth of field, cos⁴ vignetting) / wave optics (Airy pattern, angular-spectrum propagation, Fraunhofer diffraction, Gaussian beams) / imaging quality (PSF→MTF, diffraction-limited MTF, Zernike wavefront statistics) / polarisation (Jones, Stokes, Mueller) / material property tables (matprop), optical fibres (fiber), sensor characteristics (sensorchar), global light transport and more.

#### optics / appearance (7)
- `cie_xyz_from_wavelength` `signal → points` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Wavelength [nm] → the CIE 1931 2° colour-matching functions (x̄, ȳ, z̄). Returns the input shape plus a trailing 3. · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`, `poc_chromatic_confocal`
- `grating_rgb` `normalmap → rgbimage` GPU: none — Normal map + light + view → the **rainbow colours of diffraction**, (H, W, 3) in linear sRGB. · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`
- `grating_wavelengths` `no input → vector` GPU: none — Solve the grating equation d(sinθ_out − sinθ_in) = mλ for λ. · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`, `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `spectrum_to_srgb` `signal → vector` GPU: none — Spectral reflectance → **linear sRGB** (before gamma). Normalised so a white surface (reflectance 1) becomes (1,1,1). · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`, `poc_material_optical_library`, `poc_pigment_unmixing`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `poc_white_balance`
- `thin_film_reflectance` `signal → signal` GPU: yes (allow-list) — The spectral reflectance of a thin film (thickness d, index n_film). The exact characteristic-matrix solution (all multiple reflections included). · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`, `simcal_tour`
- `thin_film_rgb` `normalmap → rgbimage` GPU: none — Normal map + view → the **colour of thin-film interference**, (H, W, 3) in linear sRGB. · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`
- `ward_anisotropic` `normalmap → image2d` GPU: none — Ward's anisotropic reflection (an elliptical-Gaussian microfacet). The **stretched highlight** of a hairline finish. · examples: `appearance_structural_colour`

- `pod_from_ahat` `table → table` GPU: none — From the â-vs-a regression and the decision threshold ``a_dec``: the POD(a) curve and a50 / a90 / a90/95 (``table``). · examples: `poc_equipment_selection_map`, `poc_pod_lighting`, `poc_sam_hybrid_bonding_voids`
- `pod_hitmiss_fit` `table → table` GPU: none — Fit POD(a) to binary found/missed data with a generalised linear model (``table``). · examples: `poc_pod_lighting`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`, `poc_si_wafer_pl_defect_visibility`

- `trials_for_all_success` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Return the minimum trial count needed for all successes to establish ``p >= p_min`` at one-sided ``confidence`` (``scalar``). · examples: `proportion_interval_audit`

### vx (10 ops / 5 categories)

#### vx / filter (1)
- `vx_nonlinear_filter` `image2d × matrix → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Nonlinear filter (Section 3.38): median / minimum (erosion) / maximum (dilation) of the values of the pixels where the mask is true (REQ-0325, 0330). · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`

#### vx / geometry (3)
- `vx_remap` `image2d × matrix × matrix → image2d` GPU: none — remap (Section 3.44): output (x, y) = input (map_x[y, x], map_y[y, x]) (REQ-0392). The tables have the shape of the output; in the coordinates, input pixel centers are at integers. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`
- `vx_warp_affine` `image2d × matrix → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Affine transform (Section 3.56). **Inverse mapping**: output pixel (x, y) is taken from input (x0, y0) (REQ-0498): ``x0 = M[0,0]·x + M[0,1]·y + M[0,2]``, ``y0 = M[1,0]·x + M[1,1]·y + M[1,2]``. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`
- `vx_warp_perspective` `image2d × matrix → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Perspective transform (Section 3.57). Inverse mapping: ``x0 = M[0]·(x, y, 1)``, ``y0 = M[1]·(x, y, 1)``, ``z0 = M[2]·(x, y, 1)``, output (x, y) = input (x0/z0, y0/z0) (REQ-0508). Pixels with z0 = 0 are filled as outside. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`

#### vx / gradient (3)
- `vx_magnitude` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Gradient magnitude (Section 3.31). The conceptual definition of REQ-0270 as is: ``z = uint16(sqrt(double(uint32(x·x) + uint32(y·y))) + 0.5)``, ``mag = z > 32767 ? 32767 : z``. Both input and output are S16. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `vx_phase` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Gradient phase (Section 3.41): shifts ϕ = atan2(gy, gx) into 0 ≤ ϕ < 2π and maps it to 0–255 (REQ-0364). Output U8. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`
- `vx_sobel3x3` `image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Sobel 3×3 (Section 3.46): applies G_x = [[−1,0,1],[−2,0,2],[−1,0,1]], G_y = [[−1,−2,−1],[0,0,0],[1,2,1]] (REQ-0415) as a correlation. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`, `type_connectivity_tour`

#### vx / pixel (2)
- `vx_histogram` `image2d → pairs` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Histogram (Section 3.26): a pixel value I goes into the bin ``i = (I − offset) × numBins / range`` (offset ≤ I < offset + range, REQ-0230). Pixels outside the range are not counted. The bin is determined by integer division (truncation). · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`
- `vx_table_lookup` `image2d × signal → image2d` GPU: none — Table lookup (Section 3.47): output = table[pixel value + offset] (REQ-0421). Accepts U8 and S16 (REQ-0422). The output dtype is the table's dtype. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`

#### vx / suppress (1)
- `vx_nonmax_suppression` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Non-maximum suppression (Section 3.39). A pixel (x, y) survives only if, within the window, it is **≥ its preceding neighbors (the row above and the left in the same row) and > its following neighbors** (REQ-0337). This asymmetry is why exactly 1 pixel survives on a flat peak. Nonzero pixels of *mask* are not compared and are kept as is (nor are they used in comparisons for other pixels, REQ-0336). Suppressed pixels become 0 for U8 and INT16_MIN for S16 (REQ-0335). Neighbors that fall outside the window are not compared. · examples: `gallery_openvx_spec_values`

### drive (741 ops / 55 categories)

The name says driving, but the content is a **ledger of physics-simulation and robot PoCs**: besides driving (courses, traffic, decisions, CARLA / CommonRoad), categories such as touch (tac*), peg-in-hole (peg*), polishing (polish), grinding (grind), cutting (cutting), granular media (granular / scoop), powder X-ray diffraction (pxrd) and ball games (ball / puck) live side by side. Look things up by category name.

#### drive / agv (13)
- `adg_build` `table → table` GPU: none — Action dependency graph (Hönig, Kiesel, Tinka, Durham, Ayanian 2019). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `adg_execute` `table → table` GPU: none — Executes according to the ADG. At each time step, each vehicle stops with probability ``delay_prob`` (slipping, people, delays in loading). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `grid_distances` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Shortest number of moves on the grid to ``goal`` (BFS; obstacles are impassable). Unreachable cells are ``inf``. · examples: `gallery_drive_city_terrain`, `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `mapf_cbs` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Conflict-Based Search (Sharon, Stern, Felner, Sturtevant 2015). A collision-free plan with optimal sum of costs. · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`, `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `mapf_ecbs` `image2d → table` GPU: none — CBS with focal search at the high level (the same idea as the high level of ECBS, Barer et al. 2014). Sum of costs is **within w times the optimum**. · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `mapf_joint_astar` `image2d → table` GPU: none — A* with the positions of all vehicles as 1 single state. Optimal solution **for small problems only** (the ground truth for the CBS gate). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `mapf_prioritized` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Prioritized planning: plans 1 vehicle at a time in order, avoiding the paths of vehicles already decided (reservation table). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`, `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `naive_execute` `table → table` GPU: none — Naive execution for comparison: uses only the plan's **sequence of cells** and advances whenever the next cell is free (no ordering agreement). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `plan_conflicts` `table → table` GPU: none — List of conflicts: same cell at the same time (vertex), passing each other (edge), following (follow). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`, `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `plan_cost` `table → scalar` GPU: none — Sum of costs: the sum over vehicles of the time each **finally** arrives at its goal (it must not move after arriving). · examples: `gallery_drive_city_terrain`, `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `vda5050_check` `table → table` GPU: none — Checks the **structural rules** of a VDA 5050 order (our own second (independent) implementation, separate from the official JSON schema). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `vda5050_order` `table → table` GPU: none — Turns the plan of 1 vehicle (sequence of cells) into a VDA 5050 order (dict). Waits are removed, and the cell centers become nodes. · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`
- `warehouse_grid` `no input → any` GPU: none — Warehouse grid made of shelf rows and aisles (True = drivable). · examples: `poc_agv_fleet`

#### drive / ball (32)
- `aic_from_rss` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Akaike information criterion from a least-squares residual sum of squares: AIC = n ln(RSS/n) + 2k (Gaussian noise, variance estimated by maximum likelihood, constant term dropped). Only **differences** between models fitted to the same data are meaningful (the absolute value depends on scale and n). n ≤ k, RSS ≤ 0 and non-finite values raise ValueError (RSS = 0 is AIC = −∞ and the model-selection question does not arise). · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `apex_sequence` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Apex heights h_k = e^{2k} h₀ (k = 0..n) of a drop-and-bounce sequence. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `ball_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Ball table. The default is a table tennis ball (ITTF: diameter 40 mm, 2.7 g, thin shell). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`, `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_rally_loop`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`, `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `ballistic_vs_thrust` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — Fits both "gravity + drag" (:func:`drag_fit`) and "gravity + drag + constant specific thrust" (:func:`thrust_fit`) to the same trajectory and returns the AIC difference (:func:`aic_from_rss`) ΔAIC = AIC_ballistic − AIC_thrust. Returns ``{"ballistic", "thrust"}`` (the two fits) plus ``"aic_ballistic", "aic_thrust", "delta_aic", "thrust_norm"``. **No verdict is returned** (the :mod:`imgforensics` convention): read it by **parsimony** — the thrust model has 3 more parameters and lowers RSS slightly even on pure noise, so unless it wins by more than the penalty 2Δk the simpler (ballistic) model is kept. Noise-only ΔAIC scatters with **−2Δk as its lower bound** and roughly a χ²(Δk) width (median about −2Δk + 1; strictly a mixture, since some fits hit the wall C_d = 0), and because the thrust fit starts from the ballistic solution ΔAIC ≥ −2Δk holds. The customary "decisive" value is 10 (false positives well below 1 %), but no threshold is bundled; the caller decides. When the thrust fit's RSS is below 10× the discretisation floor ``rss_floor`` (a noise-free track, or one resolved finer than the grid) it raises ValueError — AIC compares noise, not rounding (the noise-free truth gave ΔAIC = +144 at the default dt, 2026-10-23). · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `bounce` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Update of velocity and angular velocity at the instant a rigid sphere hits a plane (Coulomb friction, the 2 regimes of Cross 2002 / Garwin 1969). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`, `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`
- `bounce_total_time` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Total time from dropping from height h₀ until coming to rest = √(2h₀/g)·(1 + e)/(1 − e) (closed form of a geometric series, e < 1). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `contact_angular_momentum` `table → signal` GPU: none — Angular momentum about the contact point L_c = I ω + m (p − p_c) × v = I ω + m r (n × v). Invariant across the bounce (theorem). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `cup_catch_check` `no input → table` GPU: none — Geometric test of whether the ball enters a cup (center, axis, radius): the ball's center lies within (cup_radius − ball_radius) of the cup axis, at a height within 1.5 times the ball radius from the cup surface (0 ≤ height ≤ 1.5 r), and the speed is ≤ v_rel_max. ``{"caught", "lateral", "height", "speed"}``. ValueError if the cup is smaller than the ball. · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `drag_coefficient_sphere` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Empirical formula for the drag coefficient of a smooth sphere (Morrison 2013, Re ≲ 1e6): 24/Re + 2.6(Re/5)/(1 + (Re/5)^1.52) + 0.411(Re/263000)^−7.94/(1 + (Re/263000)^−8) + 0.25(Re/1e6)/(1 + Re/1e6). ≈ 0.4–0.5 for a table tennis ball (Re ≈ 1–5 × 10⁴). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `drag_fit` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — Fits the "gravity + drag" model to a trajectory (t_i, p_i) with **7 parameters (p₀, v₀, C_d)** (5 for planar input) — the no-thrust version of :func:`thrust_fit` (:func:`flight_fit` keeps C_d known with 6 parameters; this one identifies C_d too). The result keys and the entrance checks (``dt`` ≤ sample spacing, ``iters`` ≥ 1, vacuum refused) are those of :func:`thrust_fit`, with ``thrust`` a zero vector. From a ground-truth trajectory C_d returns to 1e-4 (gate). · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `fit_aero` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — Identifies **the aerodynamic coefficients as well** from a trajectory: the 8 parameters (p₀, v₀, C_d, C_L) by Gauss–Newton (ω known, C_L fitted as a constant). Drag goes with the 2nd power of speed and Magnus with ω × v, so C_L is hard to determine unless the trajectory is non-straight (with spin, long enough) (``cond`` = condition number of the Jacobian is returned together with ``rms``, so you can tell). Return value ``{"p0", "v0", "cd", "cl", "rms", "cond", "iters"}``. For a ground-truth trajectory (made with constant C_L) it recovers to 1e-6 (gate). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `fit_bounce` `table → table` GPU: none — Recovers (e, μ) in closed form from (v, ω) before and after a bounce (identification). e = −v_n'/v_n. μ is the ratio of the magnitude of the tangential impulse J_t = m(v_t' − v_t) to J_n = m(v_n' − v_n) — an equality in the regime that keeps sliding, a **lower bound** (μ ≥ |J_t|/J_n) in the regime that switches to rolling partway (grip). Which one applies is told by whether the slip velocity of the contact point after the bounce is 0 (grip). Return value ``{"e", "mu", "mu_is_lower_bound", "regime", "J_n", "J_t"}``. · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `fit_parabola` `signal × points → table` GPU: none — Least-squares fit of p = p₀ + v₀ t − ½ g t² ẑ to observations (t_i, p_i) (linear, closed form). ``{"p0", "v0", "g", "rms"}``. Recovers vacuum ground truth to 1e-9 (gate). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `fit_spin` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — **Reads the spin from how the ball curves**: fits the equations of motion with drag + Magnus to a trajectory (t_i, p_i) (an interval without bounces) with the 9 parameters (p₀, v₀, ω) by Gauss–Newton (the aerodynamic coefficients are the values in ``bp`` = assumed known). · examples: `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `flight_fit` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — Fits the equations of motion with drag + Magnus (ω known) to observations (t_i, p_i) (an interval without bounces) with **the 6 parameters of the initial state (p₀, v₀)** by Gauss–Newton (finite-difference Jacobian). A parabola fit absorbs drag and Magnus into g and v₀, so its prediction bends — this one corresponds to the "tracking with an aerodynamic model" of prior work. Return value ``{"p0", "v0", "rms", "iters", "t0"}`` (p₀ and v₀ are the state at t = t[0]). Given a ground-truth trajectory it recovers it to 1e-9 (gate). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`
- `flight_ode` `table → table` GPU: none — RK4 for gravity + drag + Magnus (+ spin decay). Return value ``{"t" (N,), "p" (N, 3), "v" (N, 3), "omega" (N, 3)}`` (t = 0, dt, …, ≤ t_end). In vacuum (rho = 0) it matches :func:`flight_vacuum` (gate). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`, `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`, `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `flight_simulate` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Joins flight and bounces on the table (the plane z = table_z, only within ``table_xy`` = (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)), locating each contact time within its interval by bisection. Return value ``{"t", "p", "v", "omega" (N, 3), "contacts": [{"t", "p", "v_in", "v_out", "omega_in", "omega_out", "regime"}], "rest_t"}``. The ball has radius r, so contact occurs where the center reaches table_z + r. Bounces go on forever (Zeno), so once |v_n| at contact < ``v_rest``, the ball is set down on the table (from then on z is fixed and horizontal motion continues without friction; ``rest_t`` = that time, or None if it never happens). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_rally_loop`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `flight_state_at` `table → table` GPU: none — Advances the state (p₀, v₀, ω) by T seconds with the equations of motion (if T < 0, it **rewinds**: the RK4 step is made negative). ``{"p", "v", "omega"}``. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`
- `flight_vacuum` `signal → points` GPU: none — Parabola in vacuum (closed form): p(t) = p₀ + v₀ t − ½ g t² ẑ. ``t`` is a scalar or (N,); the return value is (3,) or (N, 3). · examples: `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `poc_ball_bounce`
- `impact_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Impact table: normal coefficient of restitution e ∈ [0, 1] (a number, or a function |v_n| → e, to match measurements in which it decreases with impact speed) and Coulomb friction coefficient μ ≥ 0. · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`, `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_rally_loop`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `incline_slip_angle` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Angle θ = atan μ [rad] at which an object starts to slide on an incline with static friction coefficient μ. · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `magnus_lift_coefficient` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Lift coefficient C_L = 1 / (2 + 1/S) from the spin ratio S = rω/|v| (0 as S → 0, 0.5 as S → ∞; an empirical formula widely used in the ball literature). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `mu_from_stop_distance` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — μ = v₀² / (2 g d) from the stopping distance. · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `pendulum_period` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Period of a small-amplitude pendulum 2π√(L/g). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `restitution_from_apexes` `signal → table` GPU: none — Estimates e from a sequence of apex heights (≥ 2, positive): log h_k is linear in k with slope 2 log e → least squares. ``{"e", "h0", "residual"}``. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `restitution_from_intervals` `signal → table` GPU: none — Estimates e from a sequence of contact times (≥ 3, increasing): intervals T_{k+1} = e T_k → the slope of log T_k is log e. ``{"e", "residual"}``. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `roll_slide_state` `table → table` GPU: none — Whether a sphere on a plane is rolling or sliding: slip velocity of the contact point s = v_t − r(ω × n). ``{"slip_speed", "rolling"}`` (rolling if |s| < 1e-9). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`
- `slide_stop_distance` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Stopping distance of an object sliding on a horizontal plane with initial speed v₀ = v₀² / (2μg) (μ > 0). · examples: `gallery_drive_ballistics`, `poc_air_hockey_intercept`
- `tether_simulate` `no input → table` GPU: none — Motion of a point mass tied to the hand ``handle`` by an inextensible string (length L) (the kendama ball). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `thrust_fit` `signal × points × table → table` GPU: none — Fits the "gravity + drag + constant specific thrust" model to a trajectory (t_i, p_i) with **10 parameters (p₀, v₀, C_d, a_T)** by Levenberg–Marquardt (finite-difference Jacobian, C_d ≥ 0 kept by projection). ``p`` is either (N, 3) world points or the **(N, 2) planar (x, z)** track lifted from a monocular side view (then the y component has neither observation nor unknown: 7 parameters, ``n`` = 2 × samples). ``bp`` is a :func:`ball_params` table (mass, frontal area, air density, g; ``radius`` is used only to give the frontal area — for a car pass the r whose A = πr² is the frontal area). Returns ``{"p0", "v0", "cd", "thrust" (3,), "thrust_norm", "rms", "rss", "rss_floor", "n", "k", "dims", "cond", "iters", "t0"}`` (``n`` = number of residuals, ``k`` = number of parameters moved; the inputs of :func:`aic_from_rss`). From a thrusted ground-truth trajectory a_T returns to 1e-5 m/s²; from a trajectory made with zero thrust ``thrust_norm`` is 1e-5 or less (gate). ``rss_floor`` is the upper bound of the sum of squares that the error ≤ a dt²/8 of linearly interpolating the RK4 grid onto the sample times can leave in the residuals. ``dt`` must not exceed the sample spacing (beyond it the model is piecewise linear between samples), ``iters`` must be ≥ 1, and in vacuum (rho = 0) C_d cannot be identified — each is a ValueError. · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `thrust_ode` `table → table` GPU: none — RK4 for gravity + drag + a **constant specific thrust** (thrust per unit mass [m/s²], fixed in direction and magnitude in world coordinates). No spin (ω = 0). Returns ``{"t" (N,), "p" (N, 3), "v" (N, 3)}`` (t = 0, dt, …, ≤ t_end). With a zero ``thrust`` it matches :func:`flight_ode` (ω = 0) to 1e-12, and in vacuum (rho = 0) it matches the closed form p₀ + v₀ t + ½ (a_T − g ẑ) t² to 1e-9 (gate). The smallest model for "almost a rocket" footage; a thrust fixed to the body that turns with it is only approximated (the shorter the segment, the better). ``t_end`` / ``dt`` must be finite numbers, ``bp`` the table from :func:`ball_params` (a missing key, a non-finite value or zero mass is a ValueError), and the step count t_end / dt is capped at 5×10⁶ (this stops a t passed in ms instead of seconds). · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`
- `time_stretch_from_gravity` `no input → table` GPU: none — Inverts, in closed form, the time-stretch factor of a video from the fitted gravitational acceleration. In footage whose time axis was stretched by k (slow motion or a relabelled frame rate) the trajectory keeps its shape while g appears as g/k², so k = √(g_ref / g_fit). Returns ``{"k", "g_fit", "g_ref", "log_k"}`` (``log_k`` = ln k is 0 without tampering and its sign tells faster/slower; when passing to :func:`imgforensics.evidence_quantile` use |log_k| as the "larger is stronger" evidence). g_fit ≤ 0, non-finite values and g_ref ≤ 0 raise ValueError (no stretch factor is defined for a trajectory whose gravity points up or is absent). · examples: `poc_video_physics_consistency`

#### drive / balltrack (10)
- `ball_detect` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Extracts ball candidates from an image: threshold → connected components → brightness-weighted subpixel centroid, equivalent radius, fill fraction. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_driving_longitudinal`, `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_weather`, `poc_kendama`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `ball_track` `table → table` GPU: none — Links the per-frame candidate lists ``detections[k] = ball_detect(frame_k)`` into 1 trajectory (the candidate closest to the constant-velocity prediction, within ``max_jump`` px). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `bounce_detect` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Extracts contact candidates from a height sequence z(t): local minima where the downward velocity turns upward (minimum over ``min_gap`` samples before and after). Return value ``{"index" (M,), "t" (M,), "z" (M,)}``. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `kalman_ca` `points → table` GPU: none — Kalman filter with a constant-acceleration model (position observations (N, D); state = position, velocity, acceleration × D). · examples: `poc_air_hockey_intercept`, `poc_ball_bounce`
- `marker_direction` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Position of a marker in the image (col, row) → direction on the sphere (unit vector in the camera frame, front hemisphere: x right, y up, z toward the viewer). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `reproject` `points × matrix × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — World points (N, 3) → (col, row) as (N, 2) (NaN where depth ≤ 0). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_kendama`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `spin_from_marker_sequence` `any → table` GPU: none — Reads the angular velocity from the marker directions ``dirs[k]`` over a sequence of frames ((M_k, 3) unit vectors; None for frames where none is found) (2 stages). · examples: `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `spin_from_markers` `points × points → table` GPU: none — Angular velocity vector ω [rad/s] from pairs of marker directions (before (M, 3), after (M, 3), unit vectors). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `track_triangulate` `table × any × any → table` GPU: none — Triangulates the per-camera trajectories (return values of :func:`ball_track`) into a 3-D trajectory: ``{"frame", "p" (N, 3), "reproj_rms" (N,)}`` (only frames seen in 2 or more views). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `triangulate_dlt` `matrix × any × any → table` GPU: none — Multi-view triangulation of 1 point (linear DLT, SVD): ``uvs`` (C, 2), ``poses`` (C, 4, 4), ``Ks`` (C, 3, 3). Return value ``{"p" (3,), "reproj_rms" px, "n_views"}``. Views with NaN are skipped. ValueError if there are fewer than 2 views. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_kendama`

#### drive / ballworld (9)
- `add_ball` `table × table → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a ball to the world at pose (p, R). The per-face labels (ball 23 / marker 24) are kept as is. Return value = index into objects. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `ball_mesh` `no input → table` GPU: none — Ball mesh (origin = center) and markers. ``markers`` = [(dir, angle_deg), …] gives multiple markers (if None, 1 marker at marker_dir). Return value ``{"V", "F", "color" (M,3), "label" (M,) (23 or 24), "radius", "markers": [unit vector …]}``. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `ball_set_pose` `table × matrix → any` GPU: none — Sets the pose of ball i to (p, R) (rewrites only the vertices). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `ball_truth` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Ground-truth projection of ball i: (col, row) of the center, image radius [px] (≈ f·r/depth), (col, row) of the marker center (NaN if on the back side). · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`
- `camera_rig` `table → table` GPU: none — Cameras surrounding the platform (n = 2: diagonally above both ends, n = 4: 4 corners). Returns ``[{"pose", "K", "eye", "width", "height"}, …]``, all looking at the center of the platform. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `icosphere` `no input → any` GPU: none — Mesh (V, F) (outward) obtained by subdividing a regular icosahedron (20 faces) 4-way ``subdiv`` times and projecting it onto the sphere. · examples: `gallery_mesh_seg_sun_gains`
- `rotation_from_omega` `no input → matrix` GPU: none — Rotation matrix for rotating at angular velocity ω [rad/s] for dt seconds (Rodrigues). R_{k+1} = R(ω dt) R_k. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `table_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Table tennis table parameters (default = ITTF standard). · examples: `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_rally_loop`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`
- `table_world` `table → table` GPU: none — World of the table (top + white lines + net) and the floor. Origin = center of the tabletop, x = length (±1.37), y = width (±0.7625), z up. The top surface of the tabletop is at z = height. · examples: `poc_ball_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_table_tennis_spin`

#### drive / braidpath (12)
- `braid_artin_images` `signal × scalar → table` GPU: none — Artin representation of a braid: images (freely reduced words) of the generators x₁..xₙ of the free group F_n.
- `braid_class_representatives` `any → table` GPU: none — Partitions several plans (output of any planner) into homotopy classes and picks the lowest-cost plan in each class as its representative. · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `braid_equivalent` `signal × signal × scalar → table` GPU: none — Whether two braid words represent the same braid (are related by the relations alone). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `braid_from_trajectories` `any → table` GPU: none — Builds a braid word (a sequence of crossing signs) from planar trajectories (and stationary obstacle points). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `braid_reduce` `signal × scalar → signal` GPU: none — Reduces a braid word by Dehornoy handle reduction. **Returns the empty word ⇔ the braid is trivial** (same class). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `dynnikov_act` `any × signal → table` GPU: none — Applies a braid word to arbitrary Dynnikov coordinates (a; b) (integer or real —— the formulas are piecewise linear). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `dynnikov_coordinates` `signal × scalar → table` GPU: none — Dynnikov coordinates of the braid acting on the standard curve diagram E = (0, …, 0; −1, …, −1) (integers, no overflow). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `grid_hole_points` `image2d → matrix` GPU: none — One representative point per grid hole (connected component of blocked cells not touching the border): the centre [x, y] of the blocked cell nearest the centroid. · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `grid_paths_to_xy` `any → any` GPU: none — Converts grid paths (each agent's (row, col) sequence) into (K, T, 2) [x, y] = [col, −row] (shorter paths are padded with their last point). · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `homotopy_class_compare` `any × any → table` GPU: none — Whether two path families with the same start and end points (multi-agent plans) are in the same homotopy class. · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `homotopy_shortest_paths` `image2d × any × any → table` GPU: none — On a grid (True = traversable, 4-neighbourhood), the k shortest paths from start to goal in distinct homotopy classes, shortest first. · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`
- `pairwise_winding` `any → matrix` GPU: none — Relative winding number for each pair of strands [turns] (total change of the argument of the relative vector / 2π). Symmetric matrix, zero diagonal. · examples: `poc_braid_homotopy_classes`

#### drive / carla (25)
- `camera_pose_to_carla` `matrix → any` GPU: none — render3d world → camera 4×4 → CARLA camera [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw]. Inverse of :func:`carla_camera_pose`. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_camera_pose` `any → matrix` GPU: none — World pose of a CARLA camera → render3d / driveworld **world → camera** 4×4 (same type as :func:`driveworld.camera_pose`). A CARLA camera looks along local +x with right = +y and up = +z; render3d looks along −z with right = +x and up = +y. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_depth_decode` `rgb → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Raw image of the CARLA depth camera (24 bit: R low, G, B high) → distance from the image plane [m]. d = code / (2²⁴ − 1) · 1000. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_depth_encode` `image2d → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Distance from the image plane [m] → CARLA raw depth image (uint8 (H,W,3)). inf and values above 1000 m map to the maximum; negative values and NaN raise ValueError. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_intrinsics` `no input → matrix` GPU: none — K of a CARLA camera (**horizontal** field of view fov, f = W / (2 tan(fov/2)), principal point (W/2, H/2)). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_label_map` `image2d → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — CARLA semantic segmentation (uint8 image of tags) → Fullseye label image (int, −1 = empty/unlabeled). Unknown tags raise ValueError. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_label_unmap` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Fullseye label image → CARLA tag image (uint8, representative tag). Inverse of :func:`carla_label_map` (identity on the label side). · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_labels` `no input → table` GPU: none — Table of CARLA 0.9.16 semantic tags: ``[{"tag", "carla", "label", "fullseye"}, …]`` (29 rows, in tag order). · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_pose_to_world` `any → matrix` GPU: none — CARLA [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw] → Fullseye 4×4 (world ← object, right-handed: the signs of y and yaw are flipped). R_f = M R_c M, t_f = M t_c (M = diag(1, −1, 1)). The object's local frame is x forward, y left, z up (same as the cars in driveworld). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_rotation_angles` `matrix → any` GPU: none — 3×3 (CARLA's formula) → (roll, pitch, yaw) [deg]. pitch = asin(R₂₀), yaw = atan2(R₁₀, R₀₀), roll = atan2(−R₂₁, R₂₂). The degenerate case |pitch| = 90° raises ValueError. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_rotation_matrix` `no input → matrix` GPU: none — CARLA / UE4 (roll, pitch, yaw) [deg] → 3×3 (the same formula as the rotation part of ``carla.Transform.get_matrix()``, kept left-handed). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_check` `table → table` GPU: none — Checks the keys, shapes and dtypes of a scene record and returns a summary (ValueError if it does not pass). Return value = ``{"width", "height", "has_lead", "has_instance", "meta"(dict), "n_tags"}``. · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_load` `any → table` GPU: none — Reads a scene record (npz) → dict (``meta`` becomes a dict; ``depth`` [m] is decoded and added). Missing or corrupted items raise ValueError. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_render` `table → table` GPU: none — Re-shoots a scene record in our own world (same K, same mounting height, same field of view) → driveworld.world_camera images (``color`` / ``label`` / ``depth`` …) + ``pose`` + ``K``. The counterpart for viewing **side by side** with the CARLA image. · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_save` `table → any` GPU: none — Writes a scene record to npz (after validating it). Returns the path written. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_synthetic` `no input → table` GPU: none — Turns our own world (straight road + lead vehicle) into a **scene record in CARLA conventions** (same keys and types as a captured recording). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`, `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_scene_world` `table → table` GPU: none — Scene record → our own world (straight road + lead vehicle placed at the recorded pose). Keeping the relative placement of camera and lead vehicle, normalizes the camera to (20, 0) facing +x (CARLA map coordinates are not used). Without a lead vehicle, only the road. · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `carla_transform_matrix` `any → matrix` GPU: none — CARLA [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw] → 4×4 (world ← object, kept in CARLA coordinates) = ``Transform.get_matrix()``. · examples: `poc_carla_bridge`
- `carla_xy_yaw` `any → any` GPU: none — CARLA pose → carpath / driveworld (x, y, yaw) (flips the signs of y and yaw; yaw in radians). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `intrinsics_to_carla` `matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Inverse of :func:`intrinsics_to_fullseye` (shifts the principal point back by 0.5). · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`
- `intrinsics_to_fullseye` `matrix → matrix` GPU: none — CARLA K (pixel corners at integers, principal point W/2) → Fullseye / render3d K (pixel centers at integers, principal point (W−1)/2). Just shifts the principal point by 0.5. · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`, `poc_carla_bridge`
- `lead_from_depth` `image2d × image2d × matrix → table` GPU: none — Rule-based distance to the lead vehicle (same formula for both worlds): ``depth_median`` = median depth of the car pixels in the central band of the image (width band × W) (constant, since the rear face is parallel to the image plane), ``row_distance`` = horizontal distance from the car's bottom row via the flat-road formula (driveenv.road_row_distance), ``bbox`` = (top, bottom, left, right), ``n_pixels``, ``found``. - `scene_pair_table` `table → table` GPU: none — Score and line up one scene recording with both **CARLA's image** and **your own world image**.
