- `world_pose_to_carla` `matrix → any` GPU: none — Fullseye 4×4 (world ← object) → CARLA [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw]. Inverse of :func:`carla_pose_to_world`. · examples: `gallery_drive_carla_bridge`

#### drive / commonroad (10)
- `cr_checker_result` `any → table` GPU: none — Reads the JSON written by the official checker under WSL (tools/check_solution_json.py). · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_collision` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Collision with obstacles (rectangle-vs-rectangle SAT, per time_step) and road boundary (whether the vehicle's 4 corners lie inside the union of the lanelet polygons). · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_drive` `table → table` GPU: none — Runs our own driver (longitudinal IDM + pure pursuit) on a CommonRoad planning problem. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_drive_sweep` `table → table` GPU: none — Rule-based gap acceptance: tries a grid of driver parameters in order, gentlest first, and returns **the first run that passes all gates**. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_feasible` `table → table` GPU: none — Kinematic feasibility (a second (independent) implementation of the same idea as the grader's ``solution_feasible``). · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_read` `any → table` GPU: none — Reads CommonRoad 2020a XML (a string or a path). · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_route` `table → table` GPU: none — Produces a sequence of lanelets by BFS over successors (fewest hops), chains their centerlines and resamples every ``step`` m. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_solution_xml` `table × table → any` GPU: none — Returns the official solution XML (same form as commonroad-io ``CommonRoadSolutionWriter``) as a string. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `cr_synthetic` `no input → any` GPU: none — Returns, as a string, a minimal CommonRoad 2020a XML for tests and CI. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`
- `ks_step` `any × any → any` GPU: none — Advances the kinematic single-track (KS) model by dt with RK4 under a piecewise-constant input u = (δ̇, a). Reference point = center of the rear axle. · examples: `poc_driving_commonroad`

#### drive / course (13)
- `course_contains` `table × points → signal` GPU: none — Bool array telling, by the even-odd rule, whether points lie inside the **drivable area** (the element's polygon, or the union of the elements for a layout). · examples: `poc_driving_school`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `course_crank` `no input → table` GPU: none — Crank course (Z-shaped): entry → left 90° → B → right 90° → exit. · examples: `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_town`
- `course_crossing` `no input → table` GPU: none — Railroad crossing: a track crosses a road of width w (along the x axis) at a right angle. Straights of length ``approach`` lie on both sides of the crossing surface (gauge + 2 outer rail strips = 2.6 m). ``rails`` (2, 2, 2) are the segments of the 2 rails (x = L/2 ± gauge/2, across the full road width), ``crossing_zone`` = (x0, x1) is the crossing surface, ``stop_lines`` (1, 2, 2) lies in the left lane ``stop_setback`` before the crossing surface. The polygon is a rectangle (the rails are metadata). Standard: gauge 1.1, outer rail strip 0.75 → ``params["regulation"]``. Area = w·(2(rail_outer + gauge/2) + 2·approach). · examples: `poc_driving_school`
- `course_intersection` `no input → table` GPU: none — Four-way intersection on the main course: 2 roads of width w cross at right angles at the origin, each arm has length ``arm`` (from the edge of the crossing area), and the 4 concave corners are rounded off with radius ``corner_radius``. · examples: `poc_driving_longitudinal`, `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_weather`
- `course_layout` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Places multiple elements by rigid motions ``(x, y, yaw)`` and combines them into 1 dict. · examples: `poc_driving_longitudinal`, `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_weather`, `poc_ttc_rss`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `course_loop` `no input → table` GPU: none — Loop course (oval): returns ``{"elements": [...], "placements": [...]}`` with 2 straights + 2 semicircles placed around the origin (pass it as is to :func:`course_layout`). Counterclockwise: south straight (eastbound, y = −R) → east semicircle → north straight (westbound, y = +R) → west semicircle. The straights overlap the semicircles by ``overlap`` at both ends (an overlap so that no curb rises at the seams when converted to 3-D; the sum of the areas counts that part twice). Standard (ordinary license): a straight driving section of 80 m or more, width 8 m or more. · examples: `poc_driving_school`, `poc_ttc_rss`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `course_loop_bend` `no input → table` GPU: none — Semicircle at the end of the loop course (turning 180° to the left): entry (0, 0, 0) → around the center (0, R) → exit (0, 2R, π). The polygon is the half annulus bounded by the outer arc (radius R + w/2) and the inner arc (R − w/2). Area = π R w (closed form); the polygon is smaller by the amount lost to approximating the arcs with polylines and converges as arc_pts increases. Standard (loop course): width 8 m or more, roughly oval. · examples: `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_town`
- `course_occupancy` `table → image2d` GPU: none — Rasterizes a course (element or layout) into an occupancy grid ``(occ bool [row = y, col = x], extent)``. · examples: `poc_driving_school`
- `course_parallel_parking` `no input → table` GPU: none — Parallel parking: a parking bay of length car_length + extra (default 7.5 m) × width car_width at the roadside of a road of width ``road_width`` (x ∈ [0, 2·approach + bay_length]). **No figures in the statutes (the attachment to the official notice is a drawing)** — the default is a customary value. · examples: `poc_driving_school`
- `course_road` `no input → table` GPU: none — Connector road (part of the main course): a straight of width w and length L. An element for leading the exit of a task course back to the loop course or for extending the main course. Standard (main course): width 7 m or more, must connect to the loop course. Area = w·L. · examples: `gallery_drive_city_terrain`, `gallery_drive_japan_roads`, `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_driving_longitudinal`, `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_town`, `poc_driving_weather`
- `course_s_curve` `no input → table` GPU: none — Curved course (S-shaped): straight E → left arc (central angle 2π·f) → right arc (same) → straight E. · examples: `poc_driving_school`, `poc_driving_town`
- `course_slope` `no input → table` GPU: none — Slope course: a rectangular road (along the x axis) that climbs a gentle slope to height ``height``, has a flat top section ``top``, and descends a steep slope. · examples: `poc_driving_longitudinal`, `poc_driving_school`
- `course_turnaround` `no input → table` GPU: none — Turnaround course (T-shaped): a parking bay (width bay_width along the road, depth depth) at the middle of one side of a road of width w (x ∈ [0, 2E + bay_width]), with an entrance/exit section E on each side of the bay mouth. · examples: `poc_driving_school`

The stick tips are mocap (positions written each step). The diabolo is a free-joint rigid body (mass = Table I of the paper, inertia assumed; rotation is not coupled to the string). If ``wrap_axle`` = True, the tendon wraps around the axle cylinder (radius r) (passing underneath, unverified). **Raises** ``ValueError``: params shape, timestep ≤ 0, solref is not 2 positive numbers. · examples: `poc_diabolo_model_and_vision`

- `discharge_synth` `scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Synthesizes a sequence of heightmaps in which powder falling from a circular orifice ``D0`` at the Beverloo rate piles up below into a cone with angle of repose φ. · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`

- `heap_scene_mjcf` `scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — MJCF string of a scene with rigid spheres stacked in a flat-bottomed hopper (square orifice, side ``orifice_d``) (**no mujoco needed**, listed in the ledger). · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`

- `heap_synth_cone` `scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Synthesizes a conical heap with a known angle of repose (side image = anti-aliased coverage, heightmap = height at cell centers). · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`
- `heap_volume_cone` `scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Closed form for a conical heap — given **exactly 2** of ``R``, ``H``, ``phi_deg``, returns the remaining one and the volume. · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`, `poc_powder_scoop_pour`
- `heap_volume_heightmap` `image2d × scalar → scalar` GPU: none — Heap volume from a heightmap ``Σ (z − z_ground) pitch²`` [m³]. ``ground`` is the ground height with the same shape (None = 0). - `hopper_discharge_rate` `signal × signal × scalar → table` GPU: none — Discharge rate [kg/s] from the series ``m(t)`` of mass below the floor plate — fits a line only to the band from ``lo`` to ``hi`` of the total mass (excluding start-up and the final stop; Beverloo's steady-flow assumption). - `repose_angle_heightmap` `image2d × scalar → table` GPU: none — Angle of repose φ from a heightmap — mode of the histogram of ``demops.dem_slope`` gradients. · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`

- `spoon_tilt_critical` `scalar × scalar × scalar → scalar` GPU: none — Tilt θ_c [deg] at which powder starts to spill from a spoon (2-D cross-section, quasi-static, no wall friction — **own derivation**). · examples: `poc_granular_heap_repose`

- `catch_success_rate` `table → table` GPU: none — Success rate on the big cup: scatters the initial state n times (the ball hangs L below the pivot (the string hole of the cross-piece), with Gaussian perturbations σ = jitter_pos sideways and σ = jitter_vel on the velocity (tangential component)), swings up with :func:`swing_up_plan` (hand starting point ``origin``), and carries the cup with :func:`catch_plan_ballistic`. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `elliptic_k_agm` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Complete elliptic integral of the first kind K(k) = ∫₀^{π/2} dφ / √(1 − k² sin² φ) via the arithmetic-geometric mean: K(k) = π / (2·AGM(1, √(1 − k²))). |k| < 1 (otherwise ValueError). - `hole_detect` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Finds the dark disc (the ken-tip hole) in the ball's image: inside the circle with ball center ``ball_center`` (col, row) and image radius ``ball_radius`` [px], the largest connected component of pixels whose brightness (mean of RGB) is below ``dark_ratio`` times the median ball brightness, whose saturation (max − min)/max ≥ ``min_sat`` (excludes the gray string), and whose chromaticity (RGB / |RGB|) lies at least ``min_chroma`` away from the median chromaticity of the ball (a shaded ball surface only loses brightness while its chromaticity stays the same — picking by brightness alone mistook shadows for the hole; measured and rejected). Returns ``{"found", "col", "row", "angle" (image angle from the ball center → hole centroid [rad], atan2(Δrow, Δcol)), "offset" (distance / ball_radius: 0 = facing, → 1 = rim), "ellipticity" (minor axis / major axis, from second moments: 1 = a circle seen head-on, → 0 = edge-on), "area" [px]}``. If nothing is found, found is False, area is 0, and the rest are NaN. Seen head-on, the hole center coincides with the ball center; the further it turns sideways, the closer it moves to the rim and the more it flattens (offset ≈ sin φ, ellipticity ≈ cos φ, φ = angle between the hole axis and the line of sight). ValueError unless img is (H, W, 3) and ball_radius > 0. · examples: `poc_kendama`

Hand ``hand0`` = center of the cross-piece (switching grip only turns the wrist; no regrip: assumption). The first cup is caught via the swing-up of :func:`kendama_simulate`, and that hand's position and velocity are passed as ``hand0`` / ``hand_v0``. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `kendama_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Kendama table. Default = ``preset="jka_16_2"`` (ball 60 mm, width 70 mm and overall length 180 mm are published values of the Japan Kendama Association (JKA); ken height 160 mm and cups 42 / 38 / 35 mm come from a user-provided description of the JKA 16-2 model (primary source not verified)). ``"recommended_large_cup"`` = big cup 49 mm, hole 24 mm. · examples: `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`, `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_kendama`
- `kendama_simulate` `table → table` GPU: none — 2-phase kendama simulation: while the string is taut, the ball is tied to the pivot (**the string hole of the cross-piece** = hand + kp["tie_offset"]) (projection method, the same as :func:`ballistics.tether_simulate`: with a fixed pivot in vacuum the trajectory is identical; string length = kp["pendulum_length"]); once slack, free fall (gravity + drag, kp["bp"]; rho = 0 for vacuum). Every step, :func:`kendama_catch_check` (big cup = hand + kp["cup_offset"], axis kp["cup_axis"]) judges the catch, and the simulation ends once caught. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `noisy_perceiver` `no input → any` GPU: none — Adds isotropic Gaussian noise to perception: ``perceive(t, p, v) → (p̂, v̂)`` (position σ = noise_pos [m], velocity σ = noise_vel [m/s]). A negative σ raises ValueError. rng = numpy.random.Generator. · examples: `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`
- `parabola_fit_g` `no input → table` GPU: none — Fits the parabola p(t) = p_r + v_r (t − t_ref) − ½ g (t − t_ref)² ẑ by least squares with gravity g (−z) known (6 unknowns = position and velocity). · examples: `gallery_drive_kendama_racket`
- `pendulum_launch_speed` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Giving this speed at the bottom yields amplitude θ₀ (energy conservation): v₀ = √(2gL(1 − cos θ₀)). θ₀ ∈ [0, π]. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `pendulum_period_exact` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Period 4√(L/g)·K(sin(θ₀/2)) of a pendulum (a rod, or a string within the range where it does not go slack) with amplitude θ₀ ∈ (0, π). As θ₀ → 0 it tends to 2π√(L/g). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `pendulum_rod_simulate` `no input → table` GPU: none — Rod pendulum (the constraint acts in both directions: it does not go slack) θ̈ = −(g/L) sin θ integrated with RK4. Returns ``{"t", "theta", "omega", "energy"}`` (energy = ½L²ω² − gL cos θ, unit mass). For comparison, to check the period theorem for θ₀ > π/2, where a string goes slack. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `swing_up_apex` `table → table` GPU: none — Closed form for how high a ball hanging straight down (L below the pivot, at rest) rises under :func:`swing_up_plan`. If the deceleration a > g, the string goes slack the instant deceleration begins (bang: T/2, trap: 2T/3), and the ball falls freely from the hand height z_s and speed v_s at that moment → apex z = tie_z + z_s − L + v_s²/(2g) (ball center measured from the hand's starting point; L = effective string length, tie_z = height of the pivot above the hand). If a ≤ g, it does not go slack and the ball stops L below the pivot. Returns ``{"accel", "flies", "slack_t", "z_slack", "v_slack", "apex", "apex_above_handle", "apex_above_cup"}`` (apex_above_handle = apex − lift; apex_above_cup = that minus the height of the big cup's rim: reaching the cup needs ≥ h_c, entering the cup's window needs h_c ≤ … ≤ h_c + 1.5 r_b). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `swing_up_lift` `table → scalar` GPU: none — Closed form for the lift amount of the swing-up (bang): the lift that puts the ball's apex ``apex_above_cup`` above the center of the receiving cup (the inverse of :func:`swing_up_apex`). apex − lift − cup_z = tie_z + lift/2 − L + 2 lift²/(g T²) − lift − cup_z = A, taken as a degree-2 equation in lift, positive root. Default A = max(h_c + 0.9 r_b, (top_offset − cup_z) + r_b + 0.035): an apex where the bottom of the ball clears the highest point of the kendama by 35 mm (the hold of :func:`catch_plan_staged` does not bring the cup closer until the ball has cleared it; during the clearance time ≈ 2√(2·0.035/g) = 0.17 s the cup is moved back sideways by 10 cm). Unless the deceleration 4·lift/T² exceeds g, the ball does not fly (ValueError). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `swing_up_plan` `table → any` GPU: none — Open-loop trajectory of the hand (center of the cross-piece; the string's pivot and the big cup are offset from it by kp's offsets and move with it): lifts straight up from ``origin`` by ``lift`` in ``T_lift`` seconds, then stays still. Returns a function t → (3,) (origin for t ≤ 0, at rest at origin + lift·ẑ for t ≥ T_lift). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `tether_slack_angle` `no input → any` GPU: none — Angle θ_s (from straight down) at which the string goes slack for a ball with speed v₀ = √(2gL(1 − cos θ₀)) at the bottom (the energy at which a rod would stop at θ₀). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `tether_tension_fixed` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Tension T = m(v²/L + g cos θ) of an inextensible string with a fixed hand end (v = speed, θ = angle from straight down). If negative, "a string cannot push" = it goes slack. · examples: `poc_kendama`

#### drive / kendamaworld (12)
- `add_ken` `table × table → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a ken to the world at pose (p = center of the cross-piece, R) (face labels 27/28/30/31 are kept as is). Returns the index into objects. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`
- `add_string` `table → scalar` GPU: none — Adds the string (label 29, dark gray) to the world. Returns the index into objects. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`
- `camera_perceiver` `table → any` GPU: none — Perception that derives the ball's (p̂, v̂) from images alone: ``perceive(t, p, v, scene) → (p̂, v̂) | None`` (for :func:`kendama.kendama_simulate`; with attribute ``observe_all = True`` it is called every step). **The ground truth (p, v) is used only to render the world, and v is never read.** · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `ken_mesh` `table → table` GPU: none — Mesh of the ken + cross-piece (big cup, small cup) + base cup. Origin = center of the cross-piece (hand), ken = +x (ken tip at +x), cross-piece axis = +z (big cup on top). · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_kendama`
- `ken_set_pose` `table × matrix → any` GPU: none — Sets the pose of ken i to (p, R) (rewrites only the vertices). ValueError for an object that is not a ken. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`
- `ken_truth` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Ground-truth projection of ken i_ken: the (col, row) of the rim center of the receiving cup (anchors[kp["catch_cup"] + "_rim"] moved by the pose), its depth, the cup radius in the image [px] (using the big cup's radius), and ``visible`` (in front of the camera with the pixel inside the image). Same form as ballworld.ball_truth. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`
- `kendama_clearance` `table → table` GPU: none — Clearance [m] from the ball's surface to the kendama (the solids of revolution of ken and cross-piece) (negative = the ball penetrates the kendama). With kp's trick pose (R_ken, grip point grip), hand ``hand`` and ball center ``p_ball`` (each (3,) or (N, 3)). The distance to a solid of revolution equals exactly the 2-D distance to its meridian profile, so it does not depend on the mesh discretization. Returns ``{"gap" (N,), "ken" (N,), "cross" (N,)}`` (ken / cross = clearance to each part). The physics does not resolve ball-kendama collisions, so this quantity counts the steps where "the ball passed through the kendama" (used for gates and honest reporting). ``R_ken`` (iteration 19, grip switch in combos): pass the pose as (3, 3) or per-time (N, 3, 3) instead of kp["R_ken"]. ``grip`` = override of the grip point (local). If both are None, behaves as before. · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `kendama_pose` `table → table` GPU: none — Sets the state of the kendama world: the ken (1 rigid body; grip point kp["grip"] at hand ``hand``, pose ``R_ken`` defaulting to the trick pose kp["R_ken"] in kp: cross-piece center = hand − R·grip), the ball (center ``p_ball``), and the string (cross-piece string hole → ball string hole). ``R_ball`` defaults to the rotation that points the ball's string hole (−HOLE_AXIS_LOCAL) at the cross-piece's string hole (the ball's rotation is not solved: correct while taut, approximate in flight). Returns ``{"tie", "cup" (rim center of the receiving cup), "cup_axis", "cross" (cross-piece center), "string_hole", "hole_axis" (direction of the large hole, world), "R_ball"}``. ``world`` is the one from :func:`kendama_world` (world["kendama"] is required). · examples: `poc_kendama`
- `kendama_rig` `table → table` GPU: none — Set of cameras viewing the swing-up space (x, y ∈ ±0.4 m, z ∈ 0.55 to 1.45 m: hand 1.0 m, string 0.42 m, lift 0.265 m). n = 2: azimuth 0° and 90°; n = 4: every 90°. All look at ``target`` (default (0, 0, 1.0)). Returns ``[{"pose", "K", "eye", "width", "height"}, …]`` (same form as ballworld.camera_rig). · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_kendama`
- `kendama_world` `table → table` GPU: none — A world of floor + ken (trick pose R_ken from kp, grip point kp["grip"] at ``hand``) + ball with hole + string. Origin on the floor, z up. The ball hangs below the cross-piece's string hole by the effective string length (kp["pendulum_length"]) (swung ``hang_deg`` from straight down toward ``hang_dir`` — with the diagonal (1, −1), the lateral offset is visible from both cameras at azimuth 0° and 90°). If ``p_ball`` is given, the ball is placed there. The floor is split into 0.25 m cells (as 1 large quad, any triangle reaching behind the camera is dropped whole and the floor vanishes). The return value's world["kendama"] = ``{"ken", "ball", "string"}`` (indices into objects) + ``"kp"``. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_kendama`
- `string_mesh` `no input → any` GPU: none — A thin prism joining 2 points (the ball's string hole p_ball and the cross-piece's string hole p_cup) (4 sides + both ends, 8 vertices, 12 faces, outward-facing). Square cross-section of side 2·radius. ValueError if the two points coincide. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`
- `string_set` `table → any` GPU: none — Moves both ends of string i to (p_ball, p_cup) (rewrites only the vertices). ValueError for an object that is not a string. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`

#### drive / lateral (20)
- `ackermann_steer_angles` `any → table` GPU: none — Ackermann inner and outer wheel steering angles (turning radius R at the center of the rear axle, wheelbase L, track width t). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `bicycle_model_step` `any → any` GPU: none — 1 step of the linear 2-wheel equivalent (bicycle) model (classic 4th-order Runge–Kutta; δ and u are constant within the step). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `clothoid_design` `no input → table` GPU: none — Quantities for joining a straight line → circle (radius R) with a clothoid of length L. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `clothoid_points` `no input → table` GPU: none — Points of a curve whose curvature is linear in arc length, κ(s) = κ₀ + (κ₁ − κ₀) s / length (part of a clothoid; a circular arc or straight line if κ₀ = κ₁). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `curvature_speed_plan` `any → table` GPU: none — Speed planning that builds a speed limit from a curvature sequence and enforces acceleration/deceleration limits with 2 passes, forward and backward (a classical method). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `curve_speed_limit` `any → any` GPU: none — Upper speed limit without sliding outward on a curve (radius R) with superelevation i and side-friction coefficient f: v = √(g R (i + f)/(1 − i f)) [m/s]. · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `design_min_radius` `any → any` GPU: none — Minimum curve radius from Eq. (3) of the commentary on the Road Structure Ordinance: R = V² / (127 (i + f)) [m] (V in km/h). · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `fresnel_integrals` `any → any` GPU: none — Fresnel integrals C(x) = ∫₀ˣ cos(π t²/2) dt, S(x) = ∫₀ˣ sin(π t²/2) dt (odd functions). · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `friction_circle_usage` `any → any` GPU: none — Friction-circle utilization √(a_x² + a_y²) / (μ g) (above 1 = outside the friction circle = exceeds the force the tires can receive from the road surface). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `lateral_offset` `any → table` GPU: none — Arc length s along a polyline path and lateral offset n (positive to the left of the direction of travel) of a point. Projection onto the nearest segment. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `offtracking_circle` `no input → table` GPU: none — Off-tracking transient (closed form): the vehicle pose and the radius of the inner wheel after the front-axle center has traveled arc length s since entering a circle of radius R. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `pure_pursuit_circle_offset` `no input → table` GPU: none — Steady-state circle radius ρ and lateral offset ρ − R (positive outward) when tracking a steady circle (radius R) with pure pursuit (referenced to the rear-axle center). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `pure_pursuit_curvature` `any → table` GPU: none — pure pursuit: curvature κ = 2 sin α / L_d for aiming from the rear-axle center (``pose`` = (x, y, ψ), (N, 3) allowed) at the point a distance L_d ahead on the path. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `rear_axle_path` `any → table` GPU: none — Trajectory of the rear-axle center dragged without slip by a polyline trajectory of the front-axle center (an exact pursuit curve per segment). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `stanley_steer` `any → table` GPU: none — Stanley steering angle δ = ψ_e + atan2(−k e, k_s + v) (the lateral offset e of the front-axle center is positive to the left of the path; ψ_e = path heading − ψ). · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `stanley_straight_decay` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Closed form of the front-axle lateral offset e(t) under Stanley (unclipped) on a straight path. · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `steady_cornering` `no input → table` GPU: none — Steady-state circular cornering of the linear 2-wheel equivalent (bicycle) model (speed u, turning radius R = u/r, left turn positive). · examples: `gallery_drive_lateral_env`
- `time_to_line_crossing` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — TLC: time [s] until the vehicle (its reference point) reaches the lane boundary, assuming it drives a circle (or straight line) at its current curvature. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `turn_maneuver_check` `table → table` GPU: none — Checks how a left or right turn is made (Road Traffic Act Art. 34(1)-(2) / Rules of the Road (Kyosoku) 5-7-2). All numeric margins are assumptions (``SOURCES``). · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`
- `understeer_gradient` `no input → table` GPU: none — Understeer gradient K = (m/L)(l_r/C_f − l_f/C_r) [rad/(m/s²)], and the characteristic / critical speed. · examples: `poc_driving_lateral`

#### drive / pegsym (15)
- `pegsym_scene_mjcf` `matrix × matrix → any` GPU: none — MJCF string for a polygonal peg scene (no mujoco needed): hole = one wall box per edge (below the narrowest part), a 45° chamfer plate and a bright collar (mouth face at z = 0); peg = a convex-mesh prism (cross-section ``peg_vertices``, peg frame, axis at the origin). The carriage has x, y, z slides and a yaw hinge (position control), followed by a 6-DoF spring wrist (tilt ``k_rot`` and twist ``k_yaw`` [N m/rad] are separate; the grasp is soft in twist). Cameras: the wrist camera (30 mm beside the carriage, looking straight down), an upward camera at ``station`` [m] from the hole (in the floor plane, viewing the peg end face from below), and a fixed oblique overhead camera ``side`` for figures. Each box lies only in the half-plane outside its own edge, so extending it past the corners never intrudes into the hole (the same construction works for any convex hole shape). **Raises** ValueError: polygon not convex, chamfer < 0, hole depth ≤ chamfer, friction < 0, stiffness ≤ 0. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `plane_topview` `image2d × matrix × matrix × signal → image2d` GPU: none — Resamples an oblique or from-below image into a view of the world plane z = ``z`` seen from directly above (homography = project each grid point and sample bilinearly). The camera is given by world → OpenCV camera ``R`` and ``t`` (x_c = R X + t) and intrinsics ``K`` (convention: pixel centers at integers). The grid is centered at ``centre`` = (x, y) with side ``extent`` [m] and pixel size ``res`` [m]. Columns = +x, rows = −y (north up). An image taken from below (mirrored) also comes out in the same orientation in this view. Grid points behind the camera or outside the image get ``fill``. Returns an (S, S) grayscale image (color is converted to luminance). **Raises** ValueError: image is not 2-D grayscale or (H, W, 3/4), K or R is not 3×3, t does not have 3 components, extent ≤ 0, res ≤ 0, S > 4096. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_coverage_image` `matrix → image2d` GPU: none — Coverage image 0..1 ((size, width); anti-aliasing with ``ss`` × ``ss`` subsamples) of a convex polygon (vertex list in pixel coordinates (col, row)). A building block for synthesis with ground truth. **Raises** ValueError: not convex, size < 8, ss < 1. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_fit_check` `matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Whether a point set (peg vertices, or projected vertices of a tilted peg) can be put into a convex polygonal hole **by translation alone** — solves the linear program maximizing the margin m, max m s.t. n_j·(p + t) ≤ h_j − m (all points, all edges), exactly by enumerating vertices where 3 constraints hold with equality (at most a dozen or so edges; the combinations are solved together). Returns ``fit`` (m ≥ 0), ``margin`` [m] (if negative, the minimum penetration), ``t`` (optimal translation (2,)) and ``active`` (indices of the equality edges). **Raises** ValueError: point set is not (N ≥ 1, 2) or not finite, hole is not a convex polygon, hole normals do not enclose all directions (unbounded). · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_offset` `matrix × scalar → table` GPU: none — Polygon obtained by shifting each edge of a convex polygon outward by ``clearance`` [m] (corners stay sharp = how hole drawings are made). For a regular polygon this is a similarity enlargement, so orientation and symmetry are unchanged. Returns ``vertices``, ``normals`` and ``offsets`` (n·x ≤ h). **Raises** ValueError: not convex, clearance < 0 or not finite, an edge vanishes when shifted (since there are no reflex corners, this only admits shapes where it cannot happen). · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_peg` `scalar → table` GPU: none — Peg cross-section (counterclockwise vertex list): regular n-gon (apothem ``apothem`` [m], normal of face 0 at ``yaw`` [rad]). If ``cut`` > 0, vertex 0 (between face 0 and face 1) is cut off by a line whose normal is that vertex's direction, ``cut`` [m] inside the circumcircle — keyed (symmetry n = 1). Returns ``vertices`` (V, 2), ``n`` (nominal n-fold symmetry of the shape: 1 if keyed), ``apothem``, ``circumradius``, ``yaw``, ``cut`` and ``cut``. **Raises** ValueError: n < 3, apothem ≤ 0, cut < 0 or at least the difference between circumradius and inradius (an edge vanishes). · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_two_point_depth` `matrix × matrix × scalar → table` GPU: none — Exact two-point-contact depth l₂ [m] (from the narrowest part z = 0 to the center of the tip) of a tilted polygonal peg: the part of the peg at z ≤ 0 at depth l is the convex hull of the tip-face vertices and the points where the side ridges cross z = 0. Since the hole is a vertical prism, the peg enters while the horizontal projection of these vertices fits into the hole by translation (:func:`polygon_fit_check`) and stops fitting as l deepens — that boundary is found by bisection. ``tilt_dir`` = horizontal tilt direction [rad] (world frame, the same frame as the peg cross-section). The circle formula for comparison (Whitney; the exact 3-D cylinder formula of pegsim (2R − r(cos θ + sec θ))/tan θ) is returned for the inscribed circle (r = A, R = A + δ) and the circumscribed circle (r = A/cos(π/n), R = (A + δ)/cos(π/n)) (``circle_in``, ``circle_out``). The small-angle limit for a square tilted about an axis parallel to a face is Eq. (2.28) of Goli et al. 2024, φ = (v − v′)/h, i.e. l₂ tan θ → 2δ (``goli_small_angle`` = 2δ/tan θ). For odd n (triangle) a vertex lies opposite each face, so it is deeper than the inscribed-circle formula in every direction. For even n it matches the inscribed-circle formula in the face-normal direction (1e-11 m for the square). Some combinations go up to 0.03 % beyond the inscribed-circle side (tilt 6°, 15° from the face). Returns ``l2``, ``circle_in``, ``circle_out`` and ``goli_small_angle`` (δ is the mean difference of apothems, n the number of vertices). **Raises** ValueError: θ ≤ 0 or ≥ 30°, does not enter the narrowest part while tilted, no two-point contact up to depth_max. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `polygon_yaw_read` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Reads the orientation **modulo the period 2π/n** from the complex Fourier coefficients of the object contour (subpixel iso-line, the same ``threshold_sub_pix`` as :mod:`pegtactile`) in the top view (:func:`plane_topview`, columns = +x, rows = −y). Under n-fold symmetry the only nonzero coefficients are k ≡ 1 (mod n), and arg(c₁₋ₙ c₁ⁿ⁻¹)/n does not depend on the start point (:func:`pegtactile.symmetry_order_contour`). If ``n`` is given, the phase for that n is used instead of the detected n (when n is known from the drawing; the phase can be read even if edge jitter in real images makes extra coefficients significant). ``polarity`` = whether the object is dark ("dark", a hole) or bright ("bright", the peg end face). The intensities are stretched to 0..1 using the 2 % and 98 % quantiles, then the 0.5 iso-line is taken. Returns ``n_detected``, ``n_used``, ``yaw`` (world orientation; the sign is flipped back because image rows are −y; representative in [0, P) of period 2π/n_used), ``centroid_px`` (row, col) and ``amps``. If n_used = 0 (circle), yaw = nan. **Raises** ValueError: unknown polarity, flat image, no contour, n < 0. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `relative_yaw_from_images` `image2d × image2d × scalar → table` GPU: none — Orientation difference between the peg (upward camera → view resampled onto the plane of the tip face) and the hole (wrist camera → view of the mouth plane), on the n-fold symmetry quotient: Δ = symmetry_fold(yaw_peg − yaw_hole, n). Both are read with :func:`polygon_yaw_read`; the shape-dependent phase constant (difference between vertex direction and face direction) cancels in the difference between identical shapes (since the hole is a similar shape obtained by shifting the peg outward). Keyed shapes (n = 1) are not similar, so a small offset remains (measured by a gate). Returns ``delta`` (rotating the peg by −delta aligns it), ``peg`` and ``hole`` (readings) and ``n``. **Raises** ValueError: n < 1, reading failed (exception from :func:`polygon_yaw_read`). · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `rotation_search_plan` `scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Candidates for the rotation search (yaw corrections applied to the peg): step s = P/M dividing 1 period P = 2π/n_sym into M = ⌈P/(2 phi_cap)⌉ equal parts (≤ 2 phi_cap, so the capture windows cover it without gaps). ``order`` = "alternate" (0, +s, −s, +2s, … from the estimate) or "sweep" (0, s, 2s, …). n_sym = 0 (circle) gives 1 candidate. Returns ``angles`` (M,), ``step``, ``period`` and ``M``. **Raises** ValueError: n_sym < 0, phi_cap ≤ 0, unknown order. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `rotation_window` `scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Rotation window within which the peg enters the hole (or its mouth, if chamfered). Closed form for a regular n-gon (derived): with centers aligned, the vertices lie at directions π/n ∓ φ from the face normal, and the peg enters if the normal-direction extent of the outermost vertex, a cos(π/n − |φ|), is at most A + δ (+ W): φ = π/n − arccos(x), x = (A + δ + W) cos(π/n)/A (if x ≥ 1 the window fills the half period π/n). Since arccos has a rounding floor near 1, it is written as atan2(√(1 − x²), x). If ``peg_vertices`` and ``hole_vertices`` are given, the windows in the positive and negative directions are also measured by bisection on the linear program (:func:`polygon_fit_check`, translation also free) (second (independent) implementation; the only option for keyed shapes). Returns ``phi_fit`` (the narrowest part, not the mouth), ``phi_cap`` (chamfer mouth), ``period`` = 2π/n, ``M`` = ⌈period/(2 cap)⌉ and ``lp`` (``plus``/``minus``: when vertices are given, both ends of the window entering the mouth = the connected interval containing 0; the scan divides the half period into 360 steps, the ends by bisection). Here cap is phi_eff when mu is given; otherwise finite phi_cap or the smallest lp window. · examples: `poc_peg_symmetry_search`
- `search_expected_tries` `scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Expected number of tries of the rotation search (exact, when the unknown orientation error e is uniform over 1 period). With candidates c_k (:func:`rotation_search_plan`), the k-th try succeeds when e first falls in [c_k − φ, c_k + φ] (period P), so E = Σ_k (1 − |∪_{i<k} I_i|/P). The computation splits the circle at the interval ends and, for each small interval, counts the index of the first candidate covering it (same value, O(M²) vector operations). If the step is exactly 2φ, E = (M + 1)/2 (``closed``). The ratio to a search unaware of the symmetry (period 2π, M₁ = ⌈π/φ⌉), ``ratio_vs_blind`` → 1/n. If ``estimate_sigma`` [rad] is given, e is assumed normal (wrapped to the period) with standard deviation σ around the estimate, and the expected count in "alternate" order is also returned (``expected_with_estimate``, numerical integration with 4,096 points). - `puck_scene_mjcf` `table → any` GPU: none — Self-made minimal MJCF (Coulomb version, mujoco not required): a cylindrical puck (free joint) on a plane with friction, 4 walls (boxes), an overhead camera. - `puck_slide_predict` `signal × signal × table × scalar → table` GPU: none — Chains the puck path in closed form: constant direction and uniform deceleration per segment (wall to wall), :func:`puck_wall_bounce` at the walls. · examples: `poc_air_hockey_intercept`

- `puck_synth_frames` `table × table × signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Synthetic frame sequence and ground truth: samples the closed-form path (:func:`puck_slide_predict`) at fps and draws it with :func:`puck_render_frame`. · examples: `poc_air_hockey_intercept`

- `puck_track` `any × table → table` GPU: none — Frame sequence → per-frame candidates → :func:`balltrack.ball_track` (linked by constant-velocity prediction; jumps beyond ``max_jump_px`` are dropped) → world coordinates. · examples: `poc_air_hockey_intercept`

- `striker_plan` `any × signal × table → table` GPU: none — Strike planning (rule-based): computes the joint angles for the predicted crossing point by IK and moves each servo at a constant angular velocity ≤ ω_max. - `pour_scene_mjcf` `scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — MJCF of a scene in which an open chute (floor length ``L``, width ``B``, back and side wall height ``wall``) is packed on a grid with rigid spheres up to depth ``h0`` (**no mujoco needed**). The floor is rough (sliding friction ``floor_mu``, so the bottom layer does not slide out along the floor — the same role as the rough base in granular); the side walls use ``wall_mu``. Returns: ``xml``, ``positions``, ``info`` (L, B, h0, wall, radius, lip_height, mass_each, n, timestep, A_fill = L·h0). **Raises** ``ValueError``: ``h0 ≥ wall`` / ``contact_tc < 2 timestep`` / not even 1 layer of spheres fits / misspelling. · examples: `poc_powder_scoop_pour`

- `membrane_markers` `scalar × scalar → matrix` GPU: none — Regular grid of marker centers (N, 2) = (x, y) [px] scattered over an n×n-pixel field of view (pitch pitch_px, subpixel phase (ox, oy)). - `membrane_render_markers` `rgb × matrix × scalar × scalar → rgb` GPU: none — Draws black disk markers (centers pts (N, 2) [px], radius r_px) on RGB (H, W, 3): rgb *= 1 − dark·coverage using pixel coverage. Coverage is supersampled sub² only for pixels on the disk edge (1 inside, 0 outside). The image is not warped by interpolation, so the ground truth is exact. **Raises** ValueError: rgb is not (H, W, 3), pts is not (N, 2), r_px ≤ 0, dark outside [0, 1]. · examples: `poc_knife_tactile_toughness`, `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`, `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `membrane_shear_field` `table × table × matrix × matrix × table → table` GPU: none — Displacement field of the membrane surface: tangential displacements ``ux``, ``uy`` obtained by convolving the Mindlin traction q(r) with the Cerruti kernel, the radial displacements ``urx``, ``ury`` of the normal load (:func:`hertz_surface_ur` split into x, y) [m], ``q``, the stick/slip masks ``mask_stick`` (r ≤ c) and ``mask_slip`` (c < r ≤ a), and ``r``. X, Y are grid coordinates [m] (origin at the center). **Raises** ValueError: X and Y differ in shape, or do not match n of kern. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`, `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `mindlin_fit` `table × matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Fits (c/a, μP) to marker positions pts_px (M, 2) [px] and displacements u_m (M, 2) [m]: coarse scan over c/a → fine search around the best, with μP solved by linear least squares for each c. Returns ``c_over_a``, ``q_ratio`` = 1 − (c/a)³, ``muP``, ``Q``, ``mu`` (= μP/P), ``rms_m``, ``shift_m``. ``rigid=True`` also frees a rigid shift (tx, ty) — in the prototype this was **counterproductive** (it degenerates with the 1/r tail of the outer 900 points and shifts c/a by 0.028), so it is off by default. On real hardware, drift should properly be subtracted separately using distant markers outside the contact. Fitting the true displacements gives a c/a error of 0.001; tracking from images gives 0.011 (centroid pixel-locking adds a common mode). **Raises** ValueError: shape mismatch, fewer than 3 points. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `mindlin_fit_vector` `table × matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Mindlin fit for directional shear (the 2-component version of :func:`mindlin_fit`): reads (c/a, μP, direction φ) at once. · examples: `gallery_drive_soil_tactile`
- `mindlin_model` `table × matrix × matrix × table × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Inverse model that produces the Mindlin displacement field for any c/a via **similarity laws** (only 1 convolution). · examples: `gallery_drive_soil_tactile`, `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `mindlin_partial_slip` `scalar × table × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Cattaneo–Mindlin partial slip (Johnson 1985 §7.2): a tangential force Q is applied to a sphere while it is pressed with normal force P. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`, `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `mindlin_traction` `matrix × table → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Tangential traction q(r) = q′ − q″ [Pa]: q′ = μp0√(1−r²/a²) (r < a), q″ = μp0(c/a)√(1−r²/c²) (r < c). In the slip annulus c ≤ r < a, q = μp(r) (pinned at the Coulomb limit); in the stick circle q < μp. ``mp`` is the table of :func:`mindlin_partial_slip`. Same shape as r. **Raises** ValueError: mp lacks a/c/mu/p0. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `slip_entropy` `signal → scalar` GPU: none — Shannon entropy of the histogram (bins bins, range [0, vmax] — the maximum if omitted) of the displacement magnitudes |u|, normalized by ln(bins) (0..1). The slip indicator of Yuan 2017: it rises as the stick core shrinks and more markers lie on the gradient of the slip annulus. **Raises** ValueError: no points, bins < 2. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `stick_radius_modelfree` `matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Model-free stick radius: in order of distance from the center, starting from the median δ̂ of the inner 6 points, the radius ``c_px`` of the midpoint between the first point where |ux − δ̂| exceeds rel·|δ̂| + abs_px and the point just before it (resolution = marker spacing). ``core_px`` = δ̂. pts_c are center-relative (M, 2) [px], u_px is (M, 2) [px]. **Raises** ValueError: fewer than 6 points. · examples: `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`

#### drive / tactorque (17)
- `boussinesq_kernel` `scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Discrete kernel (2n grid, already rfft2-transformed) of the surface displacement produced by normal pressure (uniform 1 Pa on 1 pixel = pitch²): ``Kx`` = ū_x, ``Ky`` = ū_y (tangential, −(1−2ν)/(4πG) · x/r² and y/r², point-load solution of Johnson 1985 §3.2), and with ``with_uz`` also ``Kz`` = ū_z ((1−ν)/(2πGr)). Pixel-averaged (sub² subsamples). Center pixel: ∫□ x/r² dA = 0 (odd function), ∫□ 1/r dA = 4h ln(1+√2) (analytic value). Normal-load counterpart built the same way as :func:`tacslip.cerruti_kernel` (tangential → tangential). **Raises** ValueError: n < 8, pitch, G ≤ 0, ν outside [0, 0.5]. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `boussinesq_surface_displacement` `matrix × table → table` GPU: none — Normal pressure p (n, n) [Pa] → surface displacements ``ux``, ``uy`` (plus ``uz`` if the kernel has ``Kz``, positive = sinking) (n, n) [m]. Linear convolution zero-padded to 2n. **Raises** ValueError: p is not (n, n), kern is not a table of :func:`boussinesq_kernel`. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `dipole_to_torque_fit` `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Linear calibration between the series D (K,) of 1 dipole component and known moments M (K,) [N·m]: D ≈ k M (through the origin) and D ≈ k₁ M + b (with intercept). Returns ``k``, ``R2`` (coefficient of determination through the origin = 1 − SS_res/SS_tot), ``k1``, ``b``, ``R2_affine``, ``rmse_M`` (residual RMS converted to M). Corresponds to the paper's calibration coefficient c = 1/k. **Raises** ValueError: K < 2, shapes differ, all M are equal. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `dipole_torque_resolution` `matrix × matrix × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Adds marker-centroid noise σ [px] to the displacements, recomputes the dipole ``trials`` times and measures the torque resolution σ_M = σ_D/|coef| [N·m]. Returns ``sigma_D`` (2,), ``sigma_M`` (2,), ``D0`` (noise-free), ``snr`` = |D0|/σ_D, ``trials``. σ_M ∝ σ (measured). **Raises** ValueError: σ < 0, trials < 2, coef = 0. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `ellipse_pressure_shifted` `matrix × matrix × scalar × scalar × scalar → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Elliptical Hertz pressure p0 √(1 − x′²/a² − y′²/b²) [Pa] with semi-axes a (x) and b (y) [m], P = 2πab p0/3 (Johnson 1985 Eq. 4.24), with the center shifted to d. For b ≫ a the shape approaches a cylindrical (ridge- or wedge-like) indentation — the 3rd shape-invariance gate. **Raises** ValueError: a, b, P ≤ 0, X and Y differ in shape. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `grasp_torque_frame` `image2d × image2d × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — From images in 1 pass: reference and current marker images (:func:`tacslip.marker_image`) → :func:`tacslip.marker_track` → field in meters → :func:`torque_decompose`. ``pitch_px``, ``r_px`` = marker grid pitch and radius [px], ``pitch`` = m/px, ``window`` is (cx, cy, R) in [px]. Area per 1 marker = (pitch_px·pitch)², neighborhood radius for the divergence = 1.5 pitch. ``P``, ``mu``, ``torsion_model`` set the torsion conversion (:func:`torque_decompose`; the default, partial slip of Hertz contact, needs P and mu; for a flat punch use ``"no_slip"``). Returns the torque_decompose table + ``track`` (matched, n0, n1, p0, u [px]). **Raises** ValueError: fewer than 9 tracked correspondences (not enough for the dipole), pitch ≤ 0, ValueError from torque_decompose. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `hertz_pressure_shifted` `matrix × matrix × table → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Hertz pressure p0 √(1 − r′²/a²) [Pa] with its center shifted to d = (dx, dy) [m] (``hz`` = the table of :func:`tacsim.hertz_sphere`). For a grasped sphere under a small tilting torque τ, the pressure center moves by d = τ/P (quasi-static moment balance), so the 1st moment of the shifted Hertz pressure about the original center is P·d = τ (exactly linear). **Raises** ValueError: hz has no a/p0, X and Y differ in shape. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `marker_divergence` `matrix × matrix × scalar → table` GPU: none — Per-point divergence ``div`` = ∂ux/∂x + ∂uy/∂y and curl ``curl`` = ∂uy/∂x − ∂ux/∂y from scattered markers pts (N, 2) and displacements u (N, 2) (unit = unit of u ÷ unit of pts). Fits a plane c0 + c1 x + c2 y by least squares to the points within the neighborhood radius ``radius`` (at most ``k_max`` points) (on a regular grid with a radius of 1.01 pitch this equals the 5-point central difference and agrees with :func:`sceneflow.flow_divergence` to 1e-15; with a radius of 1.5 pitch the 9 points give a row-averaged difference that differs by 11 % at the border, measured). Solves the normal equations for all points in one batch. Points with fewer than ``min_neighbors`` neighbors or with singular (collinear) normal equations get ``valid`` = False and div/curl = nan (fail-closed: never silently 0). The same op works for scattered FEM nodes. **Raises** ValueError: pts/u is not (N, 2), shapes differ, radius ≤ 0, N < min_neighbors. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `pressure_first_moment` `matrix × matrix × matrix × scalar → table` GPU: none — 0th and 1st moments of a pressure p (n, n) [Pa] on a grid: ``P`` = Σ p h² [N], ``M1`` = Σ (x, y) p h² [N·m], ``tau`` = (−M1_y, M1_x) (z points from the gel to the object; moment of the force −ẑ p with which the object presses on the gel). **Raises** ValueError: shapes differ, pitch ≤ 0. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `punch_pressure` `matrix × matrix × scalar × scalar → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Pressure [Pa] of a flat circular punch (radius a [m]): p = P/(2πa√(a²−r²)) + 3(M1_x x + M1_y y)/(2πa³√(a²−r²)) (r < a, 0 outside). Term 1 = Johnson 1985 Eq. 3.34; term 2 = the antisymmetric term satisfying ∫ (x, y) p dA = M1 (derivation in the module docstring, confirmed numerically by a gate). Passing ``pitch`` averages each pixel over sub×sub subsamples (reduces the grid error of the 1/√ singularity at the edge; with 4×4, Σ p h² matches P within 0.6 %, measured). **Raises** ValueError: a ≤ 0, P < 0, X and Y differ in shape, |M1| > Pa/3 (the contact separates: the linear formula no longer holds, fail-closed). · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `punch_surface_uz` `matrix × scalar × scalar × scalar × scalar → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Normal displacement [m] of the half-space surface under a flat circular punch (normal force P) (positive = sinking): uniform δ = P(1−ν)/(4Ga) inside the circle, (2δ/π) arcsin(a/r) outside (flat punch of Johnson 1985 §3.4; the equation number could not be confirmed in the text, **unverified** — verified numerically by agreeing within 0.35 % with the convolution of the Boussinesq kernel ``Kz``). **Raises** ValueError: a, P, G ≤ 0. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `rigid_rotation_fit` `matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Fits a rigid displacement u ≈ t + ω ẑ×r to the marker field inside a window by least squares: ``t`` = mean displacement, ``omega`` = Σ (x′u′_y − y′u′_x)/Σ r′² (′ = with the window mean subtracted), ``resid_rms`` = residual RMS, ``n``. In no-slip torsion the inside of the circle rotates rigidly (u_θ = βr), so ω = β is the ground truth (the mean curl/2 comes out low because the fit leaks outside at the circle edge — 11 % measured). ``window`` = (cx, cy, R). **Raises** ValueError: fewer than 3 points. · examples: `poc_knife_tactile_toughness`, `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `surface_divergence_closed_form` `matrix × scalar × scalar → matrix` GPU: none — Closed form of the divergence of the tangential surface displacement of a half-space, ∇·ū = −(1−2ν) p/(2G) (derived in this module from the Boussinesq point load ū_r = −(1−2ν)P/(4πGr) and, in 2-D, ∇·(r̂/r) = 2πδ²). Gate comparing it with the numerical divergence of the convolution (0.2 % for r < 0.8a, measured). **Raises** ValueError: G ≤ 0. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `tactile_dipole_moment` `matrix × matrix → table` GPU: none — Tactile dipole moment D = Σ_i w ρ_i r_i (2 components). ``form``: * ``"divergence"`` — paper (arXiv 2404.15626) Eqs. 4–8: ρ_i = (∇·u)_i (pass ``rho``, or :func:`marker_divergence` via ``radius``). * ``"norm_cross"`` — the paper's baseline (Eqs. 10–11, Yamaguchi & Atkeson style): ρ_i = |u_i| (the vector norm in place of the normal force). The tilt component of l_i × f_i is (l_y|u|, −l_x|u|), i.e. D rotated by 90°, so it is returned in the same "1st moment" slot. Under a symmetric tilt after zeroing, |u| is an even function of M, so it is identically 0 (blind to the sign; gate). * ``"radial"`` — this module's variant: ρ_i = u_i · r̂_i (radial component). ``origin``: ``"midpoint"`` (Eqs. 6–7, midpoint of the positive and negative centroids) / ``"centre"`` (mean of pts, the baseline's convention) / (x0, y0). ``weight``: ``"area"`` = multiply by the area per 1 point ``area`` [m²] (comparable with the closed-form coefficient −(1−2ν)/(2G), unit m³) / ``"mean"`` = 1/N (paper). With ``window`` = (cx, cy, R) only points within radius R are used (a window that cuts off shear leakage; rationale in the module docstring). Invalid points (nan) are excluded. Returns ``D`` (2,), ``tau_dir`` = (−D_y, D_x) (direction of Eq. 9, without coefficient), ``origin``, ``n``, ``rho``, ``form``, ``keep``. **Raises** ValueError: unknown form/origin/weight (misspellings fail closed), shape of pts/u, "area" without area, fewer than 3 usable points. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `tilt_shear_field` `matrix × matrix × table → table` GPU: none — Exactly the paper's "zero after grasping" procedure: convolves the difference Δp between the pressure p_before right after grasping and the pressure p_after after the torque with the Boussinesq kernel, and returns the zeroed marker displacements ``ux``, ``uy`` (, ``uz``) and ``dp``. If the 0th moment of Δp is 0 (normal force unchanged), the dipole does not depend on the origin. **Raises** ValueError: the 2 arrays differ in shape. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `torque_decompose` `matrix × matrix × scalar × scalar × scalar → table` GPU: none — Splits the marker field into 3 mechanical quantities: ``translation`` = mean displacement in the window (shear Q, unidirectional component), ``omega`` = rigid rotation angle (:func:`rigid_rotation_fit`) → torsion ``Mz`` (needs a; ``omega_curl`` = mean curl/2 for reference), ``D`` = divergence dipole (area-weighted) → tilt ``M1`` = D / coef (coef defaults to the half-space closed form −(1−2ν)/(2G); on real hardware pass the calibrated value), ``tau`` = (−M1_y, M1_x). Divergence and curl do not change when the mean displacement is subtracted (the derivative of a constant is 0), so the order does not matter. The window (cx, cy, R) is limited to the contact circle (because in a half-space pure shear creates a divergence dipole over the whole window; see the module docstring). ``radius`` = neighborhood radius for the divergence (required). · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`
- `torsion_stick_field` `matrix × matrix × scalar × scalar × table × scalar → table` GPU: none — Surface displacement field of no-slip torsion (Reissner–Sagoci, corresponding to Johnson 1985 §3.9; equation number unconfirmed → verified numerically by convolution): ``ux``, ``uy`` [m] obtained by convolving the traction q_θ = 3M_z r/(4πa³√(a²−r²)) with the kernel of :func:`tacslip.cerruti_kernel`, plus the closed form ``beta`` = 3M_z/(16Ga³), the rigid rotation inside the circle ``ux_cf`` = −βy, ``uy_cf`` = βx (r < a), and the tractions ``qx``, ``qy``. Because the convolution returns a uniform u_θ/r = β inside the circle, the β formula is verified by an independent implementation (−0.5 %, uniformity 0.14 %, measured). This is the no-slip field: for a flat punch it is exact up to 8/(3π) times full slip, but Hertz contact always slips from the edge — for the partial-slip field of Hertz contact use ``field=True`` of :func:`cuttouch.torsion_partial_slip` (see the module docstring). **Raises** ValueError: G ≤ 0, a ≤ 0, X and Y differ in shape, the kernel grid does not match. · examples: `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`

#### drive / terrain (20)
- `add_mesh_object` `table × table → scalar` GPU: none — Places a procedural mesh (tree_mesh / pedestrian_mesh …, origin = bottom center) at a pose and adds it to the world. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_driving_crossing`, `poc_driving_decisions`, `poc_driving_humanoids`, `poc_driving_lateral`, `poc_driving_traffic`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `course_distance` `table × points → table` GPU: none — Distance from points (N, 2) to the course (union of drivable polygons), and the unit vector pointing outward from the nearest point. · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `crosswalk_mesh` `no input → table` GPU: none — Crosswalk (zebra): along a segment a→b across the road, stripes of width ``stripe`` and spacing ``gap``, extended by ``length`` perpendicular to a→b (on the left-hand side of a→b). ``{"V", "F", "color", "label" (12), "n_stripes", "area"}``. · examples: `poc_driving_crossing`, `poc_driving_humanoids`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `fbm_gradient` `image2d × image2d × table → any` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Closed form of (∂h/∂x, ∂h/∂y). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `fbm_height` `image2d × image2d × table → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Closed form of the fBm height: h(x, y) = Σ_k A_k cos(2π f_k (x cosθ_k + y sinθ_k) + φ_k) (table from :func:`fbm_params`). · examples: `poc_rover_slip_risk_path`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `fbm_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Table for building an fBm surface as a sum of sines with random phases (a continuous version of the spectral synthesis of Saupe 1988). · examples: `poc_rover_slip_risk_path`
- `material_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Material table. puddle = where Perlin(puddle_freq) > puddle_level (inside the road only, label 11, color = reflection refl·sky + (1−refl)·shaded road surface), stain = likewise dark stains (the label stays road; kept in the ground-truth field "stain"), wear = wear ratio of the white lines clip(wear·(Perlin(wear_freq)·0.5+0.5)·2, 0, 1). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `mesh_signed_volume` `points × matrix → scalar` GPU: none — Signed volume of a closed mesh (divergence theorem: Σ v₀·(v₁×v₂)/6, positive for outward orientation). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `pedestrian_mesh` `no input → table` GPU: none — Procedural pedestrian: 2 legs (boxes), torso (box), head (solid of revolution). Origin = center at the feet, +x is forward. ``stride`` [m] spreads the legs forward and backward. · examples: `gallery_drive_world_objects`, `poc_driving_crossing`, `poc_driving_humanoids`, `poc_driving_traffic`, `poc_driving_weather`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `perlin2` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Evaluates Perlin's (2002, improved noise) 2-D gradient noise at world coordinates (x, y). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `radial_periodogram` `image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Radially averages the periodogram of a height field (H, W) on a grid: ``{"f", "power", "count"}`` (f in cycles/m). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `scatter_offroad` `table → points` GPU: none — Scatters objects off the road (dart throwing): each point is at least ``margin`` from the course and at least ``r_min`` from every other point. · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `spectral_slope` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Straight-line log–log fit of the radial periodogram: ``{"beta", "intercept", "n"}`` (power ∝ f^{−beta}). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `terrain_gradient` `image2d × image2d × table → any` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Closed form of (∂z/∂x, ∂z/∂y): ∇(h·w) = w∇h + h·w′(d)·∇d, ∇d = unit vector pointing outward from the nearest point. · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `terrain_height` `image2d × image2d × table → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — z = fbm(x, y)·w(d(x, y)) + undulation(x, y). Without a course, w = 1 (relief only). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `terrain_mesh` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Grid mesh that divides (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) into cells of size step, with z = terrain_height. · examples: `gallery_drive_city_terrain`
- `terrain_params` `no input → table` GPU: none — Terrain table: fBm relief (0 within ``flat`` m of the road, then smoothstep over ``blend`` m) + road-surface undulation ``road_amp·½[sin(2πx/L₁+φ₁) + sin(2πy/L₂+φ₂)]`` (also applied to the road; upper bound of the gradient = road_amp·π/min(L)). · examples: `gallery_drive_city_terrain`, `poc_world_terrain`
- `tree_mesh` `no input → table` GPU: none — Procedural tree: trunk = regular n-gonal prism (height 0.35·height), crown = cone (conifer) or spheroid (broadleaf, vertical extent 0.65·height). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `world_apply_terrain` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Applies the terrain to the output of world_build (a flat world) (in place; returns the same dict). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`
- `world_materials` `table × table × matrix × matrix × table → table` GPU: none — Applies road-surface materials pixel by pixel to the rendering ``view`` (from world_camera, including "shade"). · examples: `poc_world_terrain`

- `kyosoku_summary` `no input → table` GPU: none — Reads the ledger of reproduced Rules of the Road (Kyosoku) scenarios (docs/drive/kyosoku_scenarios.json) and turns it into a category × status count table. · examples: `poc_driving_town`

- `town_chain` `any → table` GPU: none — Places the elements by chaining them in order: solves in closed form the rigid placement that aligns the entry of element k+1 with the exit of element k (``overlap`` before it) and passes it to :func:`drivecourse.course_layout`. · examples: `poc_driving_town`
- `town_checks` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Scoring of the end-to-end run (closed-form gates + the existing railroad-crossing scoring op). · examples: `poc_driving_japan_town`, `poc_driving_town`

- `town_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Default towns. ``"default"`` = road(30) → intersection → road(20) → crossing (railroad crossing) → road(20) → slope → road(20) → parallel_parking → road(30) (all 7 m wide; stop lines: 1 at the intersection and 1 at the railroad crossing). ``"short"`` = road(20) → crossing → road(20) (fast test gate). · examples: `poc_driving_town`
- `town_rules` `no input → table` GPU: none — Rule pack (a copy of :data:`RULE_PACKS`). ``{"jurisdiction", "side": "left"|"right", "crossing_stop": "always"|"when_active", "intersection_stop": "signal", "hold_s", "look_required", "look_hold_s", "sources": [...], "verified", "notes"}``. · examples: `poc_driving_town`

#### drive / traffic (18)
- `bus_stop_rate` `any → any` GPU: none — Emergence rate that is high ahead of and behind a stopped bus: λ(x) = base + peak [exp(−½((x − rear)/spread)²) + exp(−½((x − front)/spread)²)] [events/m]. An example of the pattern in which people come out from the bus's shadow (beyond its front end) and from behind it (the values are the caller's assumptions). The upper bound is base + 2·peak. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `driver_style` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns the parameters of 3 driving styles ("careful" / "normal" / "sloppy"). **All values are assumptions** (no source). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`

- `idm_equilibrium_gap` `any → any` GPU: none — Equilibrium gap of the IDM s_e(v) = (s0 + v T) / sqrt(1 − (v/v0)^δ) (0 ≤ v < v0). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `idm_platoon_simulate` `any → table` GPU: none — Integrates an IDM platoon of following vehicles behind the leader's speed profile (car 0 = leader, 1..n = following vehicles). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `importance_risk_estimate` `any → table` GPU: none — Makes accidents more likely with trials at a raised emergence rate (rate λ') and maps back to the accident probability at the original rate λ with likelihood-ratio weights. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `lateral_wobble` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Exact discretization of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process dX = −θ X dt + σ dW (a sequence of length n, step dt). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `occlusion_reveal_distance` `any → scalar` GPU: none — Longitudinal distance at which a point ``emerge_xy`` hidden behind a car parked at the roadside (an oriented box) becomes **visible for the first time** from the ego vehicle's eye. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `occlusion_safe_speed` `any → any` GPU: none — Maximum speed at which the car can stop within distance d from the moment of becoming visible: v = b(−ρ + sqrt(ρ² + 2d/b)). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `occlusion_visible_intervals` `any → any` GPU: none — While the ego vehicle's eye advances along p(s) = ego_xy + s h for 0 ≤ s ≤ s_max, the list of intervals of advance during which the point ``emerge_xy`` is **visible**. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `ou_estimate` `signal → table` GPU: none — Reads the parameters of lateral wander (an OU process with mean 0 dX = −θX dt + σ dW) from a sequence of observations at uniform spacing dt. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `passing_decision` `no input → any` GPU: none — Returns "go" or "wait" from the distance to the oncoming vehicle ``dist_oncoming`` (at decision time, when the ego vehicle is at x_in). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `passing_gap_required` `no input → table` GPU: none — Time needed to clear the section where the car swerves into the oncoming lane to pass a parked car, and the threshold distance at which the oncoming vehicle does not arrive before then (closed form). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `passing_simulate` `no input → table` GPU: none — Runs the "go" case forward in time and returns the PET (difference between the time the ego vehicle has fully returned from the oncoming lane and the time the oncoming vehicle reaches that point). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `pedestrian_crossing` `no input → table` GPU: none — Trajectory of a pedestrian whose crossing intention is the ground truth (closed form per segment; no integration). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `poisson_events` `any → signal` GPU: none — Draws 1 realization of an inhomogeneous Poisson process on [0, x_max] by thinning (Lewis & Shedler 1979) (an array of positions in ascending order). · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `poisson_events_xt` `any → any` GPU: none — Draws 1 realization of a space-time inhomogeneous Poisson process on [0, x_max] × [0, t_max] (rate λ(x, t) [events/(m·s)]) by thinning. · examples: `poc_driving_traffic`
- `social_force_step` `points × points × points → any` GPU: none — 1 step of the social force model (per unit mass; in the form of Helbing & Molnár 1995 / Helbing, Farkas, Vicsek 2000). · examples: `gallery_drive_mirrors_crowds`

- `os_sart_reconstruct` `projstack × ctgeometry → voxel` GPU: none — OS-SART: the SIRT update applied to one ordered subset of views at a time. · examples: `ct_scan_modes`, `poc_real_walnut_cbct`

- `hessian_determinant` `hessian → voxel` GPU: none — 3-D Hessian ``hessian`` → a volume of the determinant ``det H`` ``voxel`` (signed). The exit from ``hessian``. · examples: `hessian_numpy_chain`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `hessian_vesselness` `hessian → voxel` GPU: none — 3-D Hessian → Frangi vesselness ``voxel``, range [0, 1]. · examples: `hessian_numpy_chain`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `voxel_to_hessian` `voxel → hessian` GPU: none — Volume ``voxel`` → the six components (zz, yy, xx, zy, zx, yx) of the 3-D Hessian ``hessian``. The entry into ``hessian`` built with numpy and scipy only. · examples: `hessian_numpy_chain`

#### reprconv / descriptor (3)
- `descriptor_to_matrix` `descriptor → matrix` GPU: none — Descriptor → ``matrix``. The exit from ``descriptor`` (**invertible**). · examples: `representation_conversion`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `descriptor_to_table` `descriptor → table` GPU: none — Descriptor → a summary ``table``. **One-way.** · examples: `representation_conversion`
- `matrix_to_descriptor` `matrix → descriptor` GPU: none — ``matrix`` → descriptor. The inverse of :func:`descriptor_to_matrix`. · examples: `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / direction (3)
- `angles_to_normals` `pairs → normals` GPU: none — Azimuth/elevation pairs ``(N,2)`` **[deg]** → unit normals ``(N,3)``. The exit from ``pairs``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `normals_to_angles` `normals → pairs` GPU: none — Normals ``(N,3)`` → azimuth/elevation pairs ``(N,2)`` **[deg]**. The exit from ``normals``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `poc_tacscalib_sphere_lut`, `representation_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `normals_to_egi` `normals → image2d` GPU: none — Normals ``(N,3)`` → the extended Gaussian image, an ``image2d`` of ``(n_el, n_az)``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / entry (3)
- `indices_to_positions` `indices → positions` GPU: none — Indices ``indices`` → event positions ``positions`` (physical units). The entry into ``positions``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `jones_state` `no input → jones` GPU: none — Polarisation azimuth and ellipticity → a Jones vector ``jones`` (Ex, Ey). The entry into ``jones``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `synapse_table_from_table` `table → synapse_table` GPU: none — A table ``table`` (column name → array) → a synapse table ``synapse_table (m, 3)``. The entry into ``synapse_table``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`

#### reprconv / exit (3)
- `pairs_peak_x` `pairs → measurement` GPU: none — Pairs ``pairs (x, y)`` → the x where y peaks (parabolic interpolation between samples) ``measurement``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `pose_to_matrix` `pose → matrix` GPU: none — A rigid pose ``pose (R, t)`` → a 4×4 homogeneous transform ``matrix``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `tokens_to_matrix` `tokens → matrix` GPU: none — A token sequence ``tokens (T, d)`` → a general matrix ``matrix (T, d)``. The exit from ``tokens``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`

#### reprconv / field (4)
- `table_field_image2d` `table → image2d` GPU: none — One field of a table ``table`` → a 2-D image ``image2d``. The bridge from ops that return a ``table`` to ops that take images. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `table_field_matrix` `table → matrix` GPU: none — One field of a table ``table`` → a general matrix ``matrix``. Example: the ``swt`` field of ``swt_map`` → ``text_candidates``.
- `table_field_measurement` `table → measurement` GPU: none — One field of a table ``table`` → a single number ``measurement``. Example: ``width`` of ``label_extent``.
- `table_field_signal` `table → signal` GPU: none — One field of a table ``table`` → a 1-D array ``signal``. Hands a CSV column or a dict series to signal ops.

#### reprconv / flow (4)
- `flow_apply` `points × flow_scattered → points` GPU: none — Add a scattered flow ``(N,3)`` to a point set ``(N,3)`` → ``points``. The consuming side of ``flow``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`
- `flow_magnitude` `flow_dense → voxel` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Dense scene flow ``(3,D,H,W)`` → a speed volume ``voxel (D,H,W)``. The exit from ``flow``. · examples: `perception_on_video`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `flow_speed` `flow_scattered → signal` GPU: none — Scattered flow ``(N,3)`` → a speed ``signal (N,)``. The exit from scattered ``flow``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `flow_to_rgbimage` `flow_dense → rgbimage` GPU: none — One slice of a dense scene flow → an ``rgbimage`` with hue = direction and value = speed. · examples: `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / gaussians (3)
- `gaussians_to_points` `gaussians → points` GPU: none — ``gaussians`` → the point set of their centres ``(N,3)``. The exit from ``gaussians`` (**the centres are invertible**). · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `gaussians_to_voxel` `gaussians → voxel` GPU: none — ``gaussians`` → a density ``voxel (D,H,W)``. The second exit from ``gaussians``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `points_to_gaussians` `points → gaussians` GPU: none — A point set ``(N,3)`` → isotropic ``gaussians``. **The only entry into this type.** · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`

#### reprconv / index (3)
- `indices_to_labels` `indices → labels` GPU: none — Indices ``(N,)`` → a selection mask ``labels``. The exit from ``indices`` (**invertible**). · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`
- `labels_to_indices` `labels → indices` GPU: none — ``labels`` → the indices ``(N,)`` of the non-background. The other direction of :func:`indices_to_labels`. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`
- `select_points` `points × indices → points` GPU: none — A point set ``(N,3)`` and indices ``(M,)`` → the sub-set ``(M,3)``. The consuming side of ``indices``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / keypoint (8)
- `keypoints_from_image2d` `image2d → keypoints` GPU: yes (allow-list) — A count/response image ``(H, W)`` → image coordinates ``(N,2) = (u, v)``. The way back of the round trip. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `keypoints_rowcol_to_uv` `keypoints → keypoints` GPU: none — Image points ``(row, col)`` → ``(u, v) = (col, row)``. The bridge between the two conventions of the ``keypoints`` sort. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `keypoints_to_image2d` `keypoints → image2d` GPU: none — Image coordinates ``(N,2) = (u, v)`` → a count image ``(H, W)``. The second exit from ``keypoints``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `keypoints_uv_to_points` `keypoints → points` GPU: none — Image coordinates ``(N,2) = (u, v)`` → a point set ``(N,3) = (z, y, x)``. The exit from ``keypoints``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `keypoints_uv_to_rowcol` `keypoints → keypoints` GPU: none — Image points ``(u, v) = (col, row)`` → ``(row, col)``. The reverse of :func:`keypoints_rowcol_to_uv`. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`
- `points_to_position` `points → position` GPU: none — A point set ``(N,3)`` → its centroid ``(z, y, x)``. **Not invertible** (the distribution is thrown away). · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `points_zyx_to_keypoints_uv` `points → keypoints` GPU: none — A point set ``(N,3) = (z, y, x)`` → image coordinates ``(N,2) = (u, v)``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `position_to_points` `position → points` GPU: none — A position ``(z, y, x)`` → a one-point set ``(1, 3)``. The exit from ``position`` (**invertible**). · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / pairs (3)
- `pairs_to_image2d` `pairs → image2d` GPU: none — Pairs ``(N,2)`` → a scatter-density image ``(H, W)``. The third exit from ``pairs``. · examples: `representation_conversion`
- `pairs_to_signal` `pairs → signal` GPU: none — Pairs ``(N,2)`` → the dependent variable as a ``signal (N,)``. The second exit from ``pairs``. · examples: `representation_conversion`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `pairs_to_table` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Pairs ``(N,2)`` → a summary ``table``. **One-way.** · examples: `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / score (3)
- `correlation_score` `voxel × voxel → score` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Two ``voxel`` → a normalised cross-correlation ``score`` volume. **The only entry into this type.** · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `poc_leak_localization`, `representation_conversion`, `representation_roundtrip`
- `score_to_image2d` `score → image2d` GPU: none — A ``score`` volume → its maximum-intensity projection, an ``image2d``. The second exit from ``score``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`
- `score_to_position` `score → position` GPU: none — A ``score`` volume → the location of its maximum, ``position (z, y, x)``. The exit from ``score``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `representation_conversion`

#### reprconv / structure (4)
- `frame_axis` `frame → normals` GPU: none — Frenet frame ``frame`` → the unit vectors of one axis ``normals (N,3)``. The exit from ``frame``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `knn_graph_to_conn_graph` `graph → conn_graph` GPU: none — k-nearest-neighbour graph ``graph`` → a weighted adjacency matrix ``conn_graph (n, n)``. The exit from ``graph``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `match_component` `match → measurement` GPU: none — The ``match`` sort (a 1-D result vector) → one of its components as a ``measurement``. The exit from ``match``. · examples: `type_connectivity_tour`
- `pointmap_to_points` `pointmap → points` GPU: none — Grid-organised 3-D points ``pointmap (H,W,3)`` → a point cloud ``points (N,3)``. The exit from ``pointmap``. · examples: `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`

### fileio (28 ops / 10 categories)

#### fileio / archive (4)
- `archive_create` `any × text → any` GPU: none — Create deterministic archive `bytes` from paths or named content. · examples: `archive_roundtrip`
- `archive_extract` `any × text → any` GPU: none — Safely extract an archive into an empty destination and return relative paths. · examples: `archive_roundtrip`
- `archive_list` `any → table` GPU: none — List archive member names, expanded and compressed sizes, modification times, and directory flags. · examples: `archive_roundtrip`
- `archive_probe` `any → text` GPU: none — Probe archive magic and return its format name. · examples: `archive_roundtrip`

#### fileio / e57 (2)
