- `e57_write` `table → any` GPU: none — Write a point-cloud `table` with coordinates, intensity, color, and pose as ASTM E57 `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`

#### fileio / fits (2)
- `astro_fits_read` `any → any` GPU: none — Read a primary-HDU 2-D/3-D FITS image as `(image_or_volume, meta)`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`, `poc_real_file_formats`
- `astro_fits_write` `any → any` GPU: none — Write a 2-D/3-D astronomical image and basic WCS as primary-HDU FITS `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`

#### fileio / mesh (8)
- `mesh_read_obj` `text → mesh` GPU: none — Read Wavefront OBJ `v` and `f` records (including `v//vn`) and return a triangle `mesh`.
- `mesh_read_off` `text → mesh` GPU: none — Read Geomview OFF and return a triangle `mesh` `(vertices, faces)`.
- `mesh_read_ply` `any → table` GPU: none — Read ASCII or binary PLY and return a `table` of vertices, faces, colors, normals, and scalar attributes. · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`
- `mesh_read_stl` `any → mesh` GPU: none — Read ASCII or little-endian binary STL and return a shared-vertex `mesh` `(vertices, faces)`.
- `mesh_write_obj` `mesh → text` GPU: none — Write a triangle mesh as a Wavefront OBJ string containing `v`, `vn`, and `f` (`text`).
- `mesh_write_off` `mesh → text` GPU: none — Write a triangle mesh as a Geomview OFF string (`text`).
- `mesh_write_ply` `table → any` GPU: none — Write vertices, faces, colors, normals, and arbitrary scalar attributes as ASCII or little-endian PLY (`text` / `bytes`). · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`
- `mesh_write_stl` `mesh → any` GPU: none — Write a triangle mesh as ASCII or little-endian binary STL (`text` / `bytes`).

#### fileio / mrc (2)
- `em_mrc_read` `any → any` GPU: none — Read MRC2014/CCP4 mode 0/1/2/6 as `(image_or_volume, meta)`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`, `poc_real_file_formats`
- `em_mrc_write` `any → any` GPU: none — Write 2-D/3-D electron-microscopy data as MRC2014/CCP4 `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`

#### fileio / nifti (2)
- `nifti_read` `any → any` GPU: none — Read single-file NIfTI-1 (`.nii` / `.nii.gz`) as `(array, meta)`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`, `poc_real_file_formats`
- `nifti_write` `any → any` GPU: none — Write a 3-D/4-D array with affine/pixdim as single-file NIfTI-1 `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`

#### fileio / nrrd (2)
- `nrrd_read` `any → any` GPU: none — Read raw/gzip NRRD as `(array, meta)` with explicit spatial units. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`
- `nrrd_write` `any → any` GPU: none — Write a multidimensional array and `space directions` as raw/gzip NRRD `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`

#### fileio / ome_tiff (2)
- `ome_tiff_read` `any → any` GPU: none — Read OME-TIFF as `(stack, meta)` and cross-check OME-XML against the array. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`, `poc_real_file_formats`
- `ome_tiff_write` `any → any` GPU: none — Write a TCZYX multidimensional array with physical sizes and channel names as OME-TIFF `bytes`. · examples: `fileio_scientific_roundtrip`

#### fileio / points (2)
- `points_read_xyz` `text → points` GPU: none — Read whitespace-delimited XYZ text and return `(N,3)` `points`. · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`
- `points_write_xyz` `points → text` GPU: none — Write finite `(N,3)` points as 17-digit XYZ text (`text`). · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`

#### fileio / table (2)
- `table_read_csv` `text → table` GPU: none — Reads the unit-aware CSV produced by :func:`table_write_csv` and returns a ``table`` containing columns, units, and metadata. · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `table_write_csv` `table → text` GPU: none — Writes a table with units and provenance as CSV text readable by pandas and MATLAB (``text``). · examples: `fileio_roundtrip`

### cadmap (4 ops / 4 categories)

#### cadmap / defect (1)
- `cad_defect_to_cad` `mesh × labels → table` GPU: none — 2-D defect label image → a **table on the CAD surface** (face ID / area on the face / 3-D centroid). · examples: `defect_to_cad`

#### cadmap / project (1)

### annotate (51 ops / 8 categories)

#### annotate / compose (3)
- `compare_frame` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Put two images side by side, with a **divider** and **labels** at the boundary. · examples: `annotate_gallery`
- `panel_grid` `image2d → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Lay panels out on a grid, with a label strip under each frame (montage / contact sheet). · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `annotate_paper_tour`
- `zoom_inset` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — A magnified inset — adds a **frame** and a **leader line** to the original figure. · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_diabolo_model_and_vision`, `poc_food_cutting_measure`

#### annotate / furniture (3)
- `color_bar` `image2d × lut → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — The legend of a LUT (a colour bar), labelled with its minimum, maximum and unit. · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_cad_scan_deviation`, `poc_ct_void_morphology`, `poc_dem_terrain`, `poc_interferometry_step`, `poc_lidar_terrain_change`, `poc_lightfield_depth`, `poc_multibeam_bathymetry`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `poc_stockpile_volume`, `poc_thermography_ndt`
- `legend_box` `image2d × entries → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — A legend of colours against descriptions. **The box height follows in closed form from the number of entries.** · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_driving_decisions`, `poc_measurement_system_analysis`, `poc_moire_alignment`, `poc_pxrd_phase_peel`, `poc_real_tless_6dof`
- `scale_bar` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — A scale bar in physical length. **The pixel↔physical conversion is taken as an argument** (never assumed). · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`

#### annotate / overlay (5)
- `annotate_invert` `image2d × mask → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Fills / outlines a region in **inverted color**. · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`
- `annotate_invert_path` `image2d × pairs → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Draws a polyline (line) in **inverted color**. Anti-aliased. · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`
- `annotate_invert_visibility` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Measures, before drawing, whether the inverted color is **actually visible on that background**. · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`
- `overlay_labels` `image2d × labels → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Overlay a colour label map with alpha. **The same label number always gets the same colour.** · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_mri_bias_field`, `poc_recycling_sorting`
- `overlay_mask` `image2d × mask → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Overlay a binary mask with alpha. **Exactly ``a*f + (1-a)*b``.** · examples: `annotate_gallery`, `poc_kendama`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`

#### annotate / paper (23)
- `annotate_angle` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): the angle at three points, shown as an arc and a value (with the two arms if wanted). · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_angle_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the arc and text position for the (smaller) angle at ``a, vertex, b``. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_colorbar` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a scalar field colour-mapped through a LUT and overlaid, with a colour bar. · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_thin_film_reflectometry`
- `annotate_dimension` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a dimension line (arrowheads at both ends, extension lines, value and unit). · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_dimension_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the geometry of a dimension line (line, extension lines, text position) in closed form. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_figure_grid` `images → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): images plus captions laid out as one figure (constant margins, panel letters). · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_flybrain_pointcloud`, `poc_itof_multifreq`, `poc_pixel_shift`
- `annotate_figure_grid_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the typesetting of a multi-panel figure (cell, panel and caption-band rectangles) in closed form. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_inset` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Returns an image (image2d): a magnified inset in a corner, with lines joining the matching corners. · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_real_defect_floor`
- `annotate_inset_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): where the magnified inset goes and at what factor, in closed form. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_leader` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): an elbowed leader line plus text (collision-avoiding across several points). · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_leader_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the placement of leader lines (elbow, text position, plate rectangle) in closed form. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_legend` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a legend of numbered round markers against their descriptions (the partner of :func:`annotate_markers`). · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_real_defect_floor`
- `annotate_markers` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a round marker carrying a number (or a short string) at each point. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_orientation` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): an arrow plus text showing a bearing (north) or an orientation. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_outline` `image2d × mask → image2d` GPU: none — Returns an image (image2d): the outline of a mask as an (anti-aliased) closed polyline, with text at the centroid. · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_rotation_invariance_audit`
- `annotate_outline_layout` `mask → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the boundary loops of a binary mask (closed polygons along pixel edges) and its centroid. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_panel_label` `image2d → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a panel letter ``(a)``/``(b)`` placed in a corner. · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`
- `annotate_scale_bar` `image2d → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): a scale bar of a round length placed in a corner (with value and unit). · examples: `paper_figure`, `poc_flybrain_pointcloud`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`
- `annotate_scale_bar_layout` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): a bar of a **round** length, at most ``target_fraction`` of the image width. · examples: `paper_figure`
- `annotate_table` `image2d × text → image2d` GPU: none — Returns an image (image2d): draws a tab-separated string as a **table** (with a semi-transparent backing panel). · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`, `poc_rotation_invariance_audit`
- `annotate_table_layout` `text → table` GPU: none — Returns a table (dict): the column and row positions at which a tab-separated string is placed as a **table**. · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`
- `annotate_text_path` `image2d × text → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Returns an image (image2d): text set along a polyline (each glyph rotated to the tangent angle). · examples: `annotate_paper_tour`, `paper_figure`

### gfx2d (44 ops / 9 categories)

#### gfx2d / camera (1)
- `viewport` `rgb → rgb` GPU: none — Crop the rectangle at ``(x, y, width, height)`` and resample it by ``scale``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`, `omni360_roundtrip`

#### gfx2d / colorspace (2)
- `linear_to_srgb` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Linear light back to sRGB encoding. Exact inverse of :func:`srgb_to_linear`. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_pigment_unmixing`, `poc_white_balance`
- `srgb_to_linear` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — sRGB-encoded values to linear light (IEC 61966-2-1). · examples: `gfx2d_scene`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_mixed_case_depalletizing`

#### gfx2d / composite (6)
- `alpha_composite` `rgba × rgba → rgba` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Porter–Duff **over** on straight-alpha ``rgba`` (Porter & Duff 1984). · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `alpha_composite_premul` `rgba_premul × rgba_premul → rgba_premul` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Porter–Duff **over** on premultiplied colour: ``src + dst*(1 - src.a)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `blend_mode` `rgb × rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Blend two opaque ``rgb`` images with a named mode (W3C Level 1). · examples: `genspark_external_review`, `gfx2d_scene`
- `layer_stack` `table → rgba` GPU: none — Composite a z-ordered list of ``rgba`` layers, bottom first. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `premultiply` `rgba → rgba_premul` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Straight-alpha ``rgba`` to **premultiplied** ``rgba``: ``(C*A, A)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `unpremultiply` `rgba_premul → rgba` GPU: none — **Premultiplied** ``rgba`` back to straight alpha: ``(C/A, A)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`

#### gfx2d / isp (12)
- `awb_gains` `rgb → vector` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Estimate white-balance gains ``(g_R, g_G, g_B)`` with ``g_G = 1``. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `brightness_contrast` `rgb → rgb` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — ``out = (rgb - 0.5) * contrast + 0.5 + brightness``, clipped to ``[0, 1]``. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `color_correction_matrix` `rgb × matrix → rgb` GPU: none — Apply a 3x3 colour-correction matrix: ``out = rgb @ ccm.T`` per pixel, clipped to ``[0, 1]``. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `hue_saturation` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Rotate the hue by *hue_deg* and scale the saturation by *saturation*, in BT.601 YCbCr: luma is kept, the chroma vector ``(Cb, Cr)`` is rotated and scaled. Output clipped to ``[0, 1]``. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `lens_shading_correct` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Multiply a frame by a lens-shading gain map and clip to ``[0, 1]``. *raw* and *gain* must have the same shape; the gain must be finite and > 0. · examples: `poc_tdi_linescan`, `raw_to_display_isp`
- `lens_shading_gain` `image2d → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — The gain map that flattens a **flat-field** frame: ``gain = mean / flat`` per colour channel (or for the whole frame when *pattern* is ``None``). · examples: `poc_tdi_linescan`, `raw_to_display_isp`
- `raw_apply_gains` `image2d × vector → image2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Multiply a Bayer frame by per-channel gains (3 values ``R, G, B`` or 4 values ``R, G1, G2, B``) and clip to ``[0, 1]`` — white balance applied **before** demosaicing, which is where a real ISP does it (interpolating unbalanced channels smears the cast across colours). · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `raw_black_level` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Black-level compensation on a Bayer frame: ``(raw - offset) / (white - offset)`` per colour channel, clipped to ``[0, 1]``. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `raw_dead_pixel_correct` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Replace every dead pixel (:func:`raw_dead_pixel_mask`) by the **median of its 8 same-colour neighbours**; every other pixel is returned bit-for-bit. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `raw_dead_pixel_mask` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Where the dead (stuck / hot) pixels are: ``1.0`` at a pixel that differs from **every one** of its 8 same-colour neighbours by more than *threshold* in the same direction, ``0.0`` elsewhere. ``(H, W)`` float64. · examples: `raw_to_display_isp`
- `raw_demosaic_bilinear` `image2d → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Bayer mosaic → ``(H, W, 3)`` RGB by bilinear interpolation, in NumPy. · examples: `poc_pixel_shift`, `raw_to_display_isp`
- `rgb_apply_gains` `rgb × vector → rgb` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Multiply the R, G, B channels by ``gains`` (3 values) and clip to ``[0, 1]``. · examples: `gallery_mesh_seg_sun_gains`

#### gfx2d / light (5)
- `light_mask` `rgb × rgb → rgb` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Modulate an ``rgb`` image by an ``rgb`` light map: ``base * (ambient + light)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `normal_map_decode` `rgb → normalmap` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Tangent-space normal map ``rgb`` in ``[0, 1]`` to unit vectors ``(H, W, 3)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `normal_map_shade` `normalmap → rgb` GPU: none — Shade a 2-D normal map with one directional light (Lambert + Blinn 1977). · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `radial_light` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — A radial light map, ``rgb`` ``(H, W, 3)``, centred on ``(x, y)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `shadow_cast_2d` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Visibility of every pixel from a point light at ``(x, y)``, as ``image2d``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`

#### gfx2d / particle (3)
- `particle_emit` `no input → table` GPU: none — Emit ``count`` particles from ``origin``, deterministically from ``seed``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `particle_render` `table → rgba` GPU: none — Splat a particle state into an ``rgba`` image. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `particle_step` `table → table` GPU: none — Advance a particle state by ``dt`` seconds. Returns a **new** dict. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`

#### gfx2d / post (8)
- `bloom` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Bleed the bright parts of an image into their neighbourhood. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`, `poc_public_camera_heading_real`
- `chromatic_aberration` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Scale the red and blue channels about the image centre, green fixed. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `color_grade` `rgb × lut → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Apply a 3-D colour LUT to an ``rgb`` image by trilinear interpolation. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `color_lut` `no input → lut` GPU: none — Build a 3-D colour LUT, ``(n, n, n, 3)`` indexed ``[r, g, b]``. · examples: `genspark_external_review`, `gfx2d_scene`
- `dither` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Quantise to ``levels`` values per channel while preserving the local mean. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `film_grain` `rgb → rgb` GPU: none — Add zero-mean Gaussian grain, deterministically from ``seed``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `palette_quantize` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Map every pixel to its nearest palette colour in Euclidean RGB. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `vignette` `rgb → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Darken towards the corners: ``out = rgb * (1 - strength * t**power)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`, `poc_search_sweep_width`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`

#### gfx2d / sprite (5)
- `nine_slice` `rgba → rgba` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Stretch a frame to a new size without deforming its corners. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `sprite_blit` `rgba × rgba → rgba` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Composite ``sprite`` onto a copy of ``dst`` at integer ``(x, y)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `sprite_sheet_slice` `rgba → sprites` GPU: none — Cut a sprite atlas into a list of equal ``rgba`` frames, row-major. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `sprite_synthesize` `no input → rgba` GPU: none — A deterministic anti-aliased test sprite, ``rgba`` ``(size, size, 4)``. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `sprite_transform` `rgba → rgba` GPU: none — Rotate and/or scale an ``rgba`` sprite about its centre. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`

#### gfx2d / tile (2)
- `parallax_layers` `sprites → rgba` GPU: none — Scroll a set of ``rgba`` layers at different rates and composite them. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`
- `tilemap_render` `sprites → rgba` GPU: none — Paint a grid of tile indices into one ``rgba`` image. · examples: `gfx2d_scene`

### multivar (18 ops / 6 categories)

#### multivar / analysis (4)
- `doe_main_effects` `design × signal → table` GPU: none — Level means per factor — the response table of a designed experiment — with dispersion and SN. · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`
- `mv_pca` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Principal components of a table (samples x variables) and how many of them the data support. · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`
- `mv_pls` `matrix × signal → table` GPU: none — Partial least squares regression of Y on X with cross-validated Q^2, the Q^2 rule and VIP. · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`
- `rsm_fit` `design × signal → table` GPU: none — Fit a response surface on a ``design`` (coded units): ANOVA, lack of fit, stationary point. · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`

#### multivar / coding (2)
- `doe_decode` `design → matrix` GPU: none — ``design`` -> natural-unit matrix (n, k); or decode any coded point(s) with its ranges. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`, `multivar_inspection_tour`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `sensitivity_tour`
- `doe_encode` `matrix → design` GPU: none — Natural-unit settings (n, k) -> ``design`` with coded values (−1..+1 = lo..hi). · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`

#### multivar / features (1)
- `feat_image_vector` `images → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Images -> feature table ``{"matrix" (N, F), "names", "units", ...}``, one row per image. · examples: `multivar_inspection_tour`

#### multivar / identifiability (2)
- `mv_confounding` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Collinearity index gamma_K (Brun, Reichert & Künsch 2001): which parameters the data can fix. · examples: `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `sensitivity_tour`
- `mv_residual_pca` `matrix → table` GPU: none — Do the residuals of a fitted model still carry structure? PCA of a residual matrix vs. noise. · examples: `sensitivity_tour`

#### multivar / plan (5)
- `doe_box_behnken` `no input → design` GPU: none — Box-Behnken design (Box & Behnken 1960) for 3, 4 or 5 factors -> ``design``. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`
- `doe_central_composite` `no input → design` GPU: none — Central composite design (Box & Wilson 1951) -> ``design``. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`, `multivar_inspection_tour`
- `doe_fractional_factorial` `no input → design` GPU: none — Regular two-level fractional factorial 2^(k-p) from generators (Box & Hunter 1961) -> ``design``. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`
- `doe_lhs` `no input → design` GPU: none — Latin hypercube design (McKay, Beckman & Conover 1979) -> ``design``. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`, `multivar_inspection_tour`, `sensitivity_tour`, `simcal_checks_tour`
- `doe_orthogonal_array` `no input → design` GPU: none — Orthogonal array L4 / L8 / L9 / L12 / L16 / L18 / L27 from a published table -> ``design``. · examples: `doe_plan_tour`, `multivar_inspection_tour`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`

#### multivar / sensitivity (4)
- `doe_morris` `no input → design` GPU: none — Morris one-at-a-time screening plan: ``r`` trajectories of k+1 runs -> ``design``. · examples: `sensitivity_tour`
- `doe_saltelli` `no input → design` GPU: none — Sample matrices for Sobol' indices (Saltelli et al. 2010) -> ``design`` of n (k + 2) runs. · examples: `sensitivity_tour`
- `sens_morris` `design × signal → table` GPU: none — Morris elementary effects -> mu, mu*, sigma per factor (Morris 1991; mu* Campolongo et al. 2007). · examples: `sensitivity_tour`
- `sens_sobol` `design × signal → table` GPU: none — First-order and total Sobol' indices with bootstrap confidence intervals. · examples: `sensitivity_tour`

### simcal (10 ops / 4 categories)

#### simcal / check (4)
- `simcal_discrepancy` `calresult → calresult` GPU: none — Is there structure in the noise-normalised residuals that the model cannot produce (model discrepancy)? · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`
- `simcal_identifiability` `calresult → calresult` GPU: none — Fisher information, Cramér-Rao bound, correlations, collinearity and profile likelihood of every fitted knob. · examples: `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`
- `simcal_uncertainty` `calresult → calresult` GPU: none — Standard deviations and intervals of the determined knobs: Laplace (inverse Fisher) or parametric bootstrap. · examples: `poc_simcal_thin_film`
- `simcal_validate` `calresult × simmodel → calresult` GPU: none — Over-fitting gates on held-out images; any one failing rejects the calibration (the estimates are withdrawn). · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`

#### simcal / fit (2)
- `simcal_fit` `simmodel → calresult` GPU: none — Fit the free knobs of an observed simmodel to its images (weighted least squares) -> ``calresult``. · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`, `simcal_tour`
- `simcal_screen` `simmodel → table` GPU: none — Which knobs move the images above the camera noise, which are confounded, and how many output directions exist. · examples: `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_tour`

#### simcal / model (3)
- `simcal_model` `no input → simmodel` GPU: none — Build a ``simmodel``: a forward chain of ops whose arguments are knobs with units, ranges and a noise model. · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`, `simcal_tour`
- `simcal_observe` `simmodel × images → simmodel` GPU: none — Attach measured images to a simmodel: alignment, region of interest and exposure normalisation. · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_telecentric`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`, `simcal_tour`
- `simcal_simulate` `simmodel → images` GPU: none — Run a simmodel's chain at given knob values -> one 2-D array per condition (``images``). · examples: `poc_pocket_interreflection`, `poc_simcal_pixel_shift`, `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`, `simcal_tour`

#### simcal / report (1)
- `simcal_report` `calresult → table` GPU: none — One table of a calibration: each knob's value, unit, interval and class, the gates, and the reasons for refusals. · examples: `poc_simcal_thin_film`, `simcal_checks_tour`

### converge (6 ops / 4 categories)

#### converge / iterate (1)
- `iterate_fixed_point` `no input → table` GPU: none — Solve x = g(x) by fixed-point iteration (plain / Aitken / Anderson) and refuse if it does not converge. · examples: `converge_tour`

#### converge / montecarlo (2)
- `mc_photon_slab` `no input → table` GPU: none — Diffuse reflectance, total transmittance and absorption of a layered turbid slab by MCML-type Monte Carlo, with confidence intervals. · examples: `converge_tour`
- `mc_sequential_mean` `no input → table` GPU: none — Sequential Monte Carlo mean: add samples until the confidence interval is narrower than the tolerance.

#### converge / stopping (1)
- `iv_richardson_lucy_until` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Richardson-Lucy deconvolution stopped by the discrepancy principle (Poisson: Bertero 2010, tau = 1; Gaussian: Morozov); refuses data outside the model's range. · examples: `converge_tour`

#### converge / verification (2)
- `conv_gci` `no input → table` GPU: none — Grid convergence index of the finest solution: Celik et al. 2008 procedure, eqs. (1)-(7). · examples: `converge_tour`
- `conv_observed_order` `no input → table` GPU: none — Apparent order of convergence p from three systematically refined solutions (Celik et al. 2008, eq. 3).

### codematch (6 ops / 3 categories)

#### codematch / change (1)
- `radial_reach_filter` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Radial Reach Filter (RRF): compares a background and the current image by the signs of the reaches in 8 directions. · examples: `poc_code_matching_breakdown`

#### codematch / code (2)
- `increment_sign` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Sign of the increment to the neighbouring pixel, ``b = [I(next) >= I(this)]`` (uint8 1 / 0).
- `orientation_code` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Orientation-code image: gradient direction quantised into ``n_codes`` steps (the OCM coding).

#### codematch / match (3)
- `isc_match` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Increment sign correlation (ISC): returns the position where the largest fraction of increment signs agree. · examples: `poc_code_matching_breakdown`
- `ocm_match` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Orientation code matching (OCM): returns the position with the smallest mean cyclic code difference. · examples: `poc_code_matching_breakdown`
- `scc_match` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Selective correlation coefficient (SCC): normalised correlation over only the pixels whose increment signs agree. · examples: `poc_code_matching_breakdown`

### aoi (8 ops / 4 categories)

#### aoi / aggregate (1)
- `tiled_map` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Splits an image into tiles and turns a per-tile quantity into a small map. → dict. · examples: `aoi_frontend_tour`

#### aoi / geometric (1)
- `register_image` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Returns the translation that aligns an inspection image to a reference image, together with quantities that reveal when it does not fit. → dict. · examples: `aoi_frontend_tour`, `poc_multimodal_mi_registration`

#### aoi / photometric (1)
- `flat_field_correct` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Undoes uneven illumination and sensor-sensitivity variation by a dark-subtracted division. → corrected image. · examples: `aoi_frontend_tour`

#### aoi / symmetry (5)
- `center_from_symmetric_edges` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Robustly pools the midpoints of symmetric outer-edge pairs and returns a 2-D centre. · examples: `poc_symmetry_self_reference_inspection`
- `reflection_axis` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Estimates the angle and offset of the reflection axis of a line-symmetric 2-D image.
- `rotational_symmetry` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Returns the 180-degree point-symmetry centre and the rotational order from polar autocorrelation. · examples: `poc_symmetry_self_reference_inspection`
- `symmetry_difference_map` `image2d × table → image2d` GPU: none — Returns a self-referenced difference map against an estimated reflection axis or rotation centre. · examples: `poc_symmetry_self_reference_inspection`
- `symmetry_score` `image2d × table → measurement` GPU: none — Returns distance from symmetry by normalising the self-referenced difference by image dynamic range. · examples: `poc_symmetry_self_reference_inspection`

### matchreg (12 ops / 2 categories)

#### matchreg / featmatch (6)
- `features_accuracy_table` `image2d → table` GPU: none — On pairs synthesised with known transforms, returns keypoint repeatability, matching precision and homography error per condition as a table. → table. · examples: `poc_part_locate_features`
- `features_match` `table × table → table` GPU: none — Matches two feature tables by nearest neighbour + ratio test (+ mutual nearest neighbour). → table (``kind="feature_matches"``). · examples: `poc_part_locate_features`
- `features_orb` `image2d → table` GPU: none — ORB keypoints and 256-bit binary descriptors (Rublee et al. 2011). → table (``kind="features"``). · examples: `poc_part_locate_features`
- `features_sift` `image2d → table` GPU: none — SIFT keypoints and 128-dimensional descriptors (DoG extrema, Lowe 2004). → table (``kind="features"``). · examples: `poc_part_locate_features`
- `ransac_fundamental` `table → table` GPU: none — Robustly estimates the fundamental matrix F (``x2ᵀ F x1 = 0``) from matched pairs. → table (``kind="fundamental"``).
- `ransac_homography` `table → table` GPU: none — Robustly estimates a homography (pts1 → pts2, homogeneous (x, y)) from matched pairs. → table (``kind="homography"``). · examples: `poc_part_locate_features`

#### matchreg / intensityreg (6)
- `register_accuracy_map` `image2d × flow2d → table` GPU: none — On a pair synthesised with a known deformation field, returns the per-pixel error of the estimated field (an accuracy map). → table. · examples: `poc_sheet_deformation_ffd`
- `register_capture_range` `image2d → table` GPU: none — For each size of initial misalignment, returns the fraction of registrations started from the identity that return to the truth (the capture range). → table.
- `register_ecc` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Aligns moving to fixed with the parametric transform that maximises the enhanced correlation coefficient (ECC). → table (``kind="registration"``). · examples: `poc_multimodal_mi_registration`
- `register_ffd` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Non-rigidly aligns moving to fixed with a cubic B-spline free-form deformation (FFD). → table (``kind="registration"``). · examples: `poc_sheet_deformation_ffd`
- `register_mi` `image2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — Aligns moving to fixed with the rigid / similarity / affine transform that maximises (normalised) mutual information. → table (``kind="registration"``). · examples: `poc_multimodal_mi_registration`
- `registration_to_flow2d` `table → flow2d` GPU: none — Extracts the deformation field ``flow2d`` ((2,H,W) ``(dy, dx)``) from a registration result table. → flow2d. · examples: `poc_sheet_deformation_ffd`

### calib (29 ops / 7 categories)

#### calib / calib_truth (3)
- `calibration_error_map` `table → table` GPU: none — Compares the true K and distortion with the estimate and returns a map of where in the image the reprojection error (px) and 3-D error (mm) are large (``table``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`
- `calibration_next_pose` `table → table` GPU: none — Recommends, among candidate board poses, the one view that would reduce the calibration uncertainty (mean over the image) the most (``table``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`
- `calibration_uncertainty_map` `table → table` GPU: none — Maps the covariance of the calibration estimate onto the image and returns the predicted uncertainty of every pixel (px, or mm at depth Z) (``table``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`

#### calib / calibrate (5)
- `camera_calibration` (halcon: `camera_calibration`) `keypoints → table` GPU: none — [Partial] Estimates only the intrinsic matrix K from several views of a planar target by Zhang's method (camera_calibration). · examples: `camera_intrinsics_calibration`, `lens_calibration_loop_demo`, `poc_calibration_truth_map`, `poc_camera_calibration`
- `camera_calibration_lm` `keypoints → table` GPU: none — Jointly refines intrinsics, distortion and all poses by LM from Zhang's initial estimate and returns them with their covariance (``table``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`, `poc_real_chessboard_undistort`
- `find_marks_and_pose` (halcon: `find_marks_and_pose`) `image2d → table` GPU: none — Mark detection + pose estimation of the calibration plate (plane homography → pose) (find_marks_and_pose).
- `hand_eye_calibration` (halcon: `hand_eye_calibration`) `no input → matrix` GPU: none — Solves AX=XB from a series of motion pairs and estimates X (4x4) (hand_eye_calibration).
- `stereo_calibration_lm` `keypoints → table` GPU: none — Jointly refines both cameras' intrinsics and distortion, the board poses and the right camera's relative pose (R, T) by LM (``table``).

#### calib / checkerboard (3)
- `checkerboard_points` `no input → keypoints` GPU: none — Returns the board coordinates (x, y) of the inner corners of a checkerboard in row-major order (``keypoints``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`
- `find_checkerboard_corners` `image2d → keypoints` GPU: none — Detects the inner corners of a checkerboard image to sub-pixel accuracy and returns them in the board's row-major order (``keypoints``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`
- `sim_checkerboard` `no input → table` GPU: none — Synthesizes a checkerboard image with known K, distortion and pose and returns it with the true pixel of every corner (``table``). · examples: `poc_calibration_truth_map`

#### calib / fit (4)
- `hom_vector_to_proj_hom_mat2d` (halcon: `hom_vector_to_proj_hom_mat2d`) `keypoints → matrix` GPU: none — Finds a 3x3 projective transform (homography, DLT) from 4 or more correspondences (hom_vector_to_proj_hom_mat2d). · examples: `poc_panorama_drift`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`
- `vector_angle_to_rigid` (halcon: `vector_angle_to_rigid`) `no input → matrix` GPU: none — Finds a 2-D rigid transform from one pair of (point, angle) (vector_angle_to_rigid).
- `vector_to_rigid` (halcon: `vector_to_rigid`) `keypoints → matrix` GPU: none — Finds a 2-D rigid transform (rotation + translation, Kabsch) from point correspondences (vector_to_rigid).
- `vector_to_similarity` (halcon: `vector_to_similarity`) `keypoints → matrix` GPU: none — Finds a 2-D similarity transform (rotation + scale + translation, Umeyama) from point correspondences (vector_to_similarity). · examples: `poc_document_scan`, `poc_star_astrometry`

#### calib / plane (5)
- `contour_to_world_plane_xld` (halcon: `contour_to_world_plane_xld`) `table → table` GPU: none — Maps an XLD contour (dict {cs:[Nx2]}) to the world plane (contour_to_world_plane_xld). · examples: `poc_wound_area_tracking`
- `gen_image_to_world_plane_map` (halcon: `gen_image_to_world_plane_map`) `no input → table` GPU: none — Builds the image → world plane (z=0) mapping table (gen_image_to_world_plane_map).
- `gen_radial_distortion_map` (halcon: `gen_radial_distortion_map`) `no input → table` GPU: none — Builds the inverse map (row_map, col_map) of a radial distortion (gen_radial_distortion_map).
- `image_points_to_world_plane` (halcon: `image_points_to_world_plane`) `table → keypoints` GPU: none — Back-projects pixels onto the world plane z=0 from the camera intrinsics and extrinsics (image_points_to_world_plane).
- `image_to_world_plane` `keypoints → keypoints` GPU: none — Maps image points to the world plane (z=0) with a plane homography (image_to_world_plane). · examples: `poc_document_scan`, `poc_matrix_code_reading`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`

#### calib / project (3)
- `project_3d_point` (halcon: `project_3d_point`) `points → keypoints` GPU: none — Perspective-projects 3-D points into the camera and returns pixels (row, col) (project_3d_point).

- `project_point_hom_mat3d` (halcon: `project_point_hom_mat3d`) `points → keypoints` GPU: none — Projects 3-D points with a 4x4 or 3x4 projection matrix P=K[R|t] and returns pixels (row, col) (project_point_hom_mat3d).

- `caltab_points` (halcon: `caltab_points`) `no input → keypoints` GPU: none — Returns the ideal mark coordinates of a calibration plate (world, mm; origin = first mark) as (y, x) (caltab_points).
- `create_caltab` (halcon: `create_caltab`) `no input → table` GPU: none — Creates a calibration-plate description (ideal points, origin at the plate centre) (create_caltab).

### generative (42 ops / 6 categories)

#### generative / illusion (13)
- `illusion_cafe_wall` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Café wall illusion. Although **the mortar lines are exactly horizontal**, they look tilted. · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`
- `illusion_checker_shadow` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Checker shadow. **The 2 marked squares have exactly the same pixel value**. · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_ebbinghaus` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Ebbinghaus illusion. **The 2 central circles have exactly the same radius**. · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`
- `illusion_fraser_spiral` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Fraser illusion. **It looks like a spiral, but is actually concentric circles**. · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_ground_truth` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns, as a table, the **exact invariants** that the illusions preserve (empty ``name`` gives all of them). · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`
- `illusion_hermann_grid` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Hermann grid. **The intersections are exactly the same white as everywhere else** (the dark spots are made by the eye). · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_kanizsa` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Kanizsa triangle. A triangle is seen although **not even 1 contour line is drawn**. · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_muller_lyer` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Müller-Lyer illusion. **The 2 shafts are exactly equal in length**. · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `illusion_poggendorff` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Poggendorff illusion. **The oblique line is exactly 1 straight line** (it is merely hidden by the band). · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`
- `illusion_ponzo` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Ponzo illusion. **The 2 horizontal bars are exactly equal in length** (perspective cues change the length). · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_scintillating_grid` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Scintillating grid. A Hermann grid with white discs placed at the intersections. · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_simultaneous_contrast` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Simultaneous contrast. **The 2 gray patches have exactly the same value** (only their surroundings differ). · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `illusion_zollner` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Zöllner illusion. Although **the long lines are exactly parallel**, they appear to converge. · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`

#### generative / loop (2)
- `perpetual_loop` `no input → rgbvideo` GPU: none — Creates a **seamless looping video** → ``rgbvideo`` (T,H,W,3). · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`, `poc_periodic_video_boundary`
- `perpetual_loop_seam` `rgbvideo → table` GPU: none — Quantifies the **seam** of a looping video as numbers (``table``). · examples: `poc_endless_zoom_and_turning_solids`, `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`, `poc_periodic_video_boundary`

#### generative / perpetual (12)
- `perpetual_apollonian` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Apollonian circle packing — keeps inserting circles tangent to the gaps (it never ends). · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_chaos_game` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Chaos game — just rolling a die and moving halfway each time produces the Sierpiński triangle. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_elementary_ca` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Elementary cellular automaton (Wolfram's 256 rules), extended endlessly from top to bottom. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_flow_field` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Flow field — keeps advecting particles along the field (it does not end unless stopped). · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_harmonograph` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Harmonograph — 2 damped pendulums keep drawing a curve that never closes. · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `perpetual_identities` `no input → table` GPU: none — Returns the **exact claims** each system must satisfy, together with measured values (``table``). · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_ifs_attractor` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Attractor of an iterated function system (Barnsley fern) — just iterating 4 formulas endlessly. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_langtons_ant` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Langton's ant — with just 2 rules, after 10,000 steps it keeps building a "highway". · examples: `gallery_illusion_invariants`
- `perpetual_plasma` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Diamond-square algorithm (the "plasma" of the 1980s) — keep subdividing and it gets infinitely fine. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_reaction_diffusion` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Gray–Scott reaction-diffusion — patterns emerge, split and keep multiplying. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_ten_print` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — ``10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1)); : GOTO 10`` — a maze that grows forever. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_truchet` `no input → rgb` GPU: none — Truchet tiles — just randomizing the orientation of 2 quarter-circle arcs yields an unbroken network of curves. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`

#### generative / pl (3)
- `pl_diffusion_psf` `no input → image2d` GPU: none — Return the carrier-diffusion PSF (the 2-D Green function K0(r/L)/2πL², summing to 1) as an image. · examples: `poc_si_wafer_pl_defect_visibility`
- `pl_groove_visibility` `no input → table` GPU: none — Closed-form contrast and CNR of a shadow groove and a sink groove from groove width, diffusion length and noise (table). · examples: `poc_si_wafer_pl_defect_visibility`
- `pl_image_simulate` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Build a PL image from an excitation map and a recombination map (exact steady-state diffusion solve + optical PSF + noise). · examples: `poc_si_wafer_pl_defect_visibility`

#### generative / sem (9)
- `sem_cd_measure` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Measure a line width from a line profile (``pairs``: x and signal) with the two CD-SEM methods. · examples: `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_charging_series` `image2d → video` GPU: none — Advance insulator charging frame by frame of the scan and return the image over time (``video``, (T, H, W)). · examples: `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_electron_mc` `no input → table` GPU: none — Monte Carlo of electrons fired into a flat specimen: backscatter coefficient η, secondary-electron yield δ and interaction volume. · examples: `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`, `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_image` `image2d → image2d` GPU: none — SEM image from a height field and a material map, firing electrons into every pixel (direct Monte Carlo). · examples: `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`, `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_line_profile` `no input → table` GPU: none — Monte Carlo line profile of a beam scanned across one line with a trapezoidal cross-section (CD-SEM). · examples: `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_render` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Render a SEM image from a height field: secondary-electron edge effect (sec θ) + Gaussian beam PSF + Poisson shot noise. · examples: `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`
- `sem_se_escape_fraction` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Fraction F(V) of secondary electrons that can leave a positively charged surface (potential V > 0). · examples: `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_se_universal_curve` `no input → signal` GPU: none — Universal secondary-electron yield curve δ/δmax = 1.28 (E/Emax)^−0.67 [1 − exp(−1.614 (E/Emax)^1.67)]. · examples: `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`
- `sem_yield_curve` `no input → table` GPU: none — Sweep the accelerating voltage, compute η(E) and δ(E) by Monte Carlo, and compare the shape of δ with the universal curve. · examples: `poc_virtual_sem_kv_cd_bse`

#### generative / stream (3)
- `perpetual_render` `table → rgb` GPU: none — Renders the state as a picture (``rgb``). It may be drawn at any step. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_state` `no input → table` GPU: none — Creates a **state** that can be run forever (``table``). When to stop is up to the caller. · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`
- `perpetual_step` `table → table` GPU: none — Advances the state by ``steps`` (returns the same dict — large arrays are not copied). · examples: `poc_illusions_and_perpetual_drawing`

### imgmetrics (42 ops / 8 categories)

#### imgmetrics / colordiff (3)
- `delta_e_2000` `lab × lab → image2d` GPU: none — CIEDE2000 colour difference (CIE 142-2001). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `delta_e_76` `lab × lab → image2d` GPU: none — CIE76 colour difference — the Euclidean distance in Lab space. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `delta_e_map` `rgbimage × rgbimage → image2d` GPU: none — Per-pixel colour-difference map between two **sRGB images**. · examples: `color_transport`, `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_colormap_readability`, `poc_pigment_unmixing`, `poc_white_balance`

#### imgmetrics / colorspace (4)
- `lab_to_rgb` `lab → rgbimage` GPU: yes (allow-list) — CIE L\*a\*b\* → sRGB ``[0, 1]``. **Out-of-gamut colours are clipped**, so a round trip through ``rgb_to_lab`` only matches inside the gamut (pinned by a test). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `rgb_to_lab` `rgbimage → lab` GPU: none — sRGB → CIE L\*a\*b\* (D65). The step before measuring ΔE. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_colormap_readability`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_solder_fillet_aoi`
- `rgb_to_xyz` `rgbimage → rgb` GPU: none — sRGB (``(..., 3)``) → CIE XYZ. The transfer function is removed first, then the matrix is applied. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `xyz_to_lab` `rgb → lab` GPU: yes (allow-list) — CIE XYZ → CIE 1976 L\*a\*b\*. The default white point is D65 2°. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`

#### imgmetrics / compression (2)
- `compressed_size` `image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Size in bytes of the array after lossless compression. The raw material for ``ncd``. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `ncd` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Normalised compression distance (Li, Chen, Li, Ma & Vitányi, IEEE TIT 50(12), 2004). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`

#### imgmetrics / fidelity (6)
- `ms_ssim` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Multi-scale SSIM (Wang, Simoncelli & Bovik, Asilomar Conf. 2003). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `mse` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Mean squared error. A raw quantity that does not depend on ``data_range``. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `psnr` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Returns the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR, in dB) of two images. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_camera_shake_deblur`, `poc_dehazing`, `poc_focus_stacking`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`, `poc_pixel_shift`, `poc_real_deblur_honesty`, `poc_superresolution_limits`
- `rmse` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Root mean squared error (in the same units as the pixel values). · examples: `ct_scan_modes`, `grasp_pose`, `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_ct_fidelity`, `poc_datacenter_thermal_field`, `poc_polarization_specular`, `poc_real_tless_6dof`, `poc_real_walnut_cbct`, `poc_structure_4d_deterioration`
- `ssim` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Structural similarity (Wang, Bovik, Sheikh & Simoncelli, IEEE TIP 13(4), 2004). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_camera_shake_deblur`, `poc_ct_fidelity`, `poc_dehazing`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`, `poc_real_walnut_cbct`, `poc_superresolution_limits`
- `ssim_map` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: none — The SSIM **map** (before averaging) — to see *where* the two differ, as a picture. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`

#### imgmetrics / information (5)
- `image_entropy` `image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Shannon entropy of one image [bit]. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`, `poc_dehazing`
- `joint_entropy` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Joint entropy H(A, B) [bit]. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `joint_histogram` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Joint histogram of two images (the normalised joint probability). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `mutual_information` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Mutual information I(A; B) [bit] = H(A) + H(B) - H(A, B). · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `normalized_mutual_information` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Normalised mutual information 2*I(A;B) / (H(A) + H(B)). 1.0 for identical images. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`

#### imgmetrics / iqa (11)
- `luma_limited_u8` `any → any` GPU: yes (allow-list) — RGB (H, W, 3) uint8 → uint8 (H, W) of Y′ = round(16 + (65.481 R + 128.553 G + 24.966 B) / 255). · examples: `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `rank_data` `any → any` GPU: none — Average ranks (starting at 1). Ties get the average of their ranks (same definition as 'average' in scipy.stats.rankdata). · examples: `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `rank_kendall_b` `any × any → scalar` GPU: none — Kendall's τ_b (with tie correction) = (C − D) / sqrt((n0 − n1)(n0 − n2)). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `rank_spearman` `any × any → scalar` GPU: none — Spearman's rank correlation ρ = Pearson correlation between average ranks (the form that is correct even with ties; the classical formula 1 − 6Σd²/(n(n²−1)) agrees only when there are no ties). 1 for monotonically increasing, −1 for reversed. If either is constant, ``nan`` (rank variance is 0; correlation is undefined). ±inf contributes only its order (a perfect-match PSNR = inf is not dropped). **Raises** ``ValueError``: length mismatch, fewer than 2, nan. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_by_distortion` `any × table → table` GPU: none — Rank correlation between the metric and the MOS for each distortion type (24). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_compare` `any × any × any → table` GPU: none — Compares your own values with the authors' values (same pairs, same order): per-row differences and rank correlations with the MOS. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_evaluate` `any × any → table` GPU: none — Applies your own metric ``fn(ref, dist) -> float`` to the TID2013 pairs and returns its rank correlation with the MOS. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_index` `any → table` GPU: none — Reads ``mos_with_names.txt`` and returns the ledger of pairs. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_metric_values` `any × any → any` GPU: none — Returns the authors' computed values ``metrics_values/<metric>.txt`` (case-insensitive, 3000 lines, no names) as a (3000,) float. The line order is the same as ``names`` of :func:`tid2013_index`. ``metric`` is a key of :func:`tid2013_published` (psnr / psnrc / ssim / mssim …). **Raises** ``ValueError``: file missing, line count ≠ 3000, non-numeric. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_published` `no input → table` GPU: none — The published rank-correlation table {metric: (SROCC, KROCC)} (14 metrics). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`
- `tid2013_root` `no input → any` GPU: none — Where the distribution is extracted. If ``root`` is absent, the environment variable ``FULLSEYE_TID2013_DATA``. If neither exists, or ``mos_with_names.txt`` is missing, ``None`` (the caller skips — the data is not in the repo). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`, `poc_iqa_tid2013`

#### imgmetrics / perceptual (7)
- `fsim` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — FSIM (feature-similarity full-reference image quality metric; luminance only, 1 = identical, **higher is better**). It agrees with TID2013's FSIM.txt to 4 digits when given **a Y′ limited grayscale image** (``iqatid.tid2013_evaluate(root, fsim, luma="limited_u8")``, 3,000 pairs, max |diff| 5.0e-5). Details: :func:`fsim_pair`. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `fsim_pair` `rgbimage × rgbimage → table` GPU: none — FSIM and FSIMc in one call (phase congruency is computed only 1 time per image — evaluators and PoCs call this one). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `fsimc` `rgbimage × rgbimage → scalar` GPU: none — FSIMc (feature-similarity full-reference image quality metric; including chroma I / Q, 1 = identical, **higher is better**). It agrees with TID2013's FSIMc.txt to 4 digits when given a color image (RGB → YIQ full range) (``iqatid.tid2013_evaluate(root, fsimc, luma="rgb")``, 3,000 pairs, max |diff| 5.0e-5). For an (H, W) input, the same value as FSIM. Details: :func:`fsim_pair`. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `gmsd` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — GMSD = standard deviation of the GMS map (N−1, the original implementation's ``std2``, Eq. 5 of the paper). 0 = identical, larger means more degraded (**lower is better** — the rank correlation with MOS is negative, and published tables report |ρ|: TID2013 overall |SROCC| 0.8038, secondary source 0.8044). Input (H, W) or (H, W, 3) (3-ch uses Y). ``iqatid.tid2013_evaluate(root, gmsd, luma="rgb")``. **Raises** ``ValueError``: same as :func:`gmsd_map`, or the map is 1 pixel (variance undefined). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `gmsd_map` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — GMS map (2 m_r m_d + c)/(m_r² + m_d² + c) ∈ (0, 1] (Eq. 3 of the paper). m = magnitude of the Prewitt ([1 0 −1]×3 /3) gradient; preprocessing is a 2×2 mean + decimation by 2 (:func:`_average_downsample`, the original implementation's 'same' convention). Input (H, W) or (H, W, 3) (3-ch uses Y = 0.299R+0.587G+0.114B, the authors' convention). **Raises** ``ValueError``: shapes differ, c ≤ 0, down_step < 1. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `phase_congruency_pc` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Phase congruency PC(x) = Σ_o E_o(x) / Σ_o Σ_s A_{s,o}(x) ∈ [0, 1] (Kovesi 1999; convention of Eq. 4 of the FSIM paper: log-Gabor with 4 scales × 4 orientations). · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`
- `vifp` `image2d × image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Pixel-domain version of VIF (the scalar GSM of Sheikh & Bovik 2006 §V, following the convention of the public vifp_mscale). 1 = identical, **higher is better**. · examples: `poc_iqa_fsim_gmsd_vif`

#### imgmetrics / report (4)
- `compare_images` `image2d × image2d → metrics` GPU: none — Measure several metrics at once and **return what was measured and how, alongside the numbers**. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `data_range_of` `image2d → scalar` GPU: none — Decide the span the pixel values may take. **It does not guess.** · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `measure_with` `metrics × image2d × image2d → metrics` GPU: none — Measure another pair **under exactly the same conditions as the previous measurement**. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`
- `metrics_table` `metrics → table` GPU: none — Turn a report into a ``(name, value)`` table — the rows describing the conditions are **always listed with it**. · examples: `image_quality_metrics`

### oned (49 ops / 4 categories)

1-D ops for profiles / signals. Their sources are 2-D measure1d, 3-D probe and audio / sensor series (dsp) — the extracted (x, y) sequence is processed with funct1d/dsp and measured.

#### oned / function (23)
- `abs_funct_1d` (halcon: `abs_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Absolute value of the y-values (HALCON ``abs_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `compose_funct_1d` (halcon: `compose_funct_1d`) `signal × signal → signal` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Composition ``y1(y2)``: the values of *y2* used as positions into *y1* (HALCON ``compose_funct_1d``). · examples: `gallery_oned_audio_funct`
- `create_funct_1d_array` (halcon: `create_funct_1d_array`) `signal → signal` GPU: none — A 1-D function from equidistant samples (HALCON ``create_funct_1d_array``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `create_funct_1d_pairs` (halcon: `create_funct_1d_pairs`) `signal × signal → signal` GPU: yes (allow-list) — A 1-D function from arbitrary ``(x, y)`` pairs, resampled to an equidistant grid (HALCON ``create_funct_1d_pairs``). · examples: `poc_veiling_glare`
- `derivate_funct_1d` (halcon: `derivate_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — First derivative by central differences (HALCON ``derivate_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_tree_ring_dendro`, `poc_veiling_glare`, `signal_funct1d`
- `distance_funct_1d` (halcon: `distance_funct_1d`) `signal × signal → measurement` GPU: none — Distance between two functions on the same grid (HALCON ``distance_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `funct_1d_to_pairs` (halcon: `funct_1d_to_pairs`) `signal → pairs` GPU: none — The function as explicit ``(x, y)`` pairs (HALCON ``funct_1d_to_pairs``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `get_pair_funct_1d` (halcon: `get_pair_funct_1d`) `signal → pairs` GPU: none — The ``(x, y)`` pair at *index* (HALCON ``get_pair_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `get_y_value_funct_1d` (halcon: `get_y_value_funct_1d`) `signal → measurement` GPU: none — The y-value at (fractional) position *x* (HALCON ``get_y_value_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_veiling_glare`, `signal_funct1d`
- `integrate_funct_1d` (halcon: `integrate_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Cumulative integral by the trapezoidal rule (HALCON ``integrate_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_cold_chain_excursion`, `poc_search_sweep_width`, `signal_funct1d`
- `invert_funct_1d` (halcon: `invert_funct_1d`) `signal → pairs` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Swap the roles of x and y: ``x = f^-1(y)`` (HALCON ``invert_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_veiling_glare`
- `local_min_max_funct_1d` (halcon: `local_min_max_funct_1d`) `signal → table` GPU: none — Indices of strict local maxima / minima (HALCON ``local_min_max_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_web_roll_periodicity`, `signal_funct1d`
- `match_funct_1d_trans` (halcon: `match_funct_1d_trans`) `signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Best integer translation between two functions by correlation (HALCON ``match_funct_1d_trans``, translation only). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `negate_funct_1d` (halcon: `negate_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: none — Sign-flipped y-values (HALCON ``negate_funct_1d``). · examples: `gallery_oned_audio_funct`, `gallery_spectrum_signal_bridge`
- `num_points_funct_1d` (halcon: `num_points_funct_1d`) `signal → measurement` GPU: none — Number of samples (HALCON ``num_points_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `sample_funct_1d` (halcon: `sample_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: none — Every *step*-th sample (HALCON ``sample_funct_1d``). · examples: `poc_cold_chain_excursion`, `signal_funct1d`
- `scale_y_funct_1d` (halcon: `scale_y_funct_1d`) `signal → signal` GPU: none — Linear map of the y-values, ``mult * y + add`` (HALCON ``scale_y_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `smooth_funct_1d_gauss` (halcon: `smooth_funct_1d_gauss`) `signal → signal` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Gaussian smoothing of a 1-D function (HALCON ``smooth_funct_1d_gauss``). · examples: `poc_fiber_orientation`, `poc_tree_ring_dendro`, `poc_web_roll_periodicity`, `signal_funct1d`
- `smooth_funct_1d_mean` (halcon: `smooth_funct_1d_mean`) `signal → signal` GPU: none — Iterated moving-average smoothing (HALCON ``smooth_funct_1d_mean``). · examples: `poc_weld_bead_profile`, `signal_funct1d`
- `transform_funct_1d` (halcon: `transform_funct_1d`) `signal → pairs` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Independent affine transform of x and y (HALCON ``transform_funct_1d``). · examples: `gallery_oned_audio_funct`
- `x_range_funct_1d` (halcon: `x_range_funct_1d`) `signal → pairs` GPU: none — The x-domain ``(0.0, n - 1.0)`` (HALCON ``x_range_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `y_range_funct_1d` (halcon: `y_range_funct_1d`) `signal → pairs` GPU: none — The value range ``(min(y), max(y))`` (HALCON ``y_range_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`
- `zero_crossings_funct_1d` (halcon: `zero_crossings_funct_1d`) `signal → indices` GPU: none — Indices where the function changes sign (HALCON ``zero_crossings_funct_1d``). · examples: `signal_funct1d`

- `chirp_mass_from_track` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Chirp mass and coalescence time from a gravitational-wave frequency track (t, f) by least squares. · examples: `poc_gw_detector_pseudo_simulation`

#### oned / signal (16)
- `bandpass` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Butterworth band-pass between *low* and *high* Hz. Both edges must be inside ``(0, rate/2)``; same length contract as :func:`lowpass`. · examples: `poc_gw_detector_pseudo_simulation`, `poc_leak_localization`

- `highpass` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Butterworth high-pass. Same Nyquist / length contract as :func:`lowpass`. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`, `optics_four_f_processor`, `signal_filter`
- `local_std` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Rolling standard deviation with a stated error bound. · examples: `gallery2d_texture_freq`
- `lowpass` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Butterworth low-pass (scipy, zero-phase filtfilt). *cutoff* must be inside ``(0, rate/2)``; an out-of-Nyquist cutoff raises instead of passing the signal through. - `peak_subbin` `signal × indices → signal` GPU: none — Peak position **between** samples — the vertex of a fit through 3 points. · examples: `poc_multibeam_bathymetry`, `poc_print_registration`, `poc_web_roll_periodicity`

- `quantize` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Scalar quantiser with the error model stated, plus optional dither. · examples: `poc_cold_chain_excursion`
- `resample` `signal → signal` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Resample a signal to *new_rate* (Fourier method). · examples: `poc_driving_school`
- `rms` `signal → measurement` GPU: none — RMS level. Scalar for the whole signal, or a framewise array when *frame* is given (a vibration/energy envelope over time). · examples: `lens_design_demo`, `lightfield_depth`, `poc_battery_electrode_breathing`, `poc_bilateral_asymmetry`, `poc_bump_coplanarity`, `poc_cad_scan_deviation`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_camera_calibration`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`, `poc_fabric_defect`, `poc_focus_stacking`, `poc_fourier_ptychography`, `poc_lens_solves_afocal`, `poc_panorama_drift`, `poc_print_registration`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`, `poc_screw_thread_metrology`, `poc_shape_from_polarization`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`, `poc_strain_history`, `poc_surface_roughness`, `poc_symmetry_restoration`, `poc_table_tennis_bounce`, `poc_tacscalib_sphere_lut`, `poc_tacsim_elastic_membrane`, `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`, `poc_thermal_radiometry`, `poc_weld_bead_profile`, `profile_shape_inspection`
- `signal_features` `signal → table` GPU: none — A compact acoustic/vibration feature vector for anomaly detection: ``rms``, ``peak``, ``crest_factor``, ``zcr``, ``spectral_centroid`` (Hz), ``peak_freq`` (Hz), ``bandwidth`` (Hz). - `spectrogram` `signal → image2d` GPU: none — STFT magnitude spectrogram -> ``(freqs, times, S)`` with ``S`` shape ``(n_freqs, n_frames)``. Hann-windowed; *hop* defaults to ``win//2``. · examples: `acoustic_condition_monitoring`, `poc_emva1288_sensor`, `poc_gw_detector_pseudo_simulation`

#### colortransport / blend (1)

- `wasserstein_1d` `signal × signal → scalar` GPU: none — The 1-D p-Wasserstein distance. **Exact.** · examples: `color_transport`, `poc_physarum_transport`
