### astrostack (14 ops / 6 categories)

#### astrostack / align (2)
- `align_frames` `images → images` GPU: none — Register a series of frames onto one reference. · examples: `astro_stacking`
- `frame_align` `image2d × image2d → matrix` GPU: none — Estimate the 2-D transform ``frame`` → ``reference`` from star correspondences. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`, `poc_print_registration`

#### astrostack / cosmic (2)
- `cosmic_ray_reject` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Cosmic-ray removal from a single frame (Laplacian sharpness). · examples: `astro_stacking`
- `cosmic_ray_reject_stack` `images → images` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Cosmic-ray removal by comparing frames — **it never hits the same place twice**. · examples: `astro_stacking`

#### astrostack / photometry (3)
- `aperture_photometry` `image2d × keypoints → table` GPU: none — Photometry with a circular aperture and an annular background (classical CCD photometry). · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_real_file_formats`, `poc_real_sky_photometry`
- `psf_fit` `image2d × keypoints → table` GPU: none — Fit a PSF to a star image and get its centre and FWHM. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_star_astrometry`
- `star_detect` `image2d → keypoints` GPU: none — Detect stars and return their ``(row, col)`` centroids. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`, `poc_real_file_formats`, `poc_search_sweep_width`, `poc_star_astrometry`

#### astrostack / quality (3)
- `frame_quality` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Score one frame — sharpness, FWHM, background, roundness, and a point for selection. · examples: `astro_stacking`
- `lucky_select` `images → indices` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Keep only the top ``keep_fraction`` by quality score — the lucky-imaging cut. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`
- `noise_sigma` `image2d → measurement` GPU: none — Robustly estimate the background noise sigma (one real number that the stars cannot spoil). · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_colocalization_crosstalk`, `poc_search_sweep_width`, `poc_star_astrometry`, `poc_thermal_radiometry`

#### astrostack / stack (2)
- `drizzle_resample` `images → image2d` GPU: none — Drizzle — build a finer grid from several sub-pixel-shifted frames (area-conserving). · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`, `poc_pixel_shift`, `poc_superresolution_limits`
- `sigma_clip_stack` `images → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Combine a series of frames (mean / median / κ-σ clipping), with the accept/reject mask. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`

#### astrostack / synth (2)
- `synth_frame_series` `no input → images` GPU: none — Re-shoot the same star field ``n_frames`` times, **each with its own noise and its own dither**. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`
- `synth_starfield` `no input → image2d` GPU: none — Synthesise one known star field — **the source of ground truth for this family**. · examples: `astro_stacking`, `poc_astro_photometry`

### videostream (16 ops / 8 categories)

#### videostream / analysis (1)
- `scene_cut_detection` `video → table` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Shot-boundary chi-square histogram distance over a clip → ``{"distance", "cut", "n"}`` (``table``). · examples: `video_streaming`

#### videostream / background (2)
- `running_gaussian_background` `video → video` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Adaptive single-Gaussian background (the running mean) per frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `running_gaussian_foreground` `video → video` GPU: none — Adaptive single-Gaussian foreground masks per frame → 0/1 ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`

#### videostream / denoise (1)
- `temporal_bilateral` `video → video` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Causal temporal bilateral denoise per frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `find_ops_by_meaning`, `video_streaming`

#### videostream / flow (1)
- `optical_flow_magnitude_stream` `video → video` GPU: none — Per-frame dense flow speed against the previous frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`

#### videostream / motion (3)
- `motion_energy_image` `video → video` GPU: none — Bobick–Davis Motion Energy Image per frame → 0/1 ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `motion_history_image` `video → video` GPU: none — Bobick–Davis Motion History Image per frame → ``(T, H, W)`` in ``[0, 1]`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `three_frame_difference` `video → video` GPU: none — Collins three-frame-difference motion mask per frame → 0/1 ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `poc_periodic_video_boundary`, `video_streaming`

#### videostream / recursive (4)
- `exponential_background` `video → video` GPU: none — Recursive background ``bg ← (1−α)·bg + α·frame`` per frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `exponential_foreground` `video → video` GPU: none — Foreground masks ``|frame − exponential background| > threshold`` → 0/1 ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `frame_difference_causal` `video → video` GPU: none — ``|frame t − frame t−1|`` with a zero first frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `running_mean_std` `video → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Welford per-pixel mean / population std over the clip → ``{"mean", "std", "n"}`` (``table``). · examples: `video_streaming`

#### videostream / restore (1)
- `deflicker` `video → video` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Luminance deflicker per frame → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`

#### videostream / window (3)
- `background_subtraction_window` `video → video` GPU: none — Causal window-median background → per-frame 0/1 foreground masks ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`
- `moving_average_window` `video → video` GPU: none — Causal per-pixel mean over the last *window* frames → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `poc_periodic_video_boundary`, `poc_strain_history`, `video_streaming`
- `temporal_median_window` `video → video` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Causal per-pixel median over the last *window* frames → ``(T, H, W)`` (``video``). · examples: `video_streaming`

### profile (12 ops / 4 categories)

#### profile / compare (2)
- `profile_align` `pairs × pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Aligns a measured contour to the design contour. Returns ``(aligned, info)``. · examples: `profile_frame_tour`
- `profile_deviation` `pairs × pairs → table` GPU: none — The **signed deviation along the normal** from the design shape. Returns a dict. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`

#### profile / frame (3)
- `profile_chord_frame` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Finds the chord (the 2 points farthest apart). Returns a dict. · examples: `profile_frame_tour`, `profile_shape_inspection`
- `profile_normalise` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Normalises by rotation and translation so that the chord length is 1, the leading edge is at the origin and the chord points along +x. · examples: `profile_frame_tour`
- `profile_resample` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Resamples the contour at equal spacing. ``kind`` is ``"arclength"`` only (for now). · examples: `profile_frame_tour`

#### profile / measure (5)
- `profile_camber` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Camber line (the midline between the upper and lower surfaces). Returns ``(x, yc)`` as an ``(n, 2)`` array. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`
- `profile_leading_edge_radius` `pairs → measurement` GPU: none — Leading-edge radius (as a fraction of the chord). Fits a circle to the points near the leading edge. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`
- `profile_sides` `pairs → table` GPU: none — Extracts the upper and lower surfaces as functions of the chordwise coordinate. Returns a dict. · examples: `profile_frame_tour`
- `profile_thickness` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Thickness distribution ``t(x)``. Returns ``(x, t)`` as an ``(n, 2)`` array. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`
- `profile_trailing_edge_gap` `pairs → measurement` GPU: none — Trailing-edge gap (as a fraction of the chord). The distance between the trailing-edge ends of the upper and lower surfaces. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`

#### profile / synth (2)
- `profile_perturb` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Returns a contour with defects of known magnitude inserted. :data:`PERTURB_KINDS`. · examples: `profile_shape_inspection`
- `profile_synth_naca4` `no input → pairs` GPU: none — Generates a NACA 4-digit airfoil in closed form. Returns an ``(N, 2)`` outline traced in a single continuous stroke. · examples: `profile_frame_tour`, `profile_shape_inspection`

### shapestat (16 ops / 5 categories)

#### shapestat / deviation (1)
- `signed_surface_distance` `points × points → signal` GPU: none — **Signed** distance from the query points to the surface. → ``(N,)``. · examples: `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `shapestat_landmark_tour`

#### shapestat / model (6)
- `shape_explained_variance` `shapemodel → signal` GPU: none — Explained-variance ratio of each principal component (sums to 1). → ``(k,)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_mahalanobis` `shapemodel × points → measurement` GPU: none — How **abnormal** the shape is as seen from the model. → float. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_pca` `shapeset → shapemodel` GPU: none — Shape PCA (statistical shape model). → dict (``shapemodel``). · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_project` `shapemodel × points → signal` GPU: none — Maps a shape into model coordinates (principal-component scores). → ``(k,)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_reconstruct` `shapemodel × signal → points` GPU: none — Reconstructs a shape from scores. → ``(N, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_synthesize` `shapemodel → points` GPU: none — Generates 1 **plausible new shape** from the model. → ``(N, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`

#### shapestat / procrustes (5)
- `generalized_procrustes` `shapeset → shapeset` GPU: none — Generalised Procrustes analysis (GPA). Brings all individuals into a common frame. → ``(K, N, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `procrustes_align` `points × points → points` GPU: none — Points of *source* superimposed onto *target*. → ``(N, 3)`` (applies :func:`procrustes_fit`). · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `procrustes_distance` `points × points → measurement` GPU: none — Procrustes distance = per-point RMS after superimposition. → float. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `procrustes_fit` `points × points → matrix` GPU: none — Similarity transform that superimposes *source* onto *target*. → ``(4, 4)`` homogeneous matrix. · examples: `poc_change_detection_misreg`, `poc_die_tilt_tsv_overlay`, `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_mean` `shapeset → points` GPU: none — Mean shape after alignment by GPA. → ``(N, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`

#### shapestat / symmetry (2)
- `landmark_asymmetry` `points → signal` GPU: none — **Signed** asymmetry for each left/right pair. → ``(M,)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `mirror_plane_from_pairs` `points → matrix` GPU: none — Derives the median (midsagittal) plane from corresponding left/right landmarks. → ``(2, 3)`` (row 1 = point, row 2 = normal). · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`

#### shapestat / synth (2)
- `shape_perturb` `points → points` GPU: none — Applies 1 **known** deformation to a shape. → ``(N, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`
- `shape_synth_family` `no input → shapeset` GPU: none — Creates a family of shapes with known modes of deformation. → ``(n_shapes, n_points, 3)``. · examples: `shapestat_landmark_tour`

### measure1d (17 ops / 4 categories)

#### measure1d / apply (2)
- `align_metrology_model` (halcon: `align_metrology_model`) `metrologymodel → metrologymodel` GPU: none — Aligns all objects of the metrology model by translating them (align_metrology_model). · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `apply_metrology_model` (halcon: `apply_metrology_model`) `metrologymodel × image2d → table` GPU: none — Measures subpixel edges along the normals of each metrology object's reference shape, refits the shape and returns the result (apply_metrology_model). · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`

#### measure1d / caliper (6)
- `fuzzy_measure_pairing` (halcon: `fuzzy_measure_pairing`) `image2d × measurehandle → table` GPU: none — Selects the edge pair that best matches a fuzzy criterion (expected width pair_size) (fuzzy_measure_pairing). · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `gen_measure_arc` (halcon: `gen_measure_arc`) `no input → measurehandle` GPU: none — Defines a measurement arc (the profile is sampled at ≈1 px spacing in the circumferential direction) (gen_measure_arc). Number of samples n = round(|angle_extent|*radius)+1, ``spacing`` = arc length/(n-1). · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `gen_measure_rectangle2` (halcon: `gen_measure_rectangle2`) `no input → measurehandle` GPU: none — Defines a rotated measurement rectangle (the profile is sampled at 1 px spacing along the major axis in direction ``phi``) (gen_measure_rectangle2). Number of samples n = max(2, round(2*length1)+1); the start point lies -(n-1)/2 px from the center. ``length2`` is the averaging width across the profile [px]. · examples: `example_scratch_width`, `poc_barcode_1d`, `poc_battery_electrode_breathing`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_screw_thread_metrology`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`, `poc_tree_ring_dendro`, `poc_water_level`, `poc_weld_bead_profile`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `measure_pairs` (halcon: `measure_pairs`) `image2d × measurehandle → table` GPU: none — Extracts pairs of rising/falling edges (the width of a structure) (measure_pairs). ``first``/``second`` = ``pos`` of each edge, ``width`` = width [px], ``first_point``/``second_point`` = (row, col). · examples: `example_scratch_width`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `measure_pos` (halcon: `measure_pos`) `image2d × measurehandle → table` GPU: none — Extracts edge positions (subpixel) and amplitudes along the measurement line (measure_pos). · examples: `poc_barcode_1d`, `poc_battery_electrode_breathing`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_screw_thread_metrology`, `poc_solar_limb_darkening`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`, `poc_tree_ring_dendro`, `poc_water_level`, `poc_weld_bead_profile`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `translate_measure` (halcon: `translate_measure`) `measurehandle → measurehandle` GPU: none — Translates a measurement object (translate_measure). · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`

#### measure1d / model (6)
- `add_metrology_object_circle_measure` (halcon: `add_metrology_object_circle_measure`) `metrologymodel → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a circle metrology object (add_metrology_object_circle_measure). · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`
- `add_metrology_object_ellipse_measure` (halcon: `add_metrology_object_ellipse_measure`) `metrologymodel → scalar` GPU: none — Adds an ellipse metrology object (add_metrology_object_ellipse_measure). ``phi`` = orientation of the ``ra`` axis (from the col axis, in radians). · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `add_metrology_object_generic` (halcon: `add_metrology_object_generic`) `metrologymodel → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a generic metrology object (add_metrology_object_generic). · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `add_metrology_object_line_measure` (halcon: `add_metrology_object_line_measure`) `metrologymodel → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a line metrology object (add_metrology_object_line_measure). Returns the index. · examples: `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure` (halcon: `add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure`) `metrologymodel → scalar` GPU: none — Adds a rectangle metrology object (add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure). ``phi`` = orientation of the ``l1`` side (from the col axis, in radians), ``l1``/``l2`` = half side lengths. · examples: `poc_dimensional_inspection`
- `create_metrology_model` (halcon: `create_metrology_model`) `no input → metrologymodel` GPU: none — Creates an empty metrology model (create_metrology_model). · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `poc_calipers_under_illusion`, `poc_dimensional_inspection`, `poc_telecentric_metrology`

#### measure1d / scale (3)
- `mm_per_px_from_reference` `measurement → measurement` GPU: none — Derives the pixel pitch in mm/px from a target of known size (scale bar, reference hole, gauge) — the calibration step. · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `example_scratch_width`
- `pixel_to_world` `measurement → measurement` GPU: none — Converts one length measured in pixels to real-world mm (``value_px * mm_per_px``). · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`
- `table_px_to_mm` `table → table` GPU: none — Adds mm columns to a measurement table (the return of ``measure_pairs`` / ``apply_metrology_model``). · examples: `example_inner_diameter_mm`, `example_scratch_width`

### roughness (9 ops / 3 categories)

#### roughness / measure (3)
- `profile_params` `signal → table` GPU: none — Profile roughness parameters Ra/Rq/Rz/Rt/Rp/Rv/Rsk/Rku (ISO 4287). · examples: `poc_food_cutting_measure`, `poc_surface_roughness`
- `surface_params` `depth → table` GPU: none — Areal roughness parameters Sa/Sq/Sp/Sv/Sz/Ssk/Sku/Sdq/Sdr (ISO 25178-2). · examples: `poc_polish_wipe_measure`, `poc_surface_roughness`
- `surface_psd` `depth → pairs` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Power spectral density of the height field. Returns ``(q, C)``. **The conventions are made explicit through the arguments.** · examples: `poc_surface_roughness`

#### roughness / prepare (5)
- `robust_gaussian_profile` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Robust Gaussian regression filter (profile): a mean line and roughness that outliers and scratches cannot drag. · examples: `example_robust_profile_filter`, `poc_robust_profile_filter`
- `robust_gaussian_surface` `depth → depth` GPU: none — Robust Gaussian regression filter (surface): waviness and roughness of a surface that scratches and spikes cannot drag. · examples: `poc_robust_profile_filter`
- `robust_spline_profile` `signal → signal` GPU: none — Robust spline filter (profile): a mean line and roughness that outliers cannot drag. · examples: `poc_robust_profile_filter`
- `surface_filter` `depth → depth` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Separates a height field into roughness and waviness (Gaussian filter of ISO 16610-21). · examples: `poc_robust_profile_filter`, `poc_surface_roughness`
- `surface_form_remove` `depth → depth` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Removes a plane / quadric surface directly on the grid. Returns ``(residual, coeffs)``. · examples: `poc_polish_wipe_measure`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_surface_roughness`

#### roughness / synth (1)
- `surface_synth_psd` `no input → depth` GPU: none — Synthesizes a height field from a specified PSD. Returns ``(z, sq_analytic)``. · examples: `poc_polish_wipe_measure`, `poc_surface_roughness`

### shape2d (17 ops / 2 categories)

#### shape2d / descriptor (11)
- `contour_epicycle_chain` `matrix → pairs` GPU: none — Returns the **chain of rotating pendulums** at phase ``t`` (``pairs``). · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `contour_fourier_complex` `pairs → matrix` GPU: none — Turns a closed contour into the coefficients of a complex Fourier series — ``z(t) = Σ c_k exp(2πi k t)``. · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `contour_fourier_truncation_energy` `matrix → table` GPU: none — The **predicted** error for each truncation order (``table``) — Parseval's exact formula. · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `descriptor_distance` `efdmodel × efdmodel → measurement` GPU: none — Distance between 2 shapes (smaller means more similar). Invariant to rotation/translation/starting point/(optionally) scale. · examples: `contour_fourier`, `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `elliptic_fourier` `pairs → efdmodel` GPU: none — Computes the elliptic Fourier coefficients of a closed contour using the Kuhl–Giardina closed form. · examples: `contour_fourier`, `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `fit_circle_xld` `contour → table` GPU: none — Fit a circle to each XLD contour and return its centre row, column and radius (``table``). · examples: `fit_circle_xld_bore`
- `fourier_smooth` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Smooths a contour by band-limiting it with a complex FFT. · examples: `contour_fourier`
- `from_xld` `table → pairs` GPU: none — Extracts the i-th contour from an XLD contour dict (``{"shape", "cs":[Nx2,...]}``). · examples: `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `invariants` `efdmodel → pairs` GPU: none — Shape descriptor invariant to rotation, translation, starting point and (optionally) scale ((N,2)). · examples: `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `normalize` `efdmodel → matrix` GPU: none — Converts EFD coefficients into the coefficients of the "canonical pose" (aligned with respect to the 1st harmonic). · examples: `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_exoplanet_transit`
- `reconstruct` `efdmodel → pairs` GPU: none — Reconstructs a contour from EFD coefficients ((M,2)). · examples: `contour_fourier`

#### shape2d / morph (6)
- `add_frame_corners` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Adds the four corners of the image (+ the edge midpoints) to the point set as fixed points. · examples: `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `blend` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: none — Cross-dissolve (1-alpha)·a + alpha·b (a, b have the same shape and lie in [0,1]). · examples: `image_morph`, `poc_live4d`
- `morph` `image2d × image2d × pairs × pairs → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Morphs 2 images A and B via corresponding points and produces the intermediate image at ratio alpha. · examples: `image_morph`, `poc_vanishing_detail_and_morphing_area`
- `morph_sequence` `image2d × image2d × pairs × pairs → images` GPU: none — Morph sequence with alpha swept 0→1 in n steps (frames that change smoothly from A to B). · examples: `image_morph`
- `warp_piecewise_affine` `image2d × pairs × pairs → image2d` GPU: none — Piecewise affine warp that moves the content at src_pts of img to dst_pts. · examples: `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`
- `warp_tps_image` `image2d × pairs × pairs → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Smooth warp that moves src_pts of img to dst_pts using a thin-plate spline. · examples: `shape2d_morph_descriptor_tour`

### piv (29 ops / 7 categories)

#### piv / assess (4)
- `piv_error_stats` `flow2d × flow2d → table` GPU: none — Breakdown of the difference from the ground truth. Returns **bias and scatter separately**. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`, `poc_strain_history`
- `piv_peak_locking` `flow2d → table` GPU: none — Strength of peak locking: how far the distribution of the fractional parts deviates from uniform. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `poc_battery_electrode_breathing`
- `piv_sample_at_windows` `flow2d → flow2d` GPU: none — Drops a per-pixel field ``(2, H, W)`` onto the grid of window centers (nearest neighbor). · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`, `poc_strain_history`
- `piv_time_statistics` `images → table` GPU: none — Image sequence → time average, RMS of the fluctuations and Reynolds stresses. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`

#### piv / estimate (4)
- `piv_cross_correlate` `image2d × image2d → flow2d` GPU: none — Computes the displacement field by per-window cross-correlation. Returns ``(flow, info)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_beam_modal_video`, `poc_change_detection_misreg`, `poc_dic_strain`, `poc_print_registration`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`, `poc_strain_history`, `poc_superresolution_limits`, `poc_tacsim_marker_shear`
- `piv_deform_pass` `image2d × image2d × flow2d → flow2d` GPU: none — 1 pass with window deformation. Correlates only after **first warping the images themselves** with the predicted displacement. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_ensemble_correlate` `images → flow2d` GPU: none — Searches for the peak **after summing** the correlation maps (ensemble correlation). · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`
- `piv_multipass` `image2d × image2d → flow2d` GPU: none — Multi-pass PIV that steps down from coarse windows to fine windows. Returns ``(flow, info)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_strain_history`

#### piv / field (8)
- `piv_divergence` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Divergence ``d(dy)/dy + d(dx)/dx``. **0 if the flow is incompressible** — usable as an independent cross-check. · examples: `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `piv_flow_magnitude` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — ``sqrt(dy^2 + dx^2)``. A **one-way** conversion that discards the direction. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `poc_sheet_deformation_ffd`, `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`
- `piv_q_criterion` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Q criterion ``-tr(J^2)/2``. It is positive where **rotation exceeds strain**. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_strain_rate` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Magnitude of the strain rate ``sqrt(2 e_ij e_ij)``. It is 0 for a rigid-body rotation. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_swirling_strength` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Swirling strength λ_ci — the magnitude of the imaginary part of the complex eigenvalues of the velocity-gradient tensor. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_to_velocity` `flow2d → flow2d` GPU: none — Pixels/frame → m/s. **Both are required arguments** (no default values are provided). · examples: `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`
- `piv_velocity_gradient` `flow2d → table` GPU: none — Returns the components of the velocity-gradient tensor together with the quantities derived from it. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_vorticity` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Vorticity ``d(dx)/dy - d(dy)/dx``. **Counter-clockwise is positive** (defined in image coordinates). · examples: `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_tactile_dipole_torque`, `poc_what_a_picture_cannot_check`

#### piv / solid (3)
- `correlation_quality` `image2d × image2d × flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — A ZNCC map that returns, point by point, **how well** a given displacement field matches. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `speckle_quality` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Returns 4 numbers indicating whether a captured speckle pattern is suitable for DIC. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `strain_from_displacement` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Computes the strain field from a displacement field. Returns ``(exx, eyy, exy)``. · examples: `poc_dic_strain`

#### piv / synth (3)
- `piv_synth_pair` `no input → image2d` GPU: none — Creates an image pair with a known displacement field. Returns ``(image_a, image_b, truth)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_strain_history`
- `piv_synth_particles` `no input → image2d` GPU: none — Creates 1 image seeded with tracer particles. Returns ``(image, positions)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_synth_sequence` `no input → images` GPU: none — Image sequence in which the same particles are moved repeatedly. Returns ``(frames, truth)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`

#### piv / validate (2)
- `piv_outlier_mask` `flow2d → mask` GPU: none — Finds outlier vectors with the normalised median test (Westerweel & Scarano 2005). · examples: `perf_hankel_plan_and_piv_stream`, `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_change_detection_misreg`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`
- `piv_replace_outliers` `flow2d × mask → flow2d` GPU: none — Fills outliers from their neighbourhood. With ``method="nan"`` they are **not filled but marked as missing**. · examples: `piv_flow_from_particles`, `poc_river_surface_velocity`

#### piv / visualise (5)
- `piv_flow_to_rgbimage` `flow2d → rgb` GPU: none — Standard flow visualisation with hue = direction and brightness = speed. Returns ``(h, w, 3)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_line_integral_convolution` `flow2d → image2d` GPU: none — Line integral convolution (LIC) — an image whose pattern is white noise blurred along the flow. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_quiver` `flow2d → rgb` GPU: none — Arrow plot (MATLAB's ``quiver``). Returns ``(h*upsample, w*upsample, 3)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_streamline_image` `flow2d → rgb` GPU: none — Streamline plot (MATLAB's ``streamslice``). Returns ``(h*upsample, w*upsample, 3)``. · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`
- `piv_streamlines` `flow2d → table` GPU: none — Traces streamlines with RK4 (corresponds to MATLAB's ``stream2`` / ``streamslice``). · examples: `piv_field_analysis_tour`

### blob (11 ops / 5 categories)

#### blob / connect (1)
- `blob_label` `mask → labels2d` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Splits a binary region into connected components and returns an ``int32`` label image (background 0, objects 1..n). · examples: `blob_split_tour`, `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_bump_coplanarity`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`, `poc_em_split_merge_score`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_gravitational_lens_invariants`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_machine_condition_fusion`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_particle_sizing`, `poc_particle_tracking`, `poc_peg_insertion_tactile`, `poc_pipe_wall_loss`, `poc_powder_grinding_ae`, `poc_print_warpage_risk`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_real_coin_metrology`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_rotation_invariance_audit`, `poc_sea_ice_concentration`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`, `poc_solder_fillet_aoi`, `poc_timelapse_growth`, `poc_traffic_counting`, `poc_vessel_network`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`

#### blob / extract (3)
- `blob_boundaries` `labels2d → mask` GPU: none — Object outlines (1 pixel wide, bool). **The borders between adjacent objects are kept as well**. · examples: `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`
- `blob_overlay` `image2d × labels2d → rgb` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Overlays the objects in different colors on the original image and returns a float RGB of shape ``(H, W, 3)``. · examples: `poc_bump_coplanarity`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_particle_sizing`, `poc_powder_grinding_ae`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `blob_region` `labels2d → mask` GPU: none — Extracts 1 object as a binary region (bool). ``index`` is **1-based**. · examples: `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_particle_sizing`

#### blob / measure (1)
- `blob_features` `labels2d → table` GPU: none — Returns the shape features of each object as **1 array per key**. · examples: `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_bump_coplanarity`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`, `poc_fresco_craquelure`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_metal_grain_size`, `poc_nuclei_ploidy`, `poc_particle_sizing`, `poc_particle_tracking`, `poc_peg_insertion_tactile`, `poc_print_warpage_risk`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_real_coin_metrology`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_rotation_invariance_audit`, `poc_sea_ice_concentration`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`, `poc_solder_fillet_aoi`, `poc_traffic_counting`, `poc_vessel_network`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`

#### blob / select (2)
- `blob_select` `labels2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Keeps only the objects whose feature value lies in ``[vmin, vmax]`` (**the numbers are reassigned starting from 1**). · examples: `poc_particle_sizing`, `poc_pipe_wall_loss`, `poc_pv_thermal_survey`, `poc_solar_el_inspection`, `poc_weld_radiograph_porosity`
- `blob_select_largest` `labels2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Keeps only ``count`` objects in order of decreasing area (**the numbers are reassigned in descending order of area**). · examples: `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_gear_tooth_metrology`, `poc_solder_fillet_aoi`, `poc_wound_area_tracking`

#### blob / split (4)
- `blob_count_interval` `mask → table` GPU: none — Counts overlapping objects. **When the count cannot be determined, returns an interval instead of a number** (fail-closed). · examples: `poc_dense_bubble_count`
- `blob_distance` `mask → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Distance from each foreground pixel **to the nearest background**. The unit is multiples of ``spacing``. · examples: `blob_split_tour`, `poc_bone_trabecular_thickness`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`, `poc_real_sem_metal_layer`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `blob_seeds` `image2d → labels2d` GPU: none — h-maxima seeds. **``h`` is an absolute value in the same units as ``distance``**. · examples: `blob_split_tour`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`
- `blob_split` `labels2d × labels2d × image2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Grows regions from the seeds **in order from the highest points** and splits merged clumps (watershed). · examples: `blob_split_tour`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`

### dem (25 ops / 5 categories)

#### dem / geodesy (12)
- `dem_cell_size_webmercator` `no input → measurement` GPU: none — Ground resolution of a Web Mercator tile [m/px]. **It varies with latitude**. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`
- `dem_datum_shift_3param` `no input → points` GPU: none — Switching the geodetic datum — a geocentric 3-parameter translation (``points``). · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_earth_curvature_drop` `no input → measurement` GPU: none — **Earth-curvature drop** [m] for line-of-sight computations. ``(1 - k) d^2 / (2 R)``. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_ecef_to_geodetic` `points → points` GPU: none — ECEF → geodetic coordinates. Returns ``(..., 3)`` holding ``(latitude[deg], longitude[deg], height[m])``. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`, `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_enu_from_geodetic` `no input → points` GPU: none — Geodetic coordinates → **local ENU** (east, north, up) around a reference point [m] (``points``). · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_geocentric_grid` `depth → pointmap` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Converts each DEM cell into **coordinates as seen from the Earth's center**. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`
- `dem_geodetic_from_enu` `points → points` GPU: none — Local ENU → geodetic coordinates (the inverse of :func:`dem_enu_from_geodetic`). ``points``. · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_geodetic_slope` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Slope of a DEM on a **latitude-longitude grid** (equal angular spacing). The cell dimensions vary with latitude. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`
- `dem_geodetic_to_ecef` `no input → points` GPU: none — Geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude, ellipsoidal height) → **Earth-centered Cartesian coordinates ECEF** [m]. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`, `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_geoid_height` `depth → signal` GPU: none — **Bilinearly interpolates** a geoid-height grid at a latitude/longitude and returns ``N`` [m] (``signal``). · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_height_frame_convert` `signal × signal → signal` GPU: none — Moves the height **reference**: ellipsoidal height ``h`` ↔ orthometric height ``H`` (``H = h - N``). ``signal``. · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_height_frame_residual` `signal × signal × signal → table` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Residual ``h - H - N`` — a detector that **does not let a mix-up of heights stay silent** (``table``). · examples: `poc_geodetic_benchmarks_real`

#### dem / hydrology (4)
- `dem_fill_sinks` `depth → depth` GPU: none — DEM with its depressions filled. The priority-flood of Barnes, Lehman & Mulla (2014). · examples: `poc_dem_terrain`
- `dem_flow_accumulation` `depth → image2d` GPU: none — Number of contributing cells: the count of upstream cells flowing into each cell (the cell itself counts as 1). · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`, `poc_dem_terrain`
- `dem_flow_direction` `depth → labels` GPU: yes (allow-list) — D8 flow direction. O'Callaghan & Mark (1984). · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_stream_network` `depth → image2d` GPU: none — Binary mask that treats cells whose flow accumulation exceeds a threshold as stream channels. · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`

#### dem / shading (1)
- `dem_hillshade` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Hillshade [0,1]. ``azimuth_deg`` is the azimuth of the light source (north 0 degrees, increasing towards east). · examples: `poc_dem_terrain`, `poc_lidar_terrain_change`, `poc_stockpile_volume`

#### dem / surface (5)
- `dem_aspect` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Slope aspect [degrees]. **North is 0 degrees, increasing towards east**. Flat cells get :data:`ASPECT_FLAT`. · examples: `poc_dem_terrain`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`
- `dem_curvature` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Curvature [1/m]. ``kind`` is ``"profile"`` (profile) / ``"planform"`` (plan) / ``"total"``. · examples: `poc_dem_terrain`
- `dem_roughness` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Terrain ruggedness index TRI — the root mean square of the elevation differences to the 8 neighbors [m]. · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`
- `dem_slope` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Slope angle. ``units`` is ``"degrees"`` / ``"radians"`` / ``"percent"``. · examples: `dem_geodesy_tour`, `poc_crop_phenotyping`, `poc_dem_terrain`, `poc_geodetic_height_frames`, `poc_lidar_terrain_change`, `poc_multibeam_bathymetry`, `poc_stockpile_volume`
- `dem_tpi` `depth → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Topographic position index TPI — the difference between the cell itself and the mean of its 8 neighbors [m]. Positive means ridge, negative means valley. · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`

#### dem / visibility (3)
- `dem_horizon_angle` `depth → image2d` GPU: none — Horizon elevation angle in a given azimuth [degrees]. 0 is horizontal; 90 means the sky straight above is blocked. · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`
- `dem_sky_view_factor` `depth → image2d` GPU: none — Sky view factor [0,1]: how much of the sky is visible. · examples: `poc_dem_terrain`
- `dem_viewshed` `depth → image2d` GPU: none — Visible area from 1 point (1 = visible). Decides whether the line of sight is blocked by the terrain. · examples: `dem_terrain_analysis_tour`, `poc_stockpile_volume`

### conngraph (28 ops / 7 categories)

#### conngraph / activity (3)
- `graph_activation_latency` `matrix → labels` GPU: inside a chain only (allow-list) — Sequence (n,) of the step (0-based) at which each node first "lit up", as integers. Nodes that never lit up get −1. · examples: `poc_malecns_activity_wave`
- `graph_activity_spread` `matrix × points × labels → table` GPU: none — Time-series table of how far the activity spread: columns step / mean_distance / active_fraction / source_fraction. · examples: `poc_malecns_activity_wave`, `poc_microns_brain_wave`
- `points_activity_video` `points × matrix → rgbvideo` GPU: none — A color video (F, H, W, 3) that puts the activity onto the point cloud and rotates it, values in [0, 1]. F = T × substeps, H = size, W = size × aspect. · examples: `poc_connectome_motor_bottleneck`, `poc_em_branch_territory`, `poc_em_second_opinion`, `poc_eye_to_brain`, `poc_malecns_activity_wave`, `poc_microns_brain_wave`

#### conngraph / circuit (1)
- `graph_conductance_states` `conn_graph × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Time series of membrane potentials ``(T, n)`` obtained by **running the wiring ``W`` directly as a circuit** (``matrix``, no learning). · examples: `poc_fly_optomotor_steering`

#### conngraph / construct (3)
- `graph_binarize` `conn_graph → conn_graph` GPU: none — A conn_graph in which edges with |W| > thresh become 1.0 and all others 0.0 (the diagonal follows the same rule). · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_degree_preserving_shuffle` `conn_graph → conn_graph` GPU: none — Degree-preserving shuffle (null model): rewires edges while keeping each node's in-degree, out-degree and the multiset of weights. · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`, `poc_malecns_activity_wave`, `poc_microns_brain_wave`
- `graph_from_synapses` `synapse_table → conn_graph` GPU: none — Turns a synapse table (m, 3) = (pre_id, post_id, count) into an n×n weighted directed adjacency matrix. · examples: `poc_fly_optomotor_steering`, `poc_microns_brain_wave`, `type_connectivity_tour`

#### conngraph / dimension (4)
- `graph_block_shuffle` `conn_graph × labels → conn_graph` GPU: none — A control ``conn_graph`` in which **the senders are shuffled** within each block of layers (labels): it keeps the multiset of weights each receiver gets and the total amount of wiring between layers, and destroys only the "from whom". · examples: `poc_connectome_motor_bottleneck`
- `graph_layer_propagate` `conn_graph × labels × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Passes the layer-0 state ``U`` (N, n_0) **forward, one stage at a time**, through the blocks ``W[layer a → layer a+1]``, giving the states of all layers ``(N, n)`` (``matrix``; columns in node order, and the layer-0 columns are ``U`` itself). · examples: `poc_connectome_motor_bottleneck`
- `states_layer_dimension` `matrix × labels → table` GPU: none — Table of the effective dimension per layer: columns layer / n / participation_ratio / ratio (= PR / n). · examples: `poc_connectome_motor_bottleneck`
- `states_participation_ratio` `matrix → measurement` GPU: none — **Effective dimension** of the state sequence ``X`` (N, n) = participation ratio ``PR = (Σλ)² / Σλ²`` (λ are the eigenvalues of the covariance, Gao et al. 2017). It is n if all columns are independent with equal variance, and 1 if the states lie along 1 direction. · examples: `poc_connectome_motor_bottleneck`

#### conngraph / reservoir (5)
- `reservoir_encode` `conn_graph × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Batch reservoir encoding of static inputs (for classification): the final state (N, n) after running each row of X for steps iterations from the zero state. · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`
- `reservoir_from_graph` `conn_graph → conn_graph` GPU: none — A conn_graph with W scaled by a constant so that its spectral radius becomes rho (preprocessing for an echo state network). A radius of 0 is rejected. · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`, `poc_malecns_activity_wave`
- `reservoir_states` `conn_graph × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Reservoir state sequence: x_{t+1} = (1−leak) x_t + leak · f(Wᵀ x_t + W_in u_t). Returns (T − washout, n). · examples: `poc_malecns_activity_wave`, `poc_microns_brain_wave`
- `ridge_predict` `matrix × matrix → matrix` GPU: none — Prediction with the readout weights (T, k) = [X, 1] · Wout. Wout is the (d+1, k) from ridge_readout. · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`
- `ridge_readout` `matrix × matrix → matrix` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Ridge-regression readout weights (d+1, k) = (X̃ᵀX̃ + αI)⁻¹ X̃ᵀY, with X̃ = [X, 1] (a bias column is appended). · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`

#### conngraph / stats (9)
- `graph_betweenness` `conn_graph → signal` GPU: none — Betweenness centrality (Brandes 2001, binary directed, unnormalised). An array of length n, one value per node. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_clustering_coefficient` `conn_graph → measurement` GPU: none — Mean local clustering coefficient (binary graph with directions collapsed, Watts–Strogatz). Nodes with degree < 2 count as 0. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_components` `conn_graph → labels` GPU: none — Labels of the weakly connected components (0-based, numbered by first appearance in node order). An int64 of length n. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`, `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `graph_degree_table` `conn_graph → table` GPU: none — Per-node table of in_degree / out_degree (binary) and in_strength / out_strength (sum of weights). · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`, `poc_theorems_as_pictures`
- `graph_laplacian_spectrum` `conn_graph → signal` GPU: none — Eigenvalues of the Laplacian L = D − A of the binary graph with directions collapsed (ascending, length n). · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`, `poc_bga_ball_type_roundtrip`
- `graph_modularity` `conn_graph × labels → measurement` GPU: none — Directed, weighted modularity Q (Leicht–Newman 2008). · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_motif_count` `conn_graph → measurement` GPU: none — Counts of 3-node motifs (binary directed, diagonal excluded): reciprocal / ffl / cycle3. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_rich_club` `conn_graph → measurement` GPU: none — Rich-club coefficient φ(k): the directed density of the subgraph spanned by nodes with total degree (in+out, binary) > k. · examples: `poc_worm_core_persists`
- `graph_spectral_radius` `conn_graph → measurement` GPU: none — Largest absolute eigenvalue of the weighted adjacency matrix W (spectral radius). · examples: `poc_larval_connectome_reservoir`

#### conngraph / view (3)
- `graph_adjacency_image` `conn_graph → image2d` GPU: none — Turns the adjacency matrix into an image (n, n) in [0, 1]. order = none / degree (descending total degree) / component (component order). · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_edges_as_lines` `conn_graph × points → table` GPU: none — Turns the edges into a table of line segments (the exit for overlaying them on a point cloud in Studio): columns pre / post / x0 y0 z0 / x1 y1 z1 / weight. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`
- `graph_layout_spectral` `conn_graph → points` GPU: none — Spectral layout: a point cloud (n, 3) whose coordinates are the Fiedler vectors (eigenvectors 2..dim+1) of the Laplacian with directions collapsed, each axis in [0, 1]. · examples: `gallery_conngraph_closed_forms`

### emproof (14 ops / 6 categories)

#### emproof / evaluate (1)
- `holdout_threshold` `signal × signal × signal × signal → table` GPU: none — Chooses the threshold **on the training side, and measures the evaluation on the other side** (a higher score means "more suspicious"). · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`

#### emproof / inject (3)
- `seg_inject_merge` `labels2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Plants **merges** for evaluation: picks ``n`` pairs of adjacent large labels and rewrites the id of one to the other. · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`, `poc_em_split_merge_score`
- `seg_inject_split` `labels2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Plants **splits** for evaluation: picks ``n`` large labels, cuts each in two at the row (``axis="row"``) or column (``"col"``) of the pixel median, and gives one side a new id (existing maximum + 1, +2, …). · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`, `poc_em_split_merge_score`
- `seg_label_changes` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Returns the difference between two label images **as pairs of merges and splits** (before vs. after calibration, or checking planted errors against the answer). · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`, `poc_em_split_merge_score`

#### emproof / response (1)
- `seg_membrane_response` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Response [0, ∞) to the **dark lines** (cell membranes) of an EM section. From the eigenvalues λ1 ≥ λ2 of the Gaussian-smoothed Hessian, ``max(λ1 − |λ2|, 0)`` (the closed form of Steger's line detection, scale-normalized by σ²). · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`, `poc_em_split_merge_score`

#### emproof / score (3)
- `seg_contingency` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — The contingency table of truth ``a`` against candidate ``b`` (sparse). · examples: `gallery_mesh_seg_sun_gains`
- `seg_rand` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Rand index, adjusted Rand index and the adapted Rand error (CREMI / SNEMI). · examples: `poc_em_split_merge_score`
- `seg_variation_of_information` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Variation of information between truth ``a`` and candidate ``b``, in bits. · examples: `poc_em_split_merge_score`, `poc_em_wiring_errors`, `poc_skeleton_run_length_vs_voi`

#### emproof / suspect (2)
- `seg_boundary_membrane_gap` `labels2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — **Suspected split**: fraction of the boundary pixels between two adjacent labels whose membrane response is below ``tau``. One row per adjacent pair. · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`
- `seg_membrane_chord_score` `labels2d × image2d → table` GPU: none — **Suspected merge**: length of the membrane "chord" crossing the interior of a label / diameter of the label. One row per label (connected component). · examples: `poc_em_second_opinion`

#### emproof / wiring (4)
- `seg_synapse_nri` `labels2d × labels2d × table → table` GPU: none — Neural reconstruction integrity (Reilly et al. 2018) of candidate ``b`` against truth ``a``. · examples: `poc_em_wiring_errors`
- `seg_synapse_partners` `labels2d × table → table` GPU: none — Read the wiring diagram a segmentation implies: which object each synapse connects. · examples: `poc_em_wiring_errors`
- `seg_wiring_exposure` `labels2d × table → table` GPU: none — How much wiring each object stakes on staying one piece — from synapse end counts alone. · examples: `poc_em_wiring_errors`
- `seg_wiring_variation` `labels2d × labels2d × table → table` GPU: none — How a candidate segmentation ``b`` corrupts the wiring diagram of truth ``a``, in bits. · examples: `poc_em_wiring_errors`

#### videocube / cube (2)
- `video_cube_cut` `video → image2d` GPU: none — One cross-section of the cube (``image2d``). ``"xt"`` = slit scan of row ``position`` (T, W), ``"yt"`` = (T, H) of a column, ``"xy"`` = the frame at time ``position`` (H, W). ``position`` is a fraction in [0, 1] (what fraction along the rows, columns or time). · examples: `poc_video_cube`
- `video_spacetime_cube` `video → voxel` GPU: none — Turns a video (T, H, W) into a space × time cube ``(T, H, W)`` float [0, 1] (``voxel``). · examples: `poc_video_cube`

#### videocube / export (1)
- `video_write_gif` `rgbvideo → text` GPU: none — Writes a frame sequence to an animated GIF (``text`` = the path written). A reusable exit point. · examples: `poc_video_cube`

#### videocube / render (2)
- `video_cube_orbit` `video → rgbvideo` GPU: none — Color video rotating the cube ``(n_frames, size, size, 3)`` float [0, 1] (``rgbvideo``). · examples: `poc_video_cube`
- `vol_render_transfer` `voxel → rgb` GPU: none — Renders the cube from an arbitrary viewpoint by **front-to-back α compositing** ``(size, size, 3)`` float [0, 1] (``rgb``). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`, `poc_video_cube`

#### videocube / summary (1)

### live4d (14 ops / 5 categories)

#### live4d / flow (4)
- `vol_flow_3d` `voxel × voxel → flow_dense` GPU: none — Dense displacement field ``(3, Z, Y, X)`` between two volumes (``flow_dense``, components dz, dy, dx [voxel]). · examples: `poc_live4d`

- `volseq_speed` `volseq → volseq` GPU: none — Returns the **speed** ``|d|`` [voxel/frame] between adjacent frames of a volume time series as ``(T − 1, Z, Y, X)`` (``volseq``). · examples: `gallery_live4d_volseq_truth`

#### live4d / render (3)

- `focus_sweep_surface_video` `volseq → rgbvideo` GPU: none — Builds a **shaded height-field video** ``(T, Y, X, 3)`` from a time series of focus sweeps (each frame a z focus stack) (``rgbvideo``). · examples: `poc_live4d`
- `volseq_render_orbit` `volseq → rgbvideo` GPU: none — Renders a volume time series **while advancing time and rotating the viewpoint** ``(n_frames, size, size, 3)`` (``rgbvideo``). · examples: `poc_live4d`

#### live4d / series (2)

- `volseq_mip_video` `volseq → video` GPU: none — Collapses a volume time series into a video ``(T, H, W)`` by maximum intensity projection along axis ``axis`` (1 = z, 2 = y, 3 = x) (``video``). · examples: `gallery_live4d_volseq_truth`

#### live4d / synth (2)
- `volseq_synth_beating` `no input → volseq` GPU: none — Volume time series ``(T, Z, Y, X)`` of a shell pulsating according to a known radius law (``volseq``, values in [0, 1] + noise). · examples: `poc_live4d`
- `volseq_synth_dividing` `no input → volseq` GPU: none — Volume time series ``(T, Z, Y, X)`` of a blob splitting in two at a known speed (``volseq``). · examples: `poc_live4d`

- `volseq_interpolate_flow` `volseq → volseq` GPU: none — Interpolates a volume time series ``(T, Z, Y, X)`` along the 3-D flow into ``(T + (T − 1)(factor − 1), Z, Y, X)`` (``volseq``). · examples: `poc_live4d`
