### printpath (23 ops / 6 categories)

#### printpath / format (2)
- `read_3mf` `text → mesh` GPU: none — Reads 3MF (``3D/3dmodel.model`` inside the zip, 3MF Core Specification) into a triangle mesh ``mesh`` = (V, F). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `write_3mf` `text × mesh → text` GPU: none — Writes a triangle mesh to 3MF (minimal configuration: ``[Content_Types].xml`` / ``_rels/.rels`` / ``3D/3dmodel.model``, unit mm). Returns the path (``text``). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`

#### printpath / gcode (5)
- `gcode_extrusion_volume` `table → measurement` GPU: none — Volume of extruded filament [mm³] = Σe × π (d / 2)² (``measurement``). The weight is density × volume (PLA ≈ 1.24 g/cm³). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `gcode_layer_image` `table → image2d` GPU: none — Draws the path of one layer as a **raster with line width** ``image2d`` (material 1, background 0, travel 0.5 when drawn, y pointing down = rows). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `gcode_read` `text → table` GPU: none — Reads G-code (RepRap / Marlin family) into a **table of line segments** ``table``: columns ``x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1`` (mm), ``e`` (filament length extruded on that segment in mm, 0 for a travel-only move), ``f`` (feed rate mm/min), ``layer`` (layer number). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `gcode_time_estimate` `table → measurement` GPU: none — Lower bound on the run time [s] = Σ(segment length / feed rate) (ignoring acceleration and jerk, ``measurement``). Segments with feed rate 0 are not counted. · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`, `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `gcode_write` `table × text → text` GPU: none — Writes a table of line segments to G-code (G21 / G90 / M82, G1 with absolute coordinates and absolute E). Returns the path written (``text``). · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`

#### printpath / inspect (1)
- `print_layer_defect_map` `image2d × image2d → image2d` GPU: none — **Signed defect map** ``image2d`` comparing an observed layer image with the expected layer image (``gcode_layer_image``): +1 = missing where material should be (gaps, clogs), −1 = present where nothing should be (stringing, overflow, spaghetti), 0 = match. · examples: `poc_print_layer_inspection`

#### printpath / npr (6)
- `engrave_lines` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Copperplate engraving — parallel lines whose **width** carries the tone. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `halftone_moire_period` `no input → table` GPU: none — The beat between two halftone screens — period and direction, in closed form. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`, `poc_moire_screen`, `poc_print_registration`
- `halftone_screen` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — A classic rotated halftone screen — dots whose area carries the tone. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`, `poc_pixel_shift`, `poc_print_registration`
- `hatch_field` `image2d → image2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Cross-hatching that **follows the picture** — direction from the structure tensor. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `mosaic_tiles_render` `image2d × pairs → image2d` GPU: none — Paint each Voronoi cell with the **mean** of the pixels it owns. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`
- `mosaic_tiles_sites` `image2d → pairs` GPU: none — Lloyd's iteration on an image — the tile centres of a mosaic. · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`

#### printpath / slice (3)
- `contours_to_gcode` `table → table` GPU: none — Turns contours (the table of ``mesh_slice_contours``) into a **table of paths that trace around them** (same columns as ``gcode_read``). · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`, `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `mesh_slice_contours` `mesh → table` GPU: none — **Table of contours** ``table`` obtained by cutting a triangle mesh with the plane ``z``: columns ``ring`` (ring number), ``x``, ``y`` (mm). · examples: `itokawa_gravity_tour`, `poc_print_layer_inspection`
- `mesh_slice_stack` `mesh → voxel` GPU: none — **Stack of layer masks** ``voxel`` (Z, Y, X) obtained by slicing a mesh in steps of ``layer_mm`` (0 / 1, Z from the bottom). · examples: `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_print_layer_inspection`

#### printpath / stroke (6)
- `mst_length` `pairs → measurement` GPU: none — Length of the minimum spanning tree (Prim). **A closed tour cannot be shorter than this** (lower bound). · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `stipple_energy` `image2d × pairs → measurement` GPU: none — Energy of weighted Lloyd ``Σ w(x) |x - c(x)|^2`` (for checking monotonic decrease). · examples: `poc_beats_fringes_and_screens`, `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `stipple_points_from_image` `image2d → pairs` GPU: none — Maps grey levels to **point density** (weighted Lloyd = centroidal Voronoi). → ``pairs`` · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `stroke_resample_closed` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Resamples a closed line at **equal arc length**. → ``pairs`` · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `stroke_tone_error` `image2d × pairs → table` GPU: none — How much the **tone** resulting from drawing the lines differs from the target. → ``table`` · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`
- `stroke_tour_closed` `pairs → pairs` GPU: none — Reorders the points into a **closed tour** that visits each point exactly 1 time and returns. → ``pairs`` · examples: `poc_one_stroke_epicycles`

### geocam (9 ops / 3 categories)

#### geocam / orientation (1)
- `camera_orientation_from_skyline` `signal × table → table` GPU: none — Determines (yaw, pitch, roll) from the skyline of a photo (row per column) and the skyline of the DEM → table. · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`

#### geocam / skyline (3)
- `dem_skyline` `depth → table` GPU: none — **Omnidirectional skyline** seen from 1 point of the DEM (horizon elevation per azimuth) → table. · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`
- `render_skyline_view` `table → image2d` GPU: none — From a skyline table and an orientation, draws the **sky mask** (H, W) seen by a camera pointing that way → image2d (0/1). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`
- `skyline_extract` `image2d → signal` GPU: none — Extracts from a photo, by dynamic programming, 1 line giving **the row of the sky–terrain boundary for each column** → signal (W,). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`

#### geocam / sun (5)
- `camera_orientation_from_sun` `keypoints × signal → table` GPU: none — Time-stamped pixel positions of the sun, ≥ 2 points → camera (yaw, pitch, roll) (SVD solution of Wahba's problem = Kabsch). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`
- `camera_orientation_from_sun_candidates` `keypoints × signal × signal → table` GPU: none — From several candidate "bright blobs" per frame (a mix of the sun, white cars, signs and text), selects with RANSAC **the 1 track that moves as the time predicts**, and determines (yaw, pitch, roll) and the focal length simultaneously → table. With a fixed camera only the sun moves at the sun's speed, so the sun is decided by its motion, not by its appearance (on Fintraffic weather cameras, an appearance gate gave 24/24 false detections, 2026-09-21). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading_real`
- `sun_bloom_fit` `image2d → table` GPU: none — The sun in real footage = a **bloom** that saturates the sensor (larger than the disk, its size changes with exposure, and it gets cut off by the image edge or by text bands). Fits a circle to the **edge** of the largest saturated blob and returns the center → table. The centroid is biased away from the cut side when the blob is cut off (measured 15 px), so the cut edges (pixels touching the image border or the ``ignore_top_rows`` band) are discarded and a circle is fitted to the remaining arc by algebraic least squares (Kåsa 1976). · examples: `gallery_mesh_seg_sun_gains`
- `sun_pixel_position` `image2d → keypoints` GPU: none — Centroid of the sun in the image (a disk that **saturates** the sensor) → keypoints (1, 2) = (u, v). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`
- `sun_position` `signal → table` GPU: none — Latitude, longitude, time (UNIX seconds, UTC) → azimuth and elevation of the sun [degrees] (NOAA solar position algorithm, the low-accuracy formula of Meeus 1998). · examples: `poc_public_camera_heading`, `poc_public_camera_heading_real`

### llmcore (10 ops / 4 categories)

#### llmcore / attend (4)
- `attention_grouped` `tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Attention that groups heads (GQA) → tokens. **Exactly matches MHA when n_kv_heads == n_heads, and MQA when == 1**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`
- `attention_linear` `tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Attention with the softmax removed → tokens. **(QKᵀ)V == Q(KᵀV) — the associative law itself**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`
- `attention_softmax` `tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Attention in one batch (reference implementation) → tokens. **The reference against which this family is checked**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`, `type_connectivity_tour`
- `attention_tiled` `tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Attention with tiles + online softmax (the core of FlashAttention) → tokens. **Not an approximation**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`

#### llmcore / decode (1)
- `kv_cache_decode` `tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Inference that advances by only 1 token (KV Cache) → tokens (1, dv). · examples: `poc_attention_identities`

#### llmcore / prepare (2)
- `rms_norm` `tokens → tokens` GPU: none — RMS normalization → tokens. **With the defaults (eps=0, no weight) the RMS of the output is exactly 1**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`
- `rope_rotate` `tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Rotary position encoding (RoPE) → tokens. **Being a rotation, it preserves the norm**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`

#### llmcore / score (3)
- `attention_apply` `attnmap × tokens → tokens` GPU: none — Mixes the values with the attention weights → tokens. **Since row sums are 1, the output is a convex combination of the inputs**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`
- `attention_scores` `tokens × tokens → attnmap` GPU: none — Raw attention scores QKᵀ/√d → attnmap (T, S). · examples: `poc_attention_identities`
- `attention_weights` `attnmap → attnmap` GPU: none — Row-wise softmax (with mask) → attnmap. **Row sums are 1 and mask positions are exactly 0**. · examples: `poc_attention_identities`

### segmentation (59 ops / 11 categories)

#### segmentation / classify (7)
- `class_2dim_sup` (halcon: `class_2dim_sup`) `image2d × image2d × mask → mask` GPU: none — Supervised classification in a 2-channel feature space: pixels inside the distribution of ref_region (class_2dim_sup). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`
- `class_2dim_unsup` (halcon: `class_2dim_unsup`) `image2d × image2d → labels2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Unsupervised k-means classification in a 2-channel feature space; returns a label image (class_2dim_unsup). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`
- `class_ndim_norm` (halcon: `class_ndim_norm`) `images × table → mask` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Classify N-D feature images with a learned normal-distribution class (Mahalanobis distance < thresh) (class_ndim_norm). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`
- `classify_image_class_lut` (halcon: `classify_image_class_lut`) `image2d × signal → labels2d` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Pixel classification through a gray-value LUT (threshold / label table) (classify_image_class_lut). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`
- `fisher_lda_fit` `matrix × signal → table` GPU: none — Fit a two-class Fisher linear discriminant (closed form, no iteration). · examples: `poc_weed_rice_ratio`
- `fisher_lda_score` `table × matrix → table` GPU: none — Score features with a discriminant fitted by ``fisher_lda_fit`` (score > 0 means class 1). · examples: `poc_weed_rice_ratio`
- `learn_ndim_norm` (halcon: `learn_ndim_norm`) `matrix → table` GPU: none — Learn a normal-distribution class (mean and covariance) from feature vectors (learn_ndim_norm). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`

#### segmentation / compare (1)
- `check_difference` (halcon: `check_difference`) `image2d × image2d → mask` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Pixels whose difference from the reference image exceeds tol, as a region (check_difference). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`

#### segmentation / contour (10)
- `chan_vese_energy` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Chan–Vese 2001 energy F = μ Length + ν Area(inside) + λ1 ∫_in |I − c1|² + λ2 ∫_out |I − c2|² (two-phase) (chan_vese_energy). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `chan_vese_evolve` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Minimises the two-phase Chan–Vese 2001 energy (by default alternating minimisation of the convex relaxation; the level-set gradient descent can also be chosen) (chan_vese_evolve). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `curvature_flow` `mask → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Level-set form of mean curvature flow (curve-shortening flow) φ_t = |∇φ| div(∇φ/|∇φ|) (inside where φ < 0; shrinks from the convex parts) (curvature_flow). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `drle_evolve` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Edge-based distance-regularized level set evolution DRLSE (Li–Xu–Gui–Fox 2010). No re-initialisation (drle_evolve). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `edge_stop_g` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Edge-stopping function g = 1 / (1 + |∇(G_σ * I)|² / k²) (the p = 2 form of Caselles–Kimmel–Sapiro 1997) (edge_stop_g). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `gvf_field` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Gradient vector flow (Xu–Prince 1998): the field (u, v) that smoothly diffuses the gradient of the edge map f away from the edges (gvf_field). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `level_set_reinit` `mask → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Turns φ (inside where φ < 0) into the signed distance function of the same zero level set (level_set_reinit). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `morph_chan_vese` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Morphological Chan–Vese (MorphACWE of Márquez-Neila–Baumela–Álvarez 2014). One iteration = data step + smoothing step (morph_chan_vese). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `morph_geodesic_ac` `image2d × mask → table` GPU: none — Morphological geodesic active contour (MorphGAC of Márquez-Neila et al. 2014). gimage = an image that is small on edges (the g of edge_stop_g) (morph_geodesic_ac). · examples: `poc_active_contours`
- `snake_evolve` `image2d × pairs → table` GPU: none — Semi-implicit update of the discrete snake (Kass–Witkin–Terzopoulos 1988): x_t = (A + γI)^(-1)(γ x_(t-1) − f_x) (eqs. (19)(20)) (snake_evolve). · examples: `poc_active_contours`

#### segmentation / graph (12)
- `alpha_expansion` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Multi-label α-expansion (Boykov–Veksler–Zabih 2001): E(f) = Σ (I_p − μ_(f_p))² + λ Σ w_pq V(f_p, f_q), where V is a metric (alpha_expansion). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `alpha_tree` `image2d → table` GPU: none — α-tree: builds the minimum spanning tree of the grid weighted by neighbour differences (Kruskal in scipy) and returns the partition for each α using only the tree edges of weight ≤ α (alpha_tree). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `area_opening_attr` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Attribute opening (Salembier et al. 1998): removes the component-tree nodes whose attribute < ``threshold`` and sets each pixel to the value of its nearest ancestor with attribute ≥ threshold (area_opening_attr). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `graph_cut_binary` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Binary graph cut (Boykov–Jolly 2001): minimises E = Σ_p D_p(x_p) + λ Σ w_pq [x_p ≠ x_q] exactly by max-flow / min-cut (graph_cut_binary). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `hierarchical_watershed` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Hierarchical watershed by dynamics: attaches the dynamics saliency to the edges of the minimum spanning forest of the relief ``image`` (low places are basins) and returns the components joined by edges with saliency ≤ ``threshold`` (if ``n_regions`` is given, the smallest threshold that yields that many regions is used) (hierarchical_watershed). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `max_tree` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Component tree (max-tree): builds the tree of connected components of the upper level sets {f ≥ h} with Union-Find (pixels processed in descending order of value) (max_tree). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `quasi_flat_zones` `image2d → table` GPU: none — α-quasi-flat zones (Soille 2008): the connected components joined only by neighbour edges with |f_p − f_q| ≤ α. Returns: ``labels`` (1..k), ``n_zones`` (quasi_flat_zones). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `quickshift` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Quick shift (Vedaldi–Soatto 2008): estimates the Parzen density P_i = Σ_j exp(−D_ij²/(2σ²)) on the features (y, x, ratio · I) (window 3σ, σ = ``kernel_size``), links each pixel to the nearest point of higher density (inside a window of radius ``search_radius``), and takes the components of the tree, after cutting branches longer than ``max_dist``, as the regions (quickshift). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `snic_superpixels` `image2d → table` GPU: none — SNIC (Algorithm 1 of Achanta–Süsstrunk 2017): non-iterative superpixels grown from grid seeds with a priority queue (snic_superpixels). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_weed_rice_ratio`
- `statistical_region_merging` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Statistical region merging SRM (Nock–Nielsen 2004): processes pairs of neighbouring pixels in ascending order of |I_p − I_q| and merges them when the predicate P(R, R') holds (statistical_region_merging). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `superpixel_quality` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Superpixel scoring: boundary recall (the recall of ``segeval.seg_boundary_f``, tolerance τ), the corrected undersegmentation error CUSE = (1/N) Σ_k |S_k − G_max(S_k)| (Neubert–Protzel 2012, eq. (2) of the SNIC paper), ASA = 1 − CUSE, the Neubert–Protzel undersegmentation error UE = (1/N) Σ_G Σ_(S∩G≠∅) min(|S∩G|, |S − G|), and the number of superpixels. Label 0 of the truth also counts as a region (the background must be covered too) (superpixel_quality). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `ultrametric_contour_map` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Ultrametric contour map (UCM) of the dynamics hierarchy: the value between neighbouring pixels p, q = the smallest threshold at which p and q fall into the same region (ultrametric_contour_map). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`

#### segmentation / grow (2)
- `expand_gray` (halcon: `expand_gray`) `image2d × mask → mask` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Grow a region from a seed by gray-value similarity (|delta| < tol) (expand_gray). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`
- `regiongrowing_n` (halcon: `regiongrowing_n`) `images → labels2d` GPU: none — Segment the whole image by multi-channel feature similarity; returns a label image (regiongrowing_n). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`

#### segmentation / plant (3)
- `cover_ratio_grade` `signal → table` GPU: none — Split a cover fraction (area share 0..1) into grades 0..len(edges) at **declared edges** ``edges``. · examples: `poc_weed_rice_ratio`
- `plant_color_index` `rgbimage → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Per-pixel plant colour indices from the three visible bands (ExG, ExR, ExGR, CIVE, NGRDI, VEG). · examples: `poc_leaf_disease_area`, `poc_weed_rice_ratio`
- `superpixel_color_texture_features` `rgbimage × labels2d → table` GPU: yes (allow-list) — Ten colour (plant indices, chromaticity) and texture (gradient, orientation coherence) features for every region of a label image. · examples: `poc_weed_rice_ratio`

#### segmentation / score (8)
- `seg_boundary_f` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Boundary F-measure at tolerance tau: precision = fraction of predicted boundary pixels within tau of a true boundary, recall the reverse (seg_boundary_f). · examples: `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`
- `seg_confusion_table` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Label-correspondence contingency table (rows = truth, columns = prediction) with max-overlap matching and a uniqueness flag (seg_confusion_table). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `seg_dice_jaccard` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Dice and Jaccard — once over the mask (union of non-background pixels), or per true label against its max-overlap partner (seg_dice_jaccard). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_am_thermal_to_ct`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`, `poc_sem_wafer_defect_edge_bias`
- `seg_hausdorff` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Hausdorff distance between the two boundary pixel sets, with a percentile variant such as HD95 (seg_hausdorff). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `seg_mean_surface_distance` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Average symmetric surface distance (ASSD): mean of the both-direction boundary distances, plus the RMS (seg_mean_surface_distance). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `seg_object_counts_match` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Object-count agreement: counts split / merged / missed / false / matched from the degrees of a 'mainly overlapping' bipartite graph (seg_object_counts_match). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `seg_score_card` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — All measures on one card: Dice/Jaccard, VI/split/merge, Rand/ARI, boundary F, Hausdorff/HD95/ASSD, over/under, split/merge/missed/false/matched and counts (seg_score_card). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `seg_under_over_segmentation` `labels2d × labels2d → table` GPU: none — Counts over- and under-segmentation as the multiplicity of the contingency-table majority vote (Levine & Nazif style) (seg_under_over_segmentation). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`

#### segmentation / threshold (4)
- `threshold_isodata` `image2d → table` GPU: none — ISODATA (Ridler–Calvard 1978): iterates t ← (μ_≤t + μ_>t)/2 **on the pixel values** until the partition stops changing (initial value = mean) (threshold_isodata). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `threshold_kapur` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Maximum-entropy threshold (Kapur–Sahoo–Wong 1985): the bin t that maximises H(t) = −Σ_(i ≤ t) (p_i/P1) ln(p_i/P1) − Σ_(i > t) (p_i/P2) ln(p_i/P2) (only bins where both sides have positive probability). Returns: ``threshold`` = upper edge of that bin, ``mask`` (bin index > t), ``bin``, ``entropy`` (H, nan for excluded bins) (threshold_kapur). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `threshold_kittler` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Minimum-error threshold (Kittler–Illingworth 1986): at each bin t, splits into a low side (bins ≤ t) and a high side and minimises J(t) = 1 + 2(P1 ln σ1 + P2 ln σ2) − 2(P1 ln P1 + P2 ln P2) (σ is the standard deviation of the bin centres on each side; bins where either side has σ = 0 are excluded). Returns: ``threshold`` = upper edge of that bin (the mask is decided by bin index > t = consistent at the edge values too), ``mask``, ``bin``, ``criterion`` (J, nan for excluded bins) (threshold_kittler). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`
- `threshold_triangle` `image2d → table` GPU: none — Triangle method (Zack–Rogers–Latt 1977): the threshold is the bin (b, h_b) between the peak (b_p, h_p) and the end bin of the longer tail (b_e, 0) whose signed perpendicular distance from the line joining them is largest (below the line is positive). Returns: ``threshold`` (centre of that bin), ``mask`` = image > threshold, ``bin``, ``distance`` (distance of each bin, nan outside the range). The zero height at the end point and the choice of tail follow the skimage / ImageJ convention (original paper to be confirmed) (threshold_triangle). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`

#### segmentation / watershed (1)
- `watersheds_marker` (halcon: `watersheds_marker`) `image2d × labels2d → labels2d` GPU: none — Marker-controlled watershed segmentation; markers is an int label image (0 = unassigned) (watersheds_marker). · examples: `halcon_segmentation_tour`, `poc_mixed_case_depalletizing`, `poc_sem_tem_same_particle`

#### segmentation / watershed3d (3)
- `distance_peaks` `voxel → labels` GPU: none — Returns an int marker array of the local maxima of the foreground distance transform, thinned out by ``min_distance`` NMS. · examples: `watershed3d_tour`
- `separate_touching` `voxel → labels` GPU: none — genuinely-new (B): an everyday wrapper that automatically separates touching objects in 1 call. · examples: `watershed3d_tour`
- `watershed_vol` `voxel → labels` GPU: none — Splits a 3D foreground into per-object labels with a watershed seeded from the distance transform (a thin composition of public ops). · examples: `watershed3d_tour`

#### segmentation / world (8)
- `lens_area` `no input → scalar` GPU: none — Closed-form overlap (lens) area of two equal-radius-r circles at centre distance d; 0 when d >= 2r (lens_area). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `voronoi_cells` `points → table` GPU: none — Voronoi partition of seeds inside a rectangle, returned as polygons with areas and internal edge lengths (brute-force half-planes, O(n^2)) (voronoi_cells). · examples: `gallery_seg_measures`
- `world_blobs_touching` `no input → table` GPU: none — World of overlapping discs (cells/grains): equal-radius circles placed in a chain, each overlapping only the previous one at centre distance 2r(1 - overlap) (world_blobs_touching). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_dense_bubble_count`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `world_gradient_illumination` `no input → table` GPU: none — World of dark objects over an illumination gradient plus noise (global thresholding breaks; local thresholding / flat-field cut it) (world_gradient_illumination). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `world_grains_voronoi` `no input → table` GPU: none — Voronoi grain world: n jittered seeds on a lattice; labels = index of the nearest seed (1..n) (world_grains_voronoi). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `world_parts_with_shadow` `no input → table` GPU: none — World of industrial parts (rotated rectangles with circular holes) with oblique-lighting shadows, facet shading and highlights (world_parts_with_shadow). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `world_texture_regions` `no input → table` GPU: none — World of 2-4 regions that share the same mean but differ only in variance and period (uncuttable by thresholding) (world_texture_regions). · examples: `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
- `world_thin_structures` `no input → table` GPU: none — World of 1-3 px lines (straight) and cracks (polylines); ground truth = centrelines and widths (world_thin_structures). · examples: `poc_active_contours`, `poc_graph_hierarchy_segmentation`, `poc_segmentation_gauntlet`
